Report 47: back-dating shipped 29 March 2020 after being 16% of 2019 reviews and is praised as available by 7 (all JP); the start-date-before-creation option exists but is hidden — 21 requests (3.57%), last July 2026, two reviewers could not find it after reading it existed; see [[C262]] for the 2024 video gate. Report 54: backfill only to yesterday — 15 (4.07%, 3.67); 'deleted on the second day because of the issue' (UA); if the schedule says Mon/Wed/Thu and you worked out Tuesday, you cannot record it at all. Report 55: log earlier days including before install — part of the praised tracking model. Report 56: back-dating existed but was hard to find — requested in June, 'a little hard' in July, 'super easy' in August. Report 57: past-date check-in went from top complaint (13, 2019–20: 'if you forget to track something you're just out of luck') to differentiator (4 praise at 5.000: 'ridiculously easy to add data for previous dates') — the one confirmed fix-to-differentiator in the corpus. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_BACKFILL 62 (rising to 0.8% in the latest era) — unfinished tasks roll to today and cannot be marked done for the day they were done ('если я выполнила задачу в 00:01 и хочу отметить её выполненной за предыдущую дату' — did it at 00:01 and want to mark it for the previous date); the report's experiment: mark done for a past date. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): any past day can be edited and a premium buyer was actively using the edit-previous-day buttons when the June build broke them; the counter-request is a lock, not removal. Report 65 (Rabit): marking the previous day was the capability premium took at launch (Nov 2020).

title: Weekly / monthly / yearly reports
statement: The #1 stated reason people pay; under-counted by keywords, dominant in the qualitative read. Report 25 (counter-evidence): paywalling all statistics — success %, graphs, per-habit calendar — averaged 1.40 and 'removes the motivation loop the category sells'; keep the basic progress view free, sell the deep report. Report 31: charts once unlocked are a named purchase trigger ('excited to see them … upgraded immediately'); stats 145 mentions, called weak by power users who want all-habit overviews, weekly totals and % of days. Report 33: statistics praised by 182 rated 4–5★ ('The statistics … is what sold me') and a named purchase trigger; 58 request an all-habit weekly grid, raw totals and multi-year history ('I want a GitHub type chart'); yearly and daily-ratio stats were removed in Habitify X. Report 34: statistics requests 14 (1.88%) — month %, all habits in one grid, counts rather than streaks; the free stats screen is 'a bit too simple'. Report 36: statistics / counts / year-in-review requested by 10, the newest rising request (4.6% of E5); one reviewer counts completions per month by hand. Report 41: statistics are Premium ('in free version… No statistics'), named as a purchase trigger ('love statistics now visible'), and 'better / deeper statistics' is still requested by 9. Report 42: statistics are the actual premium value proposition — three of six named purchase triggers ('Seeing the progress percentage of habits and which days they were done… because I found it in this app I bought the premium version'; 'The detailed stats in premium version are worth it') — while the same feature miscalculates for non-daily habits (a payer) and history is capped for free users. Report 43: percentages, grades, streaks and the green / red calendar praised by 55 (8.62%, mean 4.82) — 'Thank you for %'s and grades. This is how my brain works… I'm actually completing it so I can stay at a 90% grade' — free. Report 46: stats praised by 54 (mean 4.91 — 'I exercised 60% of the time, wrote 80% of the time'); richer statistics requested by 11 (4.55). Report 48: better reports / trends is the top open request (76, mean 4.07, still open Aug 2026) and comes almost entirely from people who like the app — the report's candidate next paid feature. Report 52: year statistics moved behind VIP in Dec 2025 and drew a one-month complaint window; the report's M3 test is a free basic year summary with a paid detailed report, a split one reviewer asked for verbatim. Report 53: extended statistics are a named purchase reason ('bought premium with extended statistics', ru) and the paid feature that broke. Report 54: long-range history requested by 28 (7.59%) and per-habit stats by 16; 48 unique (13.01%, 3.83) want 'proof that they have been consistent, over a period longer than a week, for a habit they can name' — the second-largest need after the paywall. Report 56: analytics / charts requested once in a fully free app. Report 57: weekly / monthly / yearly reports praised by 24 (the yearly report called unique); history of past reports requested by 11. Report 65 (Rabit): performance charts over time (REQ_GRAPH 2, 5.00) and a completion-% score beside the streak.

title: Week / month / year grid views
statement: 'Filling the squares' is the retention mechanic and emotional payoff. Report 23: statistics limited to the current and previous month (46 requests); the most-requested visualisation is a year heat-map / GitHub contribution grid, the single most-named competitor gap (Habitify). Report 25: statistics weak/unreadable (8) — rework the screen around 'why did I miss it'; a heat-map widget like HabitKit/Ripples requested. Report 26: statistics/history/calendar per habit was the top unmet need (40, 1.04% — 'this is a cosmetic habit tracker, it does not offer really understanding of progress'), something shipped ~late 2024, and the rate returned to 4.26% of substantive 2026 reviews because it is hard to find and stats cannot be reset. Report 27: daily, weekly and yearly views exist and a monthly view is the missing rung — requested five times over four years, the only feature request that repeatedly costs stars (2 of 6 3★); the year grid is the app's signature and its de-emphasis was noticed. Report 29: statistics (bar, pie, weekly analytics, completion rings) is the one advanced surface praised unprompted (10, mean 4.60) and asked to be extended — all-time records, a monthly/yearly grid, export — the safest place to add depth without violating simplicity. Report 30: per-habit and per-day completion percentages requested; history editing works only within the current month. Report 34: the per-habit year grid / 'year in pixels' / GitHub-style heatmap is the differentiator — 105 reviews (14.13%, zero 1★), 'the only habit tracker I could find with a whole year view'; 'Don't Break The Chain only makes sense if you can actually see your chain!' Report 46: a habit × day grid whose squares deepen in colour with each consecutive completion is the product — 228 reviews (10.47%, mean 4.86): 'Because I don't want the gradient to break, I'm motivated to check in every day'; 'Anybody that like seeing a git commit graph will love this app'; 'not ticks to check off but areas that fill with beautiful colours — so I don't feel stressed about not managing something' — praised at a near-constant 9.68–11.62% for eight years. Report 47: a dot grid that fills — and keeps what was filled — is the retention mechanic: 67 (11.38%, mean 4.70), rising to 17.1% of 2025–26 reviews ('マスが埋まっていくのを見るのが、地味に達成感を感じてとても良い'); calendar / month view praised 9; a combined all-habit overview calendar requested 6 (mean 4.50); the month view showing only a week is a payer's bug. Report 58: daily / weekly / monthly / yearly progress views with unrestricted history are an adoption reason for 5 ('you can see all of your history not just a month back'). Report 59 (Tappsk): habits show a week, not a month — 'Не нашел полноценную сводную статистику по всем привычкам' (no proper summary across all habits, 3★); REQ_STATS 114 (1.3% of the latest era); the experiment is a month view per habit. Report 60 (Mindway): a routine planner sold without any consistency view is judged 'just a to-do list' by 10 reviewers including 5 payers; the minimal fix proposed is a completion % plus current streak plus a 30-day grid (E4). Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): statistics are not on the main screen and have to be sought out — named as a reason a 4★ is 'consider[ing] other options'; P6: reachable from the main screen without adding clutter.

title: Cloud sync / multi-device as the paid differentiator
statement: Strongest true differentiator among buyers (lift ×9.8). Report 7: absent for 3+ years, sync was the #1 3★/4★ theme with named willingness to pay; ship it opt-in and end-to-end (CloudKit private database) to keep a no-account privacy promise. Report 28: cloud sync is bundled with any purchase ('I now realize just buying anything gives u cloud access'; 'il faut payer pour jumeler les comptes'); multi-device sync is named as the advantage over Finch. Report 30: iCloud sync and colour themes are advertised paid features that no reviewer in any market or period mentions. Report 33: one purchase covering iPhone, iPad, Watch, Mac, web, Android and Windows is a leading purchase trigger — and every platform that lagged became a support case (see C251). Report 47: account-based e-mail backup and sync (beta 2020, free in 'version 2.0', Feb 2024) spans iPhone, Android and iPad ('애플이랑 삼성 연동'); cross-platform sync unreliable in 2022; sync / backup failures 16 (mean 2.25, 7 in 10–18 Dec 2019 — '同期中ですとの表示が一向におわらず'); a platform bundle is a stated purchase condition ('Macのリリース、ウィジェット導入、iPadとの同期を求めます。そしたら課金します', 2026). Report 48: cross-device sync is the paid feature most often named as the purchase reason; multi-platform praise recovered from 0.78% to 3.13% with the Mac app (Mar 2022), yet sync failure is the one reliability theme that never improved (11 / 12 / 12 / 13 per era) and is the most common reliability complaint in 2022–26. Report 50: one account across iPhone, iPad and Mac, free within the cap. Report 54: iCloud sync / backup absent (8, 4.12) — 'I don't give it 5 stars because it lacks iCloud sync'. Report 55: cross-device sync was the headline paid feature and the most often named purchase reason (19 of 165 payers), mostly in 1–2★ because it failed ('If you are about to buy it for the sync option. I suggest you keep your money'; 'Paid £17.49 to sync phone/iPad/watch and it doesn't work'); SYNC_BUG 62 (1.90) with a 7.12× payer lift and 'servers are dead' by 2019. Report 56: optional iCloud sync shipped free and headlines a positive review ('Simple, free, privacy friendly - optional icloud sync'). Report 57: cross-device is the largest unmet need in the product's history — 72 (9.24%): sync 44, iPad 21, Mac 8, backup 17 — flat across eras (29 / 28 / 27) and 84% Korean; one JP report of iCloud working (2024) against six later Korean 'it doesn't'; a Premium user in 2026 'I bought Premium and iPad doesn't seem to sync'. Report 58: cross-device use requested by 2 (a 3★ whose whole review is 'so I can work in two different places') against 2 who chose the app because it has no account — if sync ships it must be optional and never a precondition for first use; accounts and servers bring the 1★ failure classes the corpus is free of. Report 59 (Tappsk): iCloud sync between devices is Premium and reviewers ask for it free ('в бесплатной версии синхронизировать устройства нельзя'; 'оставить синхронизацию в бесплатной версии'); the Mac app was sold separately in 2020–22 (MON_PER_DEVICE 59: 'Она платная для тех кто уже премиум?') and later folded into Premium. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'looked really promising and reasonably priced, but does not let you sync between your Phone and iPad' (US, 1★) — a willing buyer who did not buy solely for this; 'revenue-blocking, not cosmetic'. Report 65 (Rabit): platform_gaps 55 (11.04%, mean 4.25) — widget, Watch, iPad, desktop, sync — 'Rabit exists on exactly one surface'; SYNC_REQ 4 (4.75) and the entitlement failures share a root, no reliable account layer (S6).

title: Multiple reminders per habit
statement: Moderate purchase reason; first reminder stays free. Report 25: an optional intra-day recurring reminder (every N minutes until completed) requested by 4, including a paying user's medication use case. Report 31: multiple reminders per habit were paid in the one-time era and are among what buyers value after paying. Report 33: multiple reminders per habit were moved to Premium in 2019 and cited as a paid feature buyers value ('With the premium subscription, I can add multiple reminders'). Report 47: multiple reminders per habit with editable text are free here and praised by 10 (all 5★). Report 48: several alerts per day per tracker with user-written text — 224 praise (4.87), free. Report 55: early iOS builds allowed one reminder per day while Android allowed several. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_ADVANCE_REMINDER 68 — earlier or multiple reminders per task. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): one reminder per day only — 'Please make it possible to have reminders several times a day, so you can set a reminder to drink water or walk steps' (TJ, 3★).

title: Shared / group habits
statement: Strong purchase driver where it exists, but the worst-executed feature — demand is proven, execution is the risk. Report 23: task sharing / accountability partner exists but is described as weak and one-way; social layer requested by 28 (0.39%). Report 24: in-app community ('Circles', 370, mean 3.897) and time-boxed group challenges exist; the word 'God' being blocked in Circles drew 14 complaints. Report 25: friends / accountability / leaderboard requested by 10 fans (mean 4.80); no social feature exists. Report 26: eight Chinese reviewers ask for the community features of the discontinued '种子习惯' (Seed Habit) app. Report 31: social / shared lists / family to-do requested by 49 (mean 3.27); a parent tracking attention to each child. Report 33: challenges, friends and sharing (2022+) are mixed (challenges 19, some gated), and the report recommends hiding them until enabled. Report 48: shared / partner accountability requested by 22 (mean 4.45), including a coach who would move 100 clients onto the app if it existed. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_SHARED 65 (0.43%) never stops across eight years; the listing advertises sharing a task to a friend's Tappsk, praised by only 5.

title: Skip / holiday / pause mode (pause a habit or counter without losing history)
statement: Minor purchase factor; free or paid open. In report 3, pause/stop/archive is the highest-leverage missing feature (44 requests at mean 4.02, 'the only thing between me and 5★'). Report 23: pausing a task and un-pausing it marked the paused days as missed and destroyed the streak — the defect defeats the feature's entire purpose; reported 2023–24 with no visible fix (57 archive/pause mentions). Report 25: vacation/pause, skip-a-day ('Jump'), mark-not-done ('Cancel') and archive all exist and are praised. Report 26: a vacation/pause mode is requested with flexible recurrence (12). Report 27: a goal end date so a completed goal stops repeating but stays visible, and habit archiving, were asked for by a 3★ reviewer — both appear on the listing and were not findable. Report 28: 'the only way to remove a habit from view is to delete it, but that results in losing all its data'; one wants to mark a routine as 'established' and retire it. Report 29: an end-date / no-end-date control requested (4) — set a habit with no end and change it later. Report 30: there is no habit end-date, so deleting a finished habit wipes its history, and Skip breaks the daily completion ring so users feel they failed a day they completed — one frequency + end-date feature closes both. Report 31: every-N-days, bi-weekly, skip, vacation mode and end dates requested by 84 (mean 3.12) — 'lose a 100+ day streak because … vacation'; a streak freeze is named as the missing piece between 4★ and 5★. Report 33: pause / vacation mode never existed (18 requests; a 'reschedule' swipe) — the report asks for a pause that preserves streaks. Report 34: skip / pause / sick day requested by 5 ('i am sick and cannot swim … i dont want to loose my results'). Report 46: skip marks — a half-square and a triangle — with a 'don't skip twice' rule are praised by 41 (mean 4.93: 'no punishment other than a break in the color gradient') and confuse 19 for seven years ('What does the triangle and squares mean?????'; a subscriber who will 'cancel until this is fixed') — a legend reachable from the grid. Report 48: no skip / vacation mode (13) and weekly goals that still demand a daily answer (21 weekday-scheduling) are 'the two structural scoring complaints', sustained across all five eras from otherwise-happy users — report's change #10. Report 50: streak freeze / habit pause is the most-requested missing capability (3, mean 4.33) and archive (2) — 'It makes me feel guilty for losing my streaks, but like sometimes your routine has to change for a few days!'; 'it's much easier for me to continue a streak when it's large rather than from ground zero'; skipped days visually distinct (1) — the report's S4: ship freeze / pause / archive together as retention mechanics. Report 53: the most-upvoted review in the corpus (274 votes) asks for archive / pause — 'to keep my page organized I have to delete some habits, which means losing all the records'; skips that don't count as failures (CORE_SKIP 20, 4.20). Report 55: a sick / skip day that keeps the streak (CORE_SKIP 5). Report 57: a skip / rest day shipped mid-2024 ('which I've been eagerly waiting for') but only reachable from the calendar step and still requested after. Report 65 (Rabit): S3 — skip / exempt a legitimately impossible day without killing the plant (CORE_SKIP 2), 'turns the gamification's biggest liability into a fair mechanic'.

title: Passcode lock
statement: Minor; decide whether needed at all. Report 31: a passcode / Touch ID lock was moved behind the paywall in 2019; privacy / passcode 16 mentions. Report 33: the passcode lock was removed in 2025, a lifetime holder's complaint. Report 55: passcode lock exists; Touch ID requested (LOCK 6), including in Germany. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_PASSCODE 12 (4.92★).

title: App-icon themes
statement: Minor purchase factor. Report 23: the alternate app icon is frequently cited as a delight (included in the one-time price). Report 33: per-habit colours and themes requested by 48 ('I dislike blue … would pay more'). Report 65 (Rabit): an autistic user asks for an alternate app icon — 'não combina com quem quer ser produtivo… Sou autista e ele me incomoda muito' (REQ_APPICON 2).

title: Quit-habit / bad-habit mode
statement: Well received where shipped; see Quit Habit Decision research doc. Report 23: negative ('don't') tasks shipped in v3.0, Jul 2017. Report 25: a 'bad habit' mode exists and counts against the cap; a bad-habit limit exceeded at 200% is scored as success; a long review asks whether to name it 'smoked' or 'didn't smoke'. Report 31: build and quit habits in one list is praised by 96 ('the ONLY app I've found that does that'); quit-to-zero goals were removed in Mar 2022 and Jan 2023 (sobriety tracking), and 30 find quit/zero-goal habits confusing — restore them. Report 33: bad-habit / limit tracking done well requested by 23 — a tap per cigarette, auto-fail over the limit. Report 34: bad-habit / quit tracking 6 — 'I'd rather not see TO DO next to bad habits'. Report 36: a quit-a-habit inverse mode requested once. Report 41: break-a-bad-habit mode (max units per day) praised by 36 (mean 4.69); Screen Time as a trackable bad habit requested by 4. Report 43: negative / 'avoid' habit tracking requested by 3. Report 46: a habit-breaking mode (colour fades when the bad habit is logged) is praised by 42 (mean 4.98) — alcohol, sugar, screen time — though its logic is unclear to some. Report 48: bad-habit / 'less is better' tracking (a limit, not a goal; red / green inverts) praised by 105 (2.39%, 4.81) — a quit-smoking reviewer benchmarked 10+ rivals; yes / no semantics turn ambiguous in bad-habit logging (12). Report 50: a quit / reduce mode with a reset-on-relapse counter praised by 6 (4.83) — trichotillomania ('The fact that I have to reset the tracker every time I "fall back" gives me the more motivation'), drinking. Report 52: bad habits that deduct reward points (78, weak, mean 4.8). Report 53: limits and zero goals — 'no more than 3 coffees', count-down counters (CORE_BAD 21, 3.76). Report 54: quit-habit tracking requested (4). Report 55: quit-habit use for smoking, alcohol, nail-biting and NoFap (USE_QUIT 46, 4.83) via 'not more than' goals — 'a nail biter for 26 years but getting to tap yes! everyday is exactly what I needed to finally stop'.

title: Data export / backup / CSV
statement: Requested a lot from happy users, rarely a purchase trigger — charging for it generates requests, not revenue. Report 18: export was asked for from the app's fifth month to its last, named as a purchase condition twice ('add export and I'll subscribe for life'), and is the honest answer to five years of unresolved data-loss reports — it lets users protect themselves. Report 20: export never shipped (9 requests, mean 4.44). Report 23: CSV export is included in the one-time price. Report 25: CSV export exists but is described as weak (3). Report 27: data export is praised ('export data for nerdy kind') and the one-tap note export was removed in 2025, producing the only 2★. Report 28: no export mentioned; cloud sync paid. Report 29: add a local CSV/JSON export to Files, account-free, so a date bug can never again mean total loss — three independent export/backup requests. Report 31: backup to Dropbox/iCloud and CSV export were manual only with a repeated backup nag; export hangs ('I can't export my data to move to another app because it hangs on the CSV export') — export is the exit door, keep it open and fast; export to Google Drive was a purchase trigger. Report 33: CSV export was removed with Habitify X (Aug 2020) and back from 2022. Report 34: CSV export disabled in Feb 2026 ('Out of nowhere … years of data are stuck in this app'; 'Vendor Lock', 1★) and a paid backup required before deleting (1★) — both data-lock-in reviews are 1★ (mean 1.00) in a no-account app where export is the only exit. Report 41: CSV export shipped Feb 2023 after a year of requests ('Now that the developer has added CSV export… the app is 5-star awesome for me') and is named as a purchase reason ('so my data is safe'); praised by 14 (mean 4.71). Report 42: no export or backup; history beyond ~2 weeks paywalled ('if you don't pay you won't see last month's result'). Report 43: CSV / PDF export requested by 2; no export exists in a local-storage app that lost four-year histories. Report 46: export / backup / print requested by 3 in an app that lost users' history. Report 47: sharing / export requested by 3, RecStyle named as the CSV model. Report 48: CSV export is premium, praised and occasionally broken (16 requests, 4 export bugs). Report 52: data export requested (59, weak). Report 55: CSV / Excel export is paid and bought for; 5 of 15 export reviews report failures. Report 57: backup is manual Dropbox (Jan 2020) and Premium-gated — 'so you can't back up at all unless you buy — this is practically blackmail'. Report 65 (Rabit): backup moved behind the paywall in 2023 while restore failed for payers; zero export requests in six years.

title: Apple Health integration
statement: Small volume, very high purchase intent. Report 23: HealthKit auto-completion (277, 3.81%, mean 4.35) is 'the single highest-leverage integration in the category' — it removes the friction that killed every other habit app the reviewer tried; a weak tail of misfires (auto-completing without action 11; Health data miscounting 9). Report 25: two-way Apple Health is a purchase trigger (32, 2.44%) with a weak tail of demonstrably wrong mappings — weight read as an entry count, steps off by 568, running only measurable in minutes, step counting starting at 04:00 (9, 0.69%). Report 27: Apple Health integration (exercise, water, steps, sleep) requested once, 4★. Report 31: Apple Health integration covers ~10 preset tasks (steps, sleep, exercise minutes); 79 mentions (mean 2.85); Health sync named as the missing piece between 4★ and 5★. Report 33: Apple Health auto-logging and Fitbit, Strava, screen-time and NFC habits, described as both free and Premium; Health integration complaints rose to 2.2% of E5 and Garmin / wearable auto-completion is requested. Report 36: Apple Health requested by 3 — a 10,000-step habit that auto-completes. Report 41: Apple Health auto-completion (53 mentions) is a switch reason ('Coming from Grit, I almost instantly bought it because the Apple Health habits actually work') and a payer failure ('I paid for it specifically for synching with the health app'); Health gaps 8. Report 43: Apple Health integration requested once. Report 48: Apple Health auto-logging of steps / weight and Siri Shortcuts voice logging praised by 17 (rising to 1.56% of 2022–26); 3 Health sync bugs. Report 50: Health auto-tracking of steps, calories, distance and exercise with historical import praised by 7 (4.71, 5 US); 5 (4.60; 4.50% of US) want weight, sleep, mindful minutes and Apple Fitness session types synced instead of hand-entered — one says weight sync would move the rating to 5; a Health sync break after an update (1). Report 53: Apple Health integration is what reviewers could not find elsewhere (HK_GOOD 40 — the Watch Breathe app 'automatically marks that as complete'; calories logged from the wrist) and they ask for more sources — sleep, running, calories, blood pressure, Fitbit, Garmin, Strava (HK_WANT 31). Report 54: Health app / Fitbit sync requested (2). Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'It doesn't communicate with iPhone Health-fitness; it said it did' (TR, 2★) — if the listing promises it, an expectation mismatch, worse than an absent feature; I5: make the link work or remove the claim, the cheapest immediate fix. Report 64 (Critique AI): Apple Health and Hevy sync requested with exercise animations (us, 3★).

title: Apple Watch app (done properly: timer, two-way sync)
statement: Small volume, very high purchase intent; a half-built Watch app draws 2–3★. Report 20: an Apple Watch app was the highest-mean capability gap (62 requests, mean 4.15), asked for by the happiest users and named in churn-to-Streaks reviews; never shipped. Report 23: the Watch is the app's strongest differentiator and most fragile surface — 626 mentions (8.61%), 241 negative (mean 3.13) vs 385 positive (mean 4.35); it breaks on each watchOS generation (2016, watchOS 7, 2021–22 mirroring, watchOS 10 complications, 2024–26 blank complications); in Korea (13.5%) and Japan (13.3%) it is the dominant topic; 'I bought this for the Watch and it doesn't work' are the highest-value churn events. Report 24: in a 43,469-review coaching corpus the Watch (69, 0.16%) and widget (53, 0.12%) are marginal — the surface matters where the product is a checklist, not where it is content. Report 25: the Watch app (21 mentions, mean 4.48, 0 1★) is part of a praised Apple-platform surface (Watch + Mac + widgets + Shortcuts + Health), but one reviewer says it was 'suddenly removed' (Oct 2025) and another that the listing advertised Watch support that could not be installed. Report 26: no Apple Watch app throughout; requested by 8 (0.21%). Report 27: Apple Watch, Apple Health and macOS are each requested once (4★ 'Would be perfect with watch support'); the report says a paid tier, if ever, should attach only to such not-yet-existing capability. Report 31: the Watch app and complication were broken for long periods — 60 reviews (mean 2.33); support asked for a video, then silence; ''update coming soon'. 6 months later'; the v2 rebuild (Mar 2022) broke it and restored it months later. Report 33: the Watch app broke with iOS 13, would not launch after Habitify X, its complication broke with iOS 15.1 and sync lagged until 'finally' fixed Jan 2024 — 100 reviews (2.84 mean), 6.8% of E3, Japan 5.0% ('Streaks costs a tenth and works'); single-tap logging and area complications were removed. Report 36: Apple Watch requested by 9 (mean 4.11), one wanting the haptics on the wrist. Report 41: the Watch app shipped in 2021 on request (discussion peaked 13.7% then normalised); a privacy-minded payer cancelled because Watch sync requires iCloud and will return for 'easy normal Bluetooth sync between the phone and the watch'. Report 43: Apple Watch requested by 12 over five years (May 2019 'Not using your app due to lack of iwatch' → Jan 2024), the listing now ships Watch, and no request appears after Jan 2024. Report 46: Apple Watch shipped Mar 2021 and the request stopped (3 → 2 → 0 → 0); Watch ↔ phone sync is then a failure surface ('finished goals on the watch won't show up on the phone and vice versa… a deal breaker'). Report 47: Apple Watch requested by 6, all 2020–22; the listing shows iPhone, Mac and Vision only. Report 48: Watch app and complication praised by 24 (4.67) when working, faulted by 12 (2.33) when blank; 8 want a complication. Report 50: a Watch app shipped Jan–May 2025 after requests ('almost perfect, it just needs a watch app'); one 1★ calls it useless — no habit complication, notifications not working. Report 52: Apple Watch check-in requested every year since 2019 (PLAT_WATCH 256, 1.24%, 4.52) — 'one reviewer bought a Watch for this app'. Report 53: Watch complications configurable 'almost like watch faces themselves' are a purchase trigger (WATCH_GOOD 43, 4.70) while WATCH_BUG 62 (2.85) — duplicate water entries, sync, the Watch app crashing on launch in 2025–26; F6: re-certify the Watch app on every iOS release. Report 54: no Watch app (9, 4.22) — 'now I'm forced to use another app' (DE); 'lemme know if you're working on the watch app and I'll be the first one to buy this app' (PK). Report 55: no Watch app (PLATFORM_WANT 24). Report 56: an Apple Watch app requested once. Report 57: a Watch app shipped ~Mar 2020 ('moved to see it on the Watch') and hung on 'Loading…' for 26 (19 in 2020–21), then was largely fixed (0.94% of 2024–26). Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_WATCH 81 fell from 4.7% of the launch year to 0.0% of the latest era as PR_WATCH 37 appeared — a request that stops is the trace of a shipped feature. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): an Apple Watch app requested once (UZ, 4★); treated as absent as of Jan 2026, lowest priority of the set. Report 65 (Rabit): REQ_WATCH 5 (1.00%, mean 3.80) — two frame the Watch as how they would actually get reminded.

title: Interactive widget check-off
statement: Mark done without opening the app; small volume, very high intent. Report 18: 'let me check off without launching the app' was the single most-repeated widget request across five years and every language; some builds fixed it (Jul 2025) and then it regressed. Report 23: an interactive Today-view widget shipped Jan 2017 to enthusiasm, was lost at iOS 14 (Sept 2020) and asked for back continuously for five years (36 named requests) — one of the top three reasons for a downgrade from a previously-happy user; restore it via App Intents. Report 26: an interactive widget to tick from the home screen requested (~5); the garden-view widget is free. Report 27: reviewers wrote the widget spec — 'a small widget that just showed the current streak count for a single goal'; 'a streak counter on the widget like duolingo'; 'a grayed out version if it's still to do and a coloured version if it's done'; tappable to check off — requested in 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026; in a streak app the widget is the retention surface. Report 28: an interactive check-off widget requested continuously for four and a half years by satisfied users (mean 4.64, zero negatives). Report 29: a Home Screen widget showing today's list requested by 16 across 26 months, 7 of them in 2026. Report 31: a tappable Today-view widget (2018–2021) was replaced in Oct 2021 by a non-interactive home/lock-screen widget limited to 4 habits (a user with a memory disability 'requesting a refund'); before that, the app had no iOS 14 widget for a year — 73 of 451 reviews (16.2%) Sep 2020 – Sep 2021 and 14.0% of E2 asked about it; the widget peaks in the 4★ band (12.6% vs 3.8%). Report 33: the 2016 Today widget was removed ('the entire reason I paid'), iOS 14 widgets were non-interactive, and the May 2025 redesign removed compact, incremental (+1) and streak widgets — widget complaints 6.3% of 2025, the one surface still worsening; interactive widgets named as the 4★ → 5★ piece. Report 34: 7 interactive-widget requests, all after static widgets shipped (Mar 2024) — 'The widgets still aren't interactive' (Feb 2026). Report 36: 'instead of taking advantage of the iOS 17 update with interactive widgets, they preferred to make that option paid' (2★); interactive widget requested by 4. Report 48: widget interactivity was removed after arriving ~2020; the request persists (20). Report 50: widgets with check-off shipped by Nov 2024 after a Mar 2024 request; interactive check-off, quick-append journal, compact and weekly-progress widgets still requested (3); widget lag (1). Report 52: 'Maybe the most important features of ShineDay are its widgets. Being able to check off completed habits without opening the app' — when iOS 14 replaced tap-to-check with a ring that opens the app (Oct 2020) 55 widget-bug reviews arrived in one month; check-in was removed from the widget again in 2026. Report 53: check off from the widget, hide completed, more habits per widget (WIDGET_WANT 18). Report 54: the top request (41, 11.11%, 4.29; P1 7.5% → P3 17.6%, open since Oct 2020, first asked one month after iOS 14), 19 of them five-star and a named purchase blocker for 3 of 5 ('If there were a home-screen widget I'd open it far more often — then I'd be more willing to buy', TW); framed as retention by ADHD and autistic users ('once it's closed i never use it'); D3: build it as a completion surface, not a display surface. Report 55: widget or notification check-off requested (WIDGET_WANT 16). Report 56: per-habit home-screen widgets with one-tap completion are the differentiator (9 of 67 name them; 'the empty dots on my home screen guilt trip me into being productive and honestly? it works'); a multi-habit widget designed in detail (dates across, habits down), more than 4 widgets and transparency requested; a widget tap that opened the app instead of completing broke the most-praised interaction (fixed in v2.3.2). Report 57: the widget tap launched the app instead of checking in from the iOS 14 rewrite (Nov 2020) until Dec 2023 — 16 reviews ('if it's a widget the check should happen right there — why is the app launching?'; 'give us back checking from the widget'), zero after. Report 58: 'THE WIDGET that is clickable?? the best ever'; 'The widget option is legit a life saver!'. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): a widget that shows the next unfinished habit is requested (UZ, 4★); widgets are credited with the strongest outcome statement in the corpus.

title: Streaks / gamification
statement: High-priority praise, moderate purchase factor. Report 10 (contested): streaks added to a non-punitive pet app generated their own defect stream (171, growing 74×) and pressure stream (96) — net-negative in the written record for an ADHD audience. Report 20: a streak counter was requested 71 times (mean 3.72) — always alongside, never instead of, the decaying strength score. Report 23: streak psychology is the highest-satisfaction theme (902, 12.41%, mean 4.75, 0.7% 1★ — reviewers get out of bed to preserve a streak); rewards/badges/levels are requested by fans (136, 1.87%, mean 4.43). Report 24: streak counters with 'freeze' passes and certificates; Duolingo is named for its streak freezes. Report 27: streaks are the core praised mechanic in a deliberately non-gamified app — no pets, no flashy graphics, no urgency; behaviour-change outcomes ('I'm on a 9 day vacuuming streak!') rose 0% → 11.9% across eras. Report 28: gamification (carrots, levels, rooms, a pet) is the differentiator in an 821-review corpus — but 10 (mean 2.40) say 'it's a game, not a tracker', an expectation mismatch the listing could pre-empt. Report 31: motivation through bars filling, streaks and sounds is praised by 200 rated 4–5★ ('an adult sticker chart!'); removing the streak count from the main list in v3.0 drew 52 complaints (100% E4), including medication and 30-day pill-cycle users; the report proposes a streak-on-list toggle and testing its default on logging frequency. Report 33: motivation / streaks praised by 130 (mean 4.75); non-daily streaks broke and the streak count on the complete button changed in redesigns. Report 47: the streak resets to zero on a miss — praised as motivating by 3 (5.00) and non-punitive framing praised by 4 ('scoring points, not losing them') vs empty squares demotivating 1; a cumulative total was added by 2025 after 2020–21 requests. Report 48: streak motivation 144 at mean 4.96 — the highest of any theme with n > 100 ('I can't bear to see it go'); 507-day and 1,000-day streaks; gamified rewards requested by 17 (4.47); a 2013–14 points system was disliked (10). Report 55: 'I completed a task because I didn't want to break my streak'; 'over 10K pushups… because I don't want to disappoint the app' — motivation layer 362 (17.89%, 4.86). Report 56: do not add streak pressure, scores or gamification to a product chosen for restraint — one streak request against 'no subscription, no guilt' and 39 restraint reviews. Report 58: streaks praised by 5 ('It's so fun every time I get a streak'). Report 60 (Mindway): the absence of streaks or any progress view is what payers name when they call the product under-built — the 'encouragement' and 'tracking consistency' they expected and did not get. Report 64 (Critique AI): XP, quests and leaderboards are 'unambiguously liked' (8, 1.91%, mean 4.00) and proposed as the free hook ('keep the workout and XP/leaderboard free'), with one sharp dissent that generated tasks 'seem more like XP grabs than anything else'.

title: Scholarship / hardship / discount program
statement: The cleanest 5★ generator in report 1 (91 of 101 mentions 5★); also works around broken payment rails; never switch it off. Report 10: a 'Guardian' pay-it-forward sponsorship programme is one of the only monetisation themes with a positive mean (4.76 across 708 mentions); its one complaint is that there is no visible way to apply. Report 31: ~110 teen and low-income reviewers (2.12%, mean 2.31) in the 2022–23 TikTok cohort ('your target market at this point is us teenagers'; ages 14, 12, 11; a mental-health user who can't work) — lead with a student / low-income price in those markets. Report 34: a 50% annual offer converted ('I paid £9.99 for a whole year - bargain!'), affordability complaints come from students, Vietnam and ADHD users; the report proposes a student / regional price and New-Year sales. Report 36: AFFORD 5 (mean 2.20) — two on disability, a student, and 'there is no way I can afford it without being part of the demographic which can drop 60$ on a reminder app'. Report 41: a high-school student asks for a student deal; a Turkish 5★ says the one-time fee is too much 'at least in my country'; the report proposes purchasing-power-adjusted lifetime tiers in the long-tail storefronts. Report 42: 'I was ready to pay, but it has to be reasonable… I'm sure if you lower the price, revenue will grow' (RU); price objections at $39.99–$59.99 in high-income markets vs '500₽ a year, that's nothing'. Report 46: students and minors ask for a discount ('the only money i get is chore money and i have to wash the windows for it', 5★; a Cambridge scholarship student; 'please offer discount for students'; 'Is there a discount code for lifetime?'); the report's E5 is a student / youth discount; a discount honoured after it expired won a 5★. Report 49: 30 cannot afford it, 12 of them self-identified minors, in a 9+ app marketed on anime social media; an under-18 / student free programme exists but only 3 reviewers know of it — the report's experiment: surface it. Report 52: students without money are a named barrier ('forty-plus yuan, any conscience?', Grade 7; '¥30 when I was a student, ¥80 now'). Report 54: in CN the one-time ¥98 price competes against a ¥3/month anchor (a pricing-architecture problem). Report 57: 'how about a two-week trial then a discount — I'd just pay under ₩20,000'; a Mexican reviewer 'please put a discount on it'. Report 58: budget-constrained adopters ('as a broke student'; 'Good for broke but productive people'; 'I'm a young lady trying to save up') will not convert to a subscription.

title: Handle markets where card payment fails (RU, AR, TR, DZ, PK)
statement: Users who want to pay cannot; a discount/hardship path doubles as the workaround. Report 26: 16 reviews (mean 4.06 — willing buyers, not complaints) cannot pay — 8 Russian ('the trial button is not clickable… possibly because I live in Russia'; cards cannot be linked), 3 Chinese/Taiwanese ('tap subscribe and nothing happens'; a ¥38 tier shown with no in-app path), 2 Vietnamese (ShopeePay / MoMo requested); Russia is 19.18% of the corpus and its highest-satisfaction market — the highest-yield-per-effort monetisation item. Report 42: 'there's no way to pay from Russia' (Jun 2026) — a market with the worst defect exposure receiving paywall pressure it cannot convert. Report 49: dollar-pegged pricing in Türkiye, sanctions blocking cards, no UPI / local payment method (7). Report 52: 2018 purchase flow broken — 112 billing reviews that year, including no Alipay or WeChat Pay. Report 59 (Tappsk): the largest documented case — App Store payment became unavailable to Russian users from 2022-03; MON_PAYMENT_METHOD 74 (72 on the ru storefront, 54 of them 5★ because the reviewers want to pay and ask how — 'не могу оплатить премиум - версию, с кем мне связаться'; 'Вы теряете живые деньги' — you are losing real money); support arranged card or carrier billing case by case within minutes ('в течении 10-20 минут решили'; 'у меня мобильный оператор Megafon') and from 2024 a direct bank-card route is praised ('спасибо, что можно оплачивать напрямую по банковской карте'; 'за возможность альтернативной оплаты подписки для РФ'); the same era brought switchers from Trello and Notion after those services left Russia; the cost is the cancellation gap ([[C210]], [[C112]]). Removing the Russian storefront drops payment-access complaints from 0.7% to 0.0% and billing from 3.2% to 1.4%.

title: Localise early — it unlocks revenue
statement: Missing localisation is the biggest market-specific complaint and a stated purchase blocker; shipping a language visibly converts (Japan). Report 10: localisation is HIGH-PRIORITY at country level in eight storefronts at once (cn 26%, ru 18%, tr 19%, br 13%, es 12%); reviewers say they will not pay in English. Report 13: Arabic is the largest unserved language (20.5% of Saudi reviews); users were also served the wrong language ('I am from Turkey but this app language is Korean', 41 votes) and shown store screenshots in languages the app does not have. Report 18: Japanese Instagram ads led to an app that opened in Korean with a KakaoTalk login; Korean push notifications persisted a year after the UI was fixed, the terms page stayed English-only (one reviewer refused to trial for that reason), Traditional Chinese was largely Simplified wording, and a Dutch translation was unintelligible. Report 19: an Instagram ad ran in Spanish for an English-only app — 'tell me if there's a Spanish version and if not, refund the money'. Report 20: Russian-first UI leaked to Chinese, French and Swiss users, Chinese localisation existed and was later removed ('there was Chinese a few years ago'), and Ukrainian was requested and never added. Report 23: bad German localisation ('Die Übersetzung ins Deutsche ist total fehlgeschlagen') undercut the premium price in the corpus's worst large market (mean 3.62); machine-translated Chinese help text drew 52 upvotes and was still cited seven years later; localisation-quality complaints span de, ru, se, kr, cn, tw, jp and es (mixed EN/ES notifications, English-only icon search); a Hangul IME bug went unfixed five years. Report 24: the praise vocabulary (small steps, coaching, art, 'life-changing') appears in every language and the forced-water complaint in six; language requests concentrate in Vietnam, Uzbekistan, Russia, Brazil and Italy; Germany praises the app's craft at 19.61% (3× the corpus); China (1,250 reviews, mean 3.431, 28.6% 1★) is unreadable by an English-anchored classifier. Report 25: localisation demand is new and growing (0% → 1.0% → 2.7%; Turkish 9, Korean 3, Italian 3, Russian/Ukrainian 3, Chinese 2, Japanese 1); Korea and China are 100% 5★ and 75%/50% localisation requests ('If there is Chinese, it will definitely be loved by the Chinese market') — reached only by users tolerant of an English UI; Turkish shipped Jul 2026 and the review stream responded. Report 26: localisation requests in Arabic, Thai and Spanish; Russian localisation quality criticised in 2023 ('hire a competent localiser') and praised by 2025; the German store listing carried a typo ('Gewohnheitstrinker' — habit drinker); Chinese reviewers ask for the community features of a discontinued app ('种子习惯'); the cn aesthetic rate of 3.12% is a classifier artefact. Report 27: localisation is not an issue — zero complaints across seven non-English reviews; the two Monday-week-start requests (DE, AU) are the only regional-convention issue. Report 28: 21 localisation requests/defects (2.56%) — Spanish 5, Turkish 3, Chinese 3, Japanese 2, Russian 2, French, Thai, Arabic, Portuguese; two are defects on an existing localisation (Japanese glyphs rendered for Chinese, habit names truncated; untranslated English with Chinese selected) and a 2022 localisation update rendered every 'r' as a black square; rest-of-world markets rate higher (4.181 vs 3.956) and are 5× more blocked by language (5.56% vs 1.09%) — 'the cheapest lever in the highest-satisfaction segment'; two name language as why they leave. Report 29: the listing supports 8 languages and not Spanish or Russian, yet 8 Spanish-language reviews arrive from UZ/CL/MX/AR/ES/US and one is blocked ('No puedo cambiar la lengua, ayuden me por favor') — Spanish first is the cheapest defensible localisation case. Report 30: 13 languages functioning and one explicit localisation compliment from Chile; an Arabic onboarding blocker; 11 reviews in a language not matching their storefront. Report 31: 61 localisation requests (1.18%) and French and German reviewers say localisation is their purchase condition ('J'achèterai la version premium quand elle sera traduite en français'; didn't buy Pro because there was no German); China is the happiest storefront (4.09) and the loudest localisation demand (23.9% — '无中文无满分', no Chinese, no full marks); Ukraine 26.7%, Russia 13.6%, France 11.3%; recommended: Spanish, Portuguese, Chinese, German, French, Russian. Report 33: localisation grievances are about quality — 「たどたどしい日本語」 (halting Japanese), simplified-Chinese glyphs in Japanese, an offensive German UI string ('Pisst du dabei?'), a lost Russian UI, English-only support replies — 62 reviews (1.57%); Chinese reviewers praise the localisation; Arabic users ask for an Arabic UI; motivational copy read as 'far too American and over the top' in the Netherlands. Report 34: 19 polite localisation requests (none 1★) — Chinese 9, Russian 4, Spanish 2, French 2, Ukrainian 1 — 11 of them arriving in E3, starting the day a free-lifetime promotion reached br, vn, cn and co: promote into a market only once the app speaks its language. Report 36: localisation requests were 7.0% of E1 (six Chinese-market, May–June 2022, plus MX 1★ 'solo esté en inglés me hace perder el interés') and stopped after mid-2022, consistent with localisation shipping. Report 41: shipping Italian and Traditional Chinese (Jun 2026) brought reviewers straight back to rate 5★ ('I ran straight here to give 5 stars'); missing Spanish blocked a purchase ('es por eso que aún no acabo de lanzarme a comprarla'); Russian — requested from five unrelated storefronts — is the largest unserved language; non-English storefronts like the app equally (4.581) but self-report paying at 5.52% vs 9.9%. Report 42: Russian-language support was the original wedge in Russia ('the competitor has no Russian'), and Russia is both the most appreciative and the most defect-exposed market — where users now cannot pay at all. Report 43: all 10 language requests are non-US (4.37% of non-US reviews) — Arabic three times in fourteen months from Saudi Arabia and Oman, each capping the rating at exactly 3★ ('Nice app but it lacks Arabic support, so it deserves ⭐️⭐️⭐️'); Portuguese and Spanish requests appear answered by the listing's five languages; one 'full of spelling mistakes' (GB, 1★). Report 46: the UI reached 15 languages (Catalan praised by name; Turkish requested with 16 votes in 2020 and praised in Turkish by 2022) but the Learn content, videos and e-mails stayed English — 'all the support is in English, which surprised me because the developer is Spanish. If it were in Spanish, I'd consider subscribing' (ES); Arabic and Russian reviewers ask the same; the report: localise content, Spanish first. Report 47: machine-translated UI costs installs in every non-Japanese market — '적절한 한글화가 절실'; notification options rendered as '汽車' and '手冊' ('car' and 'handbook', TW); 'une traduction française faite de façon automatique et de très mauvaise qualité' — installed and deleted; mainland-Chinese terms shown to Taiwan (5 reviews, none Japanese); Korea's share fell from 32 (2020) to 1 (2025). Report 48: Russia (10.13% no-localization, requests 2013–17) and China (12.33%) are the clearest localization signals; a 2022 review celebrates Chinese localization arriving; rest-of-world raises localization four times as often as high-spend markets; the listing reached 10 languages. Report 49: German added May 2025 but 'sprachlich nicht ganz sauber'; the book summaries and meditations stay English-only — 'localise the content, not just the chrome' — requested in DE, KR, JP, ES, BR, PL; Korea reports unnatural translation in 18.2% of its reviews; behaviour-change praise runs 7.69% in Germany vs 18.13% in the US, plausibly a localisation-quality gap. Report 50: Korea — 4 reviews all 5★, two asking for Korean ('Add korean'; a detailed 5★ written in Korean that still cannot use the app in Korean) — the cleanest unmet-demand signal from a small storefront; experiment: localise into Korean. Report 52: incomplete English — notifications, pop-ups and ads still in Chinese on English devices — is the single largest theme in every eligible non-Chinese storefront (us 22.30%, ca 22.95%, au 20.75%; English-primary 22.1% at mean 3.00) and Traditional Chinese is missing in Taiwan (22.89%); unfixed since a 2020 peak; the ADHD / Focus store subtitle reaches a population that cannot read the app. Report 53: machine-translated or mixed-language UI in ru, br, it, se, kr and jp (DES_LOC 19 — 'you need to study more Japanese'; lock-screen reminders alternating Chinese and English). Report 54: habit lessons English-only inside localised UIs ('this software is all in English', CN; 'English texts are not translated', DE); Arabic and full Chinese requested; a German reviewer calls it 'the only habit tracker in German'; outcome language 16.9% in developed markets vs 4.6% elsewhere — 'a behaviour-change tool in developed markets and a cute utility elsewhere'. Report 55: Brazil — several give 4★ 'only because' there is no Portuguese (DES_LOC 8 of 21, 7.7% of br); a Spanish localisation that was available and then removed ('Antes estaba en español y ahora no'); R6: pt-BR first, then Russian. Report 56: the listing claims Korean and Japanese yet 24 of 43 polled storefronts, Japan included, returned zero reviews; non-English reviewers rate 5.000 vs English 4.882. Report 57: Japan is the most price-sensitive and least-localised storefront — 'settings has English and Korean mixed in'; 'I can't understand explanations written in English… the screen is so minimal that [features] aren't self-evident' (1★); incomplete Simplified Chinese (CN). Report 59 (Tappsk): Ukraine is the only storefront where a language request is distinctive — REQ_LANG 8 (7.75×) ask for a Ukrainian interface, which the 17-language listing does not declare (nor Kazakh); Russian is written from 46 storefronts including 59 reviews on the US storefront; BUG_TRANSLATION 7 (a German widget in Russian). Report 60 (Mindway): the paywall complaint appears in 13 storefronts and 6 languages with the same structure and the benefit claims in near-identical words across ten languages — 'Mindway's value proposition translates'; 59 bodies (27.31%) are non-English across 22 storefronts, and 90 of 125 polled storefronts (Japan, Korea, Spain, India, Russia, Indonesia, Philippines) returned zero reviews. Report 65 (Rabit): Spanish requested Dec 2020 ('Solo pediría añadir el español'), also German, Russian and Vietnamese (LOC_REQ 4); a Brazilian storefront user got English onboarding; being in Portuguese with a Brazilian developer is itself valued ('Amoo a pegada brasileirinha do app 😍 me sinto em casa'; DEV_LOCAL 2). Report 67 (Habio): REQ_LANG 41 (2.00%) — the only request at meaningful strength — from the free era onward ('ojalá pronto la pongan en español también'; 'Nur wie kann ich die App auf deutsch umstellen?'); France 13.19%.

title: Culturally complete icon set and calendars
statement: Islamic icons, disability icons, Hijri and lunar calendars, bigger fonts — cheap, and in markets already blocked by localisation.

title: Billing must be exactly right
statement: Wrong amount, double charge, surprise renewal are the fastest route to 1★ (×21 lift); single price shown, no trial-to-charge traps, refunds honoured, receipts clear. Report 19: a 105-review corpus that was 91% one-star and 71% about money — charged after cancelling (19), charged with no recognised subscription (19), double-billed (16), charged ≠ agreed ($29.99 annual agreed, $59.99/month billed), and terms permitting weekly renewal made 'again and again every week' structurally possible. Report 23: nothing supports deceptive billing on a single Apple payment; refund friction (79, mean 1.75, 70.9% 1★) is Apple's process, and reviewers address Apple through the review field. Report 24: charged after cancelling 1,620 (3.73%, mean 1.085), duplicate charges 584, charge without consent 338 (mean 1.047), not visible in Apple Subscriptions 125 — all consequences of billing outside Apple IAP; 1,412 edited reviews are mostly downgrades after a later charge. Report 31: billing-dispute language in 403 reviews (7.77%, mean 1.24) — refund, scam, fraud, estafa, arnaque, Abzocke, 欺诈 in eight languages — with 13 calling on Apple to remove the developer; billing & entitlement integrity rose 1.6% (E1) → 34.5% (E4) → 25.4% (E5): 768 reviews (14.81%, mean 1.30); discount offers checked out at full price in 69 (49 actually charged; '$59.99 crossed out and … $9.99 … My card was charged full price'; support: 'a bug that happens sometimes') — make the displayed price the charged price and audit introductory-offer configuration per storefront (CA, AU, GB, DE first). Report 33: billing integrity 147 (3.73%, mean 2.22) — charged more than shown (¥4,900 shown, ¥5,150 charged; a $39.99 offer charged $48.97; monthly chosen, annual charged; lifetime then an annual charge); billing-dispute register 「詐欺アプリ」, 'Abzocke', 'CON ARTISTS', 流氓. Report 36: all 3 billing reviews are 1★ — a cancellation link that returns 'Cannot cancel subscription' ('roach motel'), an unauthorised annual charge on a disabled reviewer, and five annual fees for one bundle membership with two refunds denied (China) — triaged regardless of 0.56% share as the only consumer-protection records. Report 42: three payers charged without intending — 'immediately charged for a subscription upon opening the app for the first time'; 'auto-selected a package and deducted money… hadn't even tried it' (499k₫); a promotional R$39.90/year that became R$99.90 at checkout — plus a trial that 'won't get the refund even if you cancel two minutes after'; 11 of 29 writing payers (37.9%) request refunds. Report 46: 13 billing failures (0.60%, mean 2.31) — charged on day one of a 7-day trial (twice), a subscription the app would not recognise ('App does not recognize it and won't let me add more than three habits, even after refreshing… On to the next app'; premium on iPad not on iPhone), a wrong amount (CHF 40.45 for 29.95), four refund requests — vs 2 refund references in report 43's one-time corpus. Report 47: 8 billing failures (1.36%) in a 13-payer corpus — premium reverting to free with ads back (3 in January 2021), '400円を2回も騙し取られた' (charged ¥400 twice), 'アプリを開くと毎回「購入に失敗しました。」' (a purchase-failed loop, Jul 2026), an unintended half-year subscription, a crash the moment a trial payment went through. Report 48: billing problem 23 (2.52) — 1 / 4 / 6 / 12 by era, the fastest-growing monetisation fault: charged $39.99 instead of the agreed $4.99; charged the full year at the start of a 7-day trial; charged twice after cancelling before the trial ended, blocking other App Store purchases; 'another active subscriber using the same receipt'; paid subscription not recognised after an update (3); 23 refund requests at mean 1.04★ — the lowest-mean theme with n > 10. Report 49: every overcharge review is a payer — €1.99/month becoming €30 at once, $2/month becoming $70, £25 on top of £29.99, a year charged during a trial, seven months of charges after cancellation (9; payers 8.49% vs 0.73% globally). Report 50: 3 reviews (mean 1.00, all 1★, Aug 2024 → Jan 2026) charged an amount not matching the quote — '$14.99 for the yearly membership' vs a $31.01 bank charge; 'said to be $14.99 after the free trial but I was charged $30 before my free trial was up. This app is a scam'; ~$50 annual auto-charge — the same ~$15 advertised vs ~$30 charged 17 months apart; 'The app does not accept any of my cards' (2 cannot pay) — the only defect class with a 1.00 mean and no exceptions; fix F1 and experiment: instrument price displayed vs charged per storefront. Report 52: 2018–2020 billing defects (261, 83.5% in those years: purchases that spin forever, double charges, ¥12 shown but ¥31 charged); a gb 'lifetime' purchase billed as £12.99/month (2023); a tw buyer of the NT$390 lifetime unlock charged NT$220 when the concurrent trial converted (Aug 2026); an SMS login that subscribed a user to ¥55/month of carrier services (single report, legal exposure). Report 53: unexpected charges PAY_CHARGE 34 (mean 1.38, 85.3% 1★); a one-week trial billed for a year (kr); an accidental purchase on first open. Report 54: a purchase that never unlocked ('I paid for the app and absolutely nothing. It's exactly as it was before', AU; 'Still telling me Become a habit pro!', KR) — 6, mean 1.17. Report 55: 'BEEN TRYING FOR MONTHS TO CANCEL MY SUBSCRIPTION'; auto-renewal on an account the user can't log in to; charged after a trial (PAY_CHARGE 7). Report 57: listed ₩29,000 but the card was charged ₩44,000; ₩3,994 charged after a redeem code. Report 59 (Tappsk): U_BILLING 485 (3.20%, mean 2.30★) is the largest negative that is neither a price objection nor a product defect; even the reviewer's own missed cancellation ('забыла отменить подписку', 5★) lands as a support ticket in the reviews, and refunds are reported both granted ('Все вернули! Оперативно') and refused ('Деньги, естественно, никто не возвращает'). Report 60 (Mindway): billing operations failing is 'a store-risk problem, not a pricing problem' — 11 of 216 (5.09%, mean 1.27, 10 of 11 US): charged for a year without subscribing ('this needs to be reported and i want my money back'), charged after cancelling with screenshots of inactive status, a $0.99 'free trial' billed $39.99 within hours, a 3-day trial that billed a week after cancelling on day two, monthly implied but the whole year drafted; the corpus cannot prove the charges were unauthorized, but eleven users could not tell what they had agreed to or how to get out, and seven of them used a public review as their support channel; all 13 confirmed payers are the only source of every refund, cancellation and surprise-charge report — 'the corpus contains no post-purchase success story at all'. Report 64 (Critique AI): 'On the website it said cancel anytime but it immediately billed me'; 'They say that they give a three day trial but charge you for the full year upfront'; reinstall charged again — PAY_BILLING 8 (1.91%, mean 1.50), 6 of 13 self-stated payers. Report 65 (Rabit): billing_failure 28 (5.62%, mean 1.75) nearly all payers; PAY_REFUND 8 at mean 1.12 — the lowest of any theme — for crashes after an annual subscription, reminders not working after Plus, ads despite paying, a post-trial charge, and two unanswered refund emails. Report 67 (Habio): U_BILLING_HARM 878 (42.81%, mean 1.04; 60.05% of non-seeded) — charged after cancelling 351, trial conversion 173, workbook 189, charged with no subscription 164, duplicate charges 157, amount above shown 55; U_ESCALATION 196 (9.56%): bank / card / PayPal disputes 118 and regulator / police / legal threats 94 (BBB, FTC, ACCC, state attorneys general, OCU, Sernac, Verbraucherzentrale — 'Abofalle'); a card statement under the company name the customer had to research ('Tuve que investigar que aplicaciones tenía GOTOTOP LTD').

title: Sync must work — and prove it
statement: The paid feature that breaks most; sync failure is ×12.8 over-represented among buyers. Report 13: iCloud sync complaints rose 10× from 2015 to 2021 and ran at 8.9% of 3★ reviews — the fastest-worsening dimension and the defect most likely costing renewals. Report 23: sync is the single largest reliability finding — 348 mentions (4.79%), 223 complaint-framed (3.07%, mean 3.08, 23.3% 1★), only 22 positive; the 2022 migration produced a spike (25 → 60 → 40 → 24 by year) with visible recoveries within weeks and a tail still visible in 2026 — a migration with a long, damaging tail; Germany 10.0%, Spain 10.1%, Sweden 9.7%. Report 25: cross-device sync not updating 14 (1.07%, mean 3.29), flat across eras. Report 27: sync that works but cannot be seen produces data-loss anxiety (4) and sync requests (3 — iPad; 'wish my goals were synced across my devices') in a corpus where the listing says iCloud sync already exists. Report 31: sync / backup / restore fails in 83 reviews ('Manual syncing is so 2010'); real-time iCloud sync across iPhone, iPad and Watch is requested with the iPad layout, concentrated in the 4★ band. Report 33: account-only (Firebase) sync replaced personal iCloud sync ('Original Habitify was able to sync … over personal iCloud. This has been removed'), with repeated logouts; sync failures 119 (3.02%), 7.9% of E4 — offer iCloud sync as an option alongside the account backend. Report 36: private sync is the resolution of the privacy-vs-sync tension — local-only praised ('not harvesting your data') while sync is the top request. Report 41: cross-device iCloud sync with no account is praised by 90 (11.04%) and fails for 13 (1.60%, mean 3.08) — four of them payers, because sync is the promise the app is bought on. Report 43: iCloud is simultaneously the advertised backup, an undismissable error banner ('iCloud Sign in Error - I can't turn off this message'; 'Constant iCloud Error… Sloppy code') and a backup that did not restore for a payer ('lost everything even though it was backed up to iCloud') — 5 reviews, mean 1.40, none after Aug 2022. Report 46: cross-device sync is a paid trigger ('I did upgrade so the data could be shown and updated on my watch') and a failure surface — sync 15 (mean 3.13), Watch and Mac disagreeing with the phone ('I paid a hefty price to sync with all my devices', subscriber 2★). Report 47: December 2019 sync hanging at 0% (7 reviews in 9 days); a crash loop after logging in to the free backup 6 (Feb 2024 – May 2025, log-out the workaround); registration / login failures 8, six of them from mainland China ('好像需要vpn'). Report 48: sync failure is the only reliability theme that never improved — 48 (1.09%, 2.65), flat at 11–13 per era since 2015, now the most common reliability complaint; the 2015 v3.0 sync rewrite shipped with crash-on-launch (29.55% of the era), duplicated trackers (20) and data loss (25). Report 52: sync is iCloud-only and fails across iPhone and iPad (147 reviews, 0.71%); reviewers ask for account-based sync (132). Report 55: partial, silent or 'only half' sync, a buried manual sync button; multi-device users pay for sync, open the iPad and see partial or no data — 'habitbull is a one device app only. And i have paid for pro. Unacceptable'. Report 56: 'the recent update about sync made my habits disappear, is there anyway I can get them back??' — six days after a sync request; F1: a local pre-sync snapshot and a visible restore path. Report 59 (Tappsk): BUG_SYNC 61 (5.71× among purchasers — sync is Premium-only) — 'На iphone не работает синхронизация'; the 2.6.2 release notes lead with 'iCloud sync more reliable'; a paid user lost everything and the account ('все записи удалились и больше не могу авторизоваться').

title: Crashes / launch failures
statement: Largest complaint by volume; a two-day launch crash produced more 1★ than years of minor bugs. Report 23: crashes 46 (0.63%, mean 2.80, 34.8% 1★) on three dated bugs — iPhone X freeze-on-close 2017–18, an iOS 14-era freeze, a stuck splash screen 2023–26 — plus Watch-app crashes on each watchOS generation. Report 24: crash / freeze / won't load 944 (2.17%, mean 2.367) — the recurring shape is freezing on the 'first mountain' / Journeys screen on day one. Report 25: a post-onboarding freeze — the main screen stops responding to touch — is the fastest-rising negative theme (51, 3.90%, mean 1.63; 1.3% → 2.9% → 5.8%; 27 of 34 E3 reports in May–Jul 2026; Colombia 18%, Germany 7.8%, GB 0%); iPhone 11 and iOS 26.x named, reinstalling does not fix it, one reviewer says it survived two updates; every one of these users got zero value. Report 26: crash/launch failure fell 3.37% (2021–22) → 0.13% (2024) after a visible engineering turnaround, then a 2026 cluster (n=4, three Russian, two paying — a premium subscriber crashing on the onboarding screen after reinstall) flagged for telemetry. Report 27: a September–November 2025 update-and-iOS-26 launch crash ('Ever since I updated to iOS 26 the app immediately crashes when I try to open') accounts for almost every bad rating the app ever received — all 4 1★, the only 2★ and 4 of 6 3★ fall in a five-week window (window mean 4.162 vs 4.822 elsewhere); fixed by Feb 2026 (mean 4.829, zero 1★); a solo-developer app with no support channel pays for an OS-transition break entirely in public rating. Report 28: launch failure / crash 15 (1.83%, mean 2.40) concentrated in 2022 (orange-screen failure), then a 2026 uptick ('freezing every time I open the app, I think it needs an update to keep up with ios') consistent with OS drift on a build last updated Nov 2025. Report 29: one 2026 launch failure ('Lässt sich nichtmal öffnen'); overall bug reporting fell by two-thirds (22.3% → 6.5%). Report 30: two launch-week crashes (Jul 2025, 'It just doesn't open… on iOS 18.5 and on the iOS 26 beta') and none in the following 13 months. Report 31: the app would not open in 1,052 reviews (20.29%, mean 1.30) in five waves — launch season 2016, intro freeze Oct–Dec 2021, v1.19.0 crash on launch 22 Dec 2021 → ~8 Jan 2022 (918 in the window), a post-update white-screen hang May–Jun 2022, freezes after subscribing 2022–23; devices from iPhone 6 to 12 Pro Max, so not an old-device issue; 1★ in E3 is 66.4% launch failures; the fix did not recur at scale. Report 33: an 11 Sep 2025 'Liquid glass' update crashed on launch on iOS 18 and was fixed in ~1–3 days with no lasting rating shift; in Oct–Nov 2019 Brazilian users could not open the app after purchase. Report 34: the 10–11 Apr 2024 update crashed on launch and was fixed a day later (E4 reliability 6.7% → E5 2.6%); in Feb 2026 a reviewer needed 20–30 launches to load. Report 42: a launch-blocking regression 4 Dec 2024 – 11 Jan 2025 — 7 'won't open' reviews (mean 1.71), 5 Russian inside 40 days, one a payer three months into an annual subscription ('Give my money back, crooks'). Report 43: crash / won't open is the largest single defect (20, 3.13%, mean 2.15; 18 of 20 US) with a persistent won't-open cluster Dec 2021 → Feb 2023 recurring Dec 2025 → Apr 2026; 'after purchasing, the app crashed every single time I opened it'; 'Crashes if you have less than 500MB free'. Report 47: crashes arrive as dated incidents — 19 crash reviews in January 2021 (10 of them attaching a photo, 9–24 Jan), a white screen when typing a custom habit name Oct 2020 → Jan 2024 (13, all JP, mean 1.54), 4 in January 2026 — 64 crash / cannot-open (10.87%, mean 2.84), 13 of 51 crash reviews still 5★. Report 48: two crash crises — iOS 8 / iPhone 6 (late 2014, crash on adding a tracker and on the back button, 20 reviews Sep–Dec 2014) and the v3.0 release (81 crash-on-launch reviews in 2015) — then a 2020 iOS 13 / 14 freeze (25 reviews) that vanished; the crash union fell from 37.3% of E2 to 2.9% of E5 — 'fixed, and stayed fixed… defended, not revisited'; crash / won't open is 23.3% of all 1★. Report 49: a launch-crash cluster (Oct 2024, 37.5% of the window), a 22 May 2025 update that stopped the app opening for users 20–39 days into a 66-day programme (37.8% of the fortnight), a June 2026 crash-on-task-completion wave (32.1% of the month); crash on launch fell 10.2% → 0.0% by E4 while unspecified bugs rose to 7.9% in the new game layer. Report 50: reliability flat and thin (21, 10.24%, no defect above 4 reviews in 31 months) — 'a well-built app and it has stayed well-built… the rating risk… cannot be engineered away'; 4 of 20 one-stars never used the product (crash, would not initialise, login failed). Report 52: crashes arrive in release waves — 175 of 412 crash reviews (42.5%) in six of 110 months (Jul 2018, Oct 2019, May 2023, Sep 2024, Apr 2025, Sep 2025), roughly every 12–18 months, three of them destroying data; a launch crash on iOS 14.x for 20+ days despite a stated iOS 14 floor. Report 53: crash waves at launch (Nov 2017, fixed within days), on iOS 11.3 and iOS 13, an app that quit on open for several days (Mar 2022), and the 2024–26 statistics-view crash (BUG_CRASH 133, 7.63%, 2.82). Report 55: four crash waves each tied to an update and concentrated in one storefront — Jul 2017 (all 12 UK), Jan 2018 purchase and registration (US), Nov 2018 iOS 12 (23 of 24 Brazil), Oct 2020 – Feb 2021 (26 of 30 UK) — BUG_CRASH 197 (9.73%, 2.04, 107 at 1★); the written-vs-public gap tracks incident exposure (gb 1.07★, br 1.18★ vs ca 0.30★, au 0.14★). Report 59 (Tappsk): four dated regression clusters in three years — 2021-10-22→25 an iOS-15-era update left iPhone 6/6+/7 on iOS 12–14 unable to open the app (33 crash reports in four days); 2023-06→10 completing a recurring task closed the app (trigger isolated by a reviewer to the 'show completed tasks' setting, build 2.5.397 named, 'no progress on this bug in three months'); 2023-08→12 the calendar opened on the same month of 2022; 2023-10 freezes after one action — the regression era carries the highest crash rate after launch (2.6%) and U_REGRESSION 296 'produced most of the product's 1–3★ reviews outside billing'; a launch-crash cluster in 2026-05; a locale-specific crash when setting a habit reminder appears almost only in Turkey (BUG_HABITS 19.99×, BUG_REMINDER 11.80×, BUG_CRASH 8.43×; 1–2★ 15.7% vs 5.9% global) with two Korean reports — test reminder flows under each locale. Report 60 (Mindway): only 2 of 216 (0.93%) report a crash, both within five days in 2024-10 and never again — consistent with one bad build; 'the product is barely reported as broken', which is what makes the monetization findings unambiguous. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): a 1–2 June 2026 build with broken hit-testing — taps did not register (six reviewers; one found that a swipe still worked) — produced 8 reviews in 39 hours across six storefronts (17.78% of the app's entire written history, 40% of all its 1★, −0.32 on the mean), caught a premium buyer and a $10 buyer one week after purchase, and blocked first-run habit creation ('I couldn't get past the start creating a habit step, the button won't press'); fixed within days (16 reviews from 3 Jun average 3.875, zero tap reports) but 'the regression is closed; the reviews it produced are not'. Report 64 (Critique AI): the one repeated defect is a freeze during AI plan generation (May 2025 and Apr 2026, independently), then on every launch for one reviewer; crashes on every AI review and on the coach tab 'after the update' ('I expect better from an app which costs like 30 dollars'). Report 65 (Rabit): stability union 73 (14.66%, mean 2.04) in release-tied waves — a first-run block (Jul 2021, 46.2% of its fortnight), a crash-on-launch wave (Apr–Nov 2022, eight of 13 from payers: 'Paguei o premium a toa, pq já tem mais de 7 dias que não consigo usar o app'); an unexplained crying-woman sound on every launch ('c'est effrayant') kept as an asset-integrity issue.

title: New Year peak-season robustness — year-end report and January onboarding
statement: The year-end report crashed five New Years in six; never ship risk or lock features in late December. The New Year cohort is the largest of the year and judges onboarding, not retention — every create-flow or first-day defect is amplified ~2× in January (reports 8, 9). The New Year cohort is the largest of the year and judges onboarding, not retention — every create-flow or first-day defect is amplified ~2× in January (reports 8, 9). Report 31: v1.19.0 shipped a crash on launch on 22 Dec 2021, into the New Year and a TikTok-driven install surge — 1,135 reviews in 25 days (21.89% of the corpus, 79.4% 1★, 51% non-US), 35% of lifetime 1★; 47 reviewers never got to use the app; collateral data loss ('Lost more than 2 years of data'); the 2022 mean of 1.74 is a release-engineering outcome — stage rollouts and freeze releases before acquisition or seasonal peaks. Report 58: the history view shows only 2026 and a reviewer worries 'I hope all of my 2026 is not removed' — the corpus ends 118 days before the app's first year boundary while 5 reviewers adopted it for unrestricted history; fix 1: verify and publicise year-rollover behaviour before 1 Jan 2027.

merged_from.title: Harden onboarding before January
merged_from.note: C146 (harden onboarding before January) is the same rule as C032 (never ship risk into late December) on a different surface

title: Restore purchase and entitlements must work immediately
statement: Charging and not delivering is the second-fastest route to 1★ (×13.9). Lifetime buyers told to subscribe, subscribers who cannot find their tier, premium members still upsold. Report 11: 3 of 3 paid reviewers lost purchased access — a lifetime non-consumable expired, a subscription re-locked after a week and reinstall did not restore, an active annual term was re-charged — and two titled their reviews 'scam' and 'Purchase fraud'. Report 12: 40% of self-identified payers reported that payment did not grant access (paywall re-appears, 'no subscription found', Restore Purchase redirecting to the privacy policy, HTTP 400 at login, re-purchase demanded on a new device) — rising to 12.6% of all 2025 reviews. Report 18: 25 entitlement failures (mean 2.44★; 9.94% of confirmed payers; every Japanese instance 1★) — lifetime buyers denied Pro, a PayPay lifetime never applied, a subscription active in iOS settings with premium unusable, and a lifetime holder whose entitlement was deleted when they cancelled an accidental annual plan. The worst case: a power cut reset a lifetime buyer to onboarding, wiped every routine, then demanded a subscription. Report 19: 5 of 105 paid and could not use the product — 'I can log in on my laptop but no apps'; iPhone login error 300 with no message while iPad worked; account access lost once cancellation was started. Report 20: legacy lifetime entitlements often did not survive a device change; restore-purchase failures (91, mean 1.59) recurred for years after the 2021 revocation, and 75.8% of them came from confirmed payers. Report 25: 'already paid, asked to pay again' — 8 reviews across a 16-month window (Mar 2025 → Jul 2026), including a lifetime purchase that restore does not recognise ('every time I enter the app it tells me to remove them or to buy the subscription to keep my habits'); emerging by rate, severe by kind, and the persistence argues against a one-off outage. Report 26: purchase lost or not delivered is the top paid-user failure (24, 0.63%; 12 of 72 explicit payers = 16.7%) by three mechanisms — the 2022 repricing withdrew a purchased unlock, restore-purchases fails or the button is dead, payment succeeded but premium never activated. Report 28: 10 of 24 identifiable payers (41.7%) report a purchase not delivered or not restorable — a $9.99 pack that never appeared with 'no Support button in the app. Nor on developer's website'; restore failing on a new device with the same account; a purchased cosmetic that reverted; consumables cannot be restored the way non-consumables can. Report 30: 'Списаны деньги за подписку, премиум функция не открылась' — charged with premium never unlocked — 'unambiguously a bug and should be treated as a P0 incident, not a review'; both billing failures are Russian, the only market with continuous purchase attempts. Report 31: 468 reviews (9.02%, mean 1.23; 304 explicit payers) say Premium they paid for was not granted — 2023 200, 2024 200 — including 295 'lifetime' buyers who stayed on Basic (mean 1.14, 89.5% 1★): the post-purchase 'gift' / Growth-Bundle screen appears to drop the entitlement when dismissed ('by not finishing this flow and purchasing the upsell, I think it doesn't recognize I purchased it'); one clean success ('I was successful at purchasing and using a lifetime premium upgrade') suggests a code-path defect that ran at least 16 months — make the entitlement grant atomic with the purchase and show any cross-sell after. Report 33: entitlement failure is small (69, 1.75%) and mostly portability — web (Paddle) purchases not unlocking the iPhone, a lifetime tied to one e-mail and paid twice, guest → account, a new or stolen phone, 18 days without activation, 6+ weeks and 20+ e-mails to resolve, a lifetime holder asked to subscribe on the Watch — plus a Jan 2018 wave (21, 11 in Japan) fixed within two weeks; the report asks for one entitlement per person recognised on every platform, with guest and account purchases merged automatically. Report 36: entitlements don't travel — skins 'unlocking them on each device'; a payer who cannot find out whether the subscription covers one device. Report 41: premium bought on iPhone never reached the iPad (2022) and premium intermittently reverted to free with Restore Purchases failing (2025) — 'a paying customer being shown a paywall is the most damaging possible bug'. Report 46: entitlement not recognised across devices or after a trial — 4 payers ('App does not recognize it… even after refreshing the subscription with the provided link'; '明明都在pad己開通高級版，Iphone上卻不給用'; one resolved only by refund and re-purchase); the report's #3 fix is one entitlement across iPhone, iPad, Watch, Mac and web with a visible subscription-status screen. Report 47: premium status reverted to free with ads reappearing (3 payers, January 2021); a 'purchase failed' loop on every open (Jul 2026); the report's fix #3 is entitlement recognition.
