Report 49: restore purchase fails 5 — every one a paying customer locked out of what they bought, all 1★ — 'the most severe five-review theme in the corpus'. Report 52: PAY_RESTORE 190 (0.92%, 2.61; payer lift ×3.21) — an iPhone membership not recognised on iPad, memberships lost after reinstall, and a reinstall path where restoring one's own data asks for a membership that does not restore. Report 53: PAY_RESTORE carries the highest payer lift (6.32); a lifetime buyer about to post a bait-and-switch review tapped Restore Purchase and 'the app went back to normal and no more pop ups' — so part of the 2026 legacy cluster is a restore failure the app could fix by restoring on launch (F2). Report 54: 'for a one-time-purchase product, restore-purchases is not a feature, it is the product's warranty' — 7 restore failures (every one 1★) across BR, ES, GR, TH, UA×2, US, 2021 → 2026, P3 rate 4.2% (five-fold rise), 6× more concentrated outside high-spend storefronts; F1: a visible, labelled Restore button — the single largest source of one-star reviews. Report 55: premium gone after a new phone or reinstall (PAY_RESTORE 18, 1.11, lift 10.22) because premium was tied to an e-mail account; F1: restore-purchase tied to Apple ID. Report 57: 8 restore failures, all from 2024 ('I changed phones and my Premium purchase is gone'; 'after reinstalling I get ads again'); 3 whose entitlement never applied; a July 2026 release (3.1.0) broke Premium activation and restore — 8 reviews in 5 days, six 1★, one still broken on 3.1.1, externally corroborated by the release notes. Report 59 (Tappsk): BUG_PURCHASE 142 (0.94%, 2.81★, 8.43× among purchasers) — 'оплачено 990руб за подписку, но работать в этой программе нельзя пока ещё 1499 руб не заплатите' (990 ₽ paid but you cannot work until you pay another 1,499 ₽); a lifetime unlock listed in the phone's subscriptions as 'for a year'; the fix: restore the lifetime unlock from any receipt, on any device, on the Mac, after a reinstall, with no annual charge in between. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'I paid for subscription monthly but still not working. Is this scam?' (BR, 1★) — two of six self-identified payers had an entitlement failure, 'the worst ratio in this report'; I2: audit the purchase-unlock path end to end, including a charged subscription that still behaves as free. Report 64 (Critique AI): paid but still gated — the paywall popup persists after purchase (age 15), restore fails ('I can't restore my purchase so basically I can't do anything now'), reinstall demands payment again, and a second device refuses login ('you have to pay for each device') — 4 of 13 payers (30.8%), 3 of 13 fully gated (23.1%) — 'converts a completed sale into a 1★ and a fraud accusation'; F4. Report 65 (Rabit): PAY_ENTITLE 9 (1.81%, mean 1.56) — 100% payers, Sep 2021 → Mar 2026: 'Fiz a assinatura do plano plus anual e o app não reconhece!'; a subscriber still capped at five habits; a buyer's to-do list locked; lifetime charged but 'O app consta como se eu não tivesse o pacote'; ads and 'upgrade to premium' prompts after paying; a new phone offered only a new plan; an account 'não existe' after reinstall; F2: audit fresh install, new device, reinstall and Android→iOS, and make Restore Purchases reachable. Report 67 (Habio): U_ACCESS_FAIL 97 (4.73%, mean 1.02) — cannot log in / email not found 52, paid but no premium or restore fails 43, purchased PDF not delivered 10; 'even i payed for subscription 350 kr but everything is locked'; §8.4: link web purchases to app accounts automatically.

title: Data must never be lost on update, reinstall or phone change
statement: Data loss is ×10.6 over-represented among buyers; local-only storage is the cause. Report 10: from 2025 the dominant story became app-initiated — 'it told me my pet data got corrupted' — with no automatic backup to fall back on. Report 14: data lost on update was the only theme with a perfect 1★ record and the corpus's only 'stay away' review; it recurred 5.5 years later ('backdate all my progress by memory (again)'). Report 18: data loss sat between 6% and 8% in every era after the first, five years running — the single most durable defect in a 2,048-review corpus — and hit 12.42% of confirmed payers; 'if I'd known records could all disappear I wouldn't have paid.' Report 20: update 1.41.0 (13 Mar 2025) erased habit histories globally — 126 of 161 reviews in the following seven weeks (78.3%) reported losing 2–5 years; the advertised fix did not work, a second bug wiped prior progress on the next check-off, iCloud backup was itself a paid, manual feature ('Why should a premium subscriber even have to think about whether a backup was created?'), and there was no communication. The same migration-bug class had fired in Jan 2021. Report 23: data loss 81 (1.11%, mean 2.17, 45.7% 1★), 60 of them after the 2022 sync rewrite (3.38% of post-2022 reviews, mean 2.03; 2024 peak 22) — the only theme that destroys a long-tenure customer outright ('my 3+ years record to null'; 'It's like I'm a brand new user'); an in-app backup existed and was discovered by support, not the user. Report 24: progress lost on device change with no restore (257, mean 2.693) is the most-cited reason a multi-year user stops. Report 25: data loss / reset to zero 12 (0.92%), flat ~1%; archive/delete destroys history (4) — 'archive losing history defeats the point of archiving'. Report 26: with no account or sync, a support-recommended reinstall deleted 'all the lovely growth you have achieved' along with the purchase. Report 27: the one observed churn — 'It doesnt open with the update, ive lost all my progress, guess its time for a new app' — is reliability plus data loss, not price. Report 28: 12 data/progress-loss reports (1.46%, mean 2.42) entangled with the game's intentional decay — 'on challenge mode… run out of health it resets ALL of your progress… level 278… resets you to level 1'; 'My Account is gone, I was at a high Level'; an intentional decay mechanic and an unintentional data-loss bug are indistinguishable to the user. Report 29: 9 data-loss reports (mean 2.11, the lowest-rated theme) came from the calendar bug plus a workaround users taught each other — reinstall — which wiped local-only history ('just sad I lost my data from uninstalling it'); 'the bug fix alone does not close this loop — an export or backup path does'. Report 31: data / streaks lost or reset in 94 reviews (a 109-day no-wine streak; sobriety 40 → 16 days; 200+ day streaks to 0); counts corrupted by v2.7.1/2.7.2 in 107 (58,720 — 'Do not download 2.7.2!!!'); a habit tracker's only durable asset is the user's history, which users treat as health data — gate releases on data-migration tests and stage every rollout. Report 33: v2.0 (Nov 2016) wiped history and Premium for many ('30 routines gone'); Habitify X erased 4 months of time logs; data lost 55 reviews (mean 2.25). Report 34: local-only storage lost data on reinstall, factory reset or 'for no reason' (4; 'thought this app supports iCloud sync and re-installed app … lost all data as this app needs backup file'). Report 36: 'everything you save and track is reset when the app is deleted … I do not recommend' (1★); DATALOSS 3 (mean 1.67); a new phone met the new cap ('5 habits on the old phone, 1 on the new'). Report 41: 6 data-loss reports (0.74%, mean 3.33) — 'After 215 days of tracking… everything… deleted, all history lost! No chance to restore'; 'deleted from BOTH old and new device' on migration; one recovered only by the developer by hand; a 6-month total loss filed at 5★. Report 42: data loss 6 (mean 1.33, acted on regardless of share) — 'last night it updated… All my data and tracking… is gone'; 'I had 90 days of progress on every habit, now it's all gone and became 9 days'; 'I used it for many years… After the last update progress isn't visible… looking for a replacement' — the update → restart → history-truncated pattern recurs, four of six Russian. Report 43: data loss is the most severe and accelerating defect — 12 (1.88%, mean 2.08), 0 in 2016–18 → 7 in 2022–26 (4.55%); in July 2026 two German users four days apart lost four years of locally stored history when the UI changed ('I used HabitHub for four years and after an update my locally stored data was gone'), got immediate support replies, and had already migrated — 'If I could change anything, I would sync my data to the iCloud to be sure'. Report 46: data loss 24 (1.10%, mean 2.12), doubling across halves and 8 from payers — checked squares, streaks and history silently rewritten ('marks from a couple of days or even a week ago disappear'; 'the results for habit one are somehow already displayed for habit three'; 'suddenly reset and lost all my data. What am I paying $29.99/year for'); all four 2026 cases from the Russian storefront in 23 days — 'for an app whose entire value is an unbroken visual record, silently rewritten history is the highest-severity failure possible'; the fix asked for is a per-habit change history with 'undo last 7 days' and conflict resolution that never deletes a completed mark. Report 47: data loss 16 (2.72%, mean 1.94), all Japanese, 8 of them in 3–20 August 2026 after an update — '7年間使った結果がこれ… アプリ更新したら勝手にデータ上書きされて今までの記録消えた' (seven years overwritten); '2022年から毎日つけていたトピックが消えていました'; '登録していたメアドに復旧のための確認メールは来ない' (no recovery mail); one user stopped writing memos because losing them hurts too much; the data-integrity union rose from 1.1% of reviews (2019–21) to 13.0% (2025–26) while crashes fell 13.8% → 4.8% — 'more stable to open and less trustworthy to rely on'; the report's fix #1: run it as an incident, restore server-side, guard sync against overwrite, ship a visible restore path. Report 48: data loss 58 (1.32%, 1.67), 25 in the 2015 sync rewrite; 36 of the 484 one-stars; Australia over-indexes (3.23%). Report 49: progress reset or lost 36 (14.15% of payers vs 2.92%) — an update or logout restarts a 66-day programme at day 1: 46 of 66 days lost, a 177-day streak lost, six accounts lost within 48 hours in June 2025 (window mean 1.92) — 'destroys the exact asset the product is selling'. Report 50: 'the app just pushed an update and erased all my data without any warning or options to save' (1★, May 2026); a Premium user's to-do entries lost and unrecoverable (Apr 2026) — no reviewer in 205 mentions a backup; fix F6: visible backup / restore and no destructive migrations. Report 52: DATA_LOSS 229 (1.11%, 2.73; 37.1% 1★) persistent every year; 56 tie loss to an update or crash — 'four years of to-do records all gone… I bought lifetime membership for this'; payers with data loss average 1.73. Report 55: 'now I lost my account including years worth of data' (BUG_DATA 35, mean 1.31); 'I'm a premium user and have already lost all my data twice' (br); reinstalling to escape a crash often wiped data. Report 56: a sync update deleted a user's habits (4★, the only severe defect) — the history is the asset outcome reviewers keep the app for. Report 57: 12 data-loss reports (8 since 2024, 6 at 1★) — 'today's update wiped all my previous data. If recovery is impossible, shouldn't you warn people before the update?'; 'I adjusted the count on one habit, saved, and every other habit's check-ins collapsed to one'. Report 59 (Tappsk): U_DATA_RISK 104 (0.69%) — 'но все мои задачи пропали' (all my tasks disappeared); 'Нигде не указано, что задачу надо обязательно сохранить' (nowhere does it say a task must be saved) — an unsaved-edit loss reads as data loss. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'After several months of usage all my habits disappeared upon app launch' (UA, 1★); a repeating last-week wipe on update (KZ) — two reviews (4.44%) promoted under the severe-data-loss rule. Report 65 (Rabit): 'it continuously wipes all my habits, tasks, everything and I have to start over. I have the paid version!'; 50 list items saved one by one and 'simplesmente sumiu tudo!'; 'não restaura o que tinha antes' (DATA_LOSS 10, mean 1.70; data_continuity 21, 4.22%).

title: Account system from day one
statement: Root cause of lost purchases, lost data and failed sync; requests rise as users change phones. Report 20: 'no account, no signup' was praised — and was the root cause of the 2025 data loss; the account/backup layer must exist even if signup stays optional. Report 26: no account system anywhere in the corpus — a device change, a reinstall, or support's own advice to reinstall destroys both progress and entitlement ('It also deletes the purchase price of the app if you bought it as there is no account to sign into'); absent accounts every other entitlement bug is unrecoverable — the root cause behind the top paid-user complaint. Report 27 (counter-evidence on the signup side, not the durability side): no account is praised — but iCloud sync exists and is invisible, so three reviewers fear data loss and one churned after an update lost progress; the account layer's job here is legible backup, not signup. Report 28: an account with e-mail verification exists (29 mentions, mean 3.66, mixed); a verification reset by support turned a 1★ into a 5★. Report 29 (counter-evidence): no account, no email, no login is named as the reason to choose the app; the report's rule is backup yes, account no — local-first. Report 33: guest mode is a data trap — 26 users who never created an account lost everything on update, reinstall or Mac sign-in ('Never use guest mode'; a ¥6,000 lifetime bought as a guest) — while forced login since 2016 is itself a privacy complaint. Report 36: no account at all; Chinese-market users ask for login specifically ('希望可以登陆', 17 helpful votes, third most-voted). Report 41 (counter-evidence): no account is praised (privacy / no account 10, all 5★: 'Pas de compte à créer, pas de données collectées'), and the report lists 'do not require an account' among what not to change. Report 43 (counter-evidence): no account required is listed among reasons to buy ('No subscription · Very reasonable one-time purchase price · Great data privacy (no data collected) · No ads'). Report 46: an account was required 2018–2022 (8 complaints, mean 1.50; the first review in the corpus could not sign up; login failures mean 1.89) and optional by 2024 — the complaint stopped when the requirement did. Report 48 (counter-evidence on mandatory accounts): forcing an account and online sync on a local tracker in Jan 2015 drew 39 reviews at mean 1.64 — 'a privacy objection, distinct from price' — strongest in Germany (5.04%, the largest over-index of any theme in any storefront; one review invokes German consumer law); iCloud sync later replaced the account; login / account failures 21 (1.86). Report 50 (counter-evidence): a mandatory account limited to Sign in with Apple or Google before first use lost two GB users at the gate — 'Why would I want to expose every aspect of my life to data mining in this way? Stay clear.' and 'unable to login with apple' — 'a conversion risk and a single point of failure'; S6: consider a local-first trial mode. Report 52: WeChat login cannot be bound on the Mac build for five years (12 reviews, among the most-upvoted) and QQ vs WeChat logins split Android and iOS memberships. Report 55: an optional account (e-mail, Facebook; later Apple, Google) whose January 2018 registration spinner, 'email invalid' and reset e-mails that never arrive (ACCT_BUG 57, 1.68; US 34 of 57) broke premium; F6: registration optional and robust, never block first use. Report 58: no account and no e-mail sign-up named as adoption reasons by 2 ('It makes it quick and easy to start using').

title: A support channel that exists, is reachable outside the app, and answers
statement: 'No support channel' is ×34.7 over-represented among buyers and the second-worst-rated complaint. Report 5: the only support link was inside an app that would not launch; email went unanswered while public review replies were same-day. Report 10: AI and canned support replies; paying users 13× over-represented among support complaints. Report 11: 'there is no way in app to talk with developer or team' — with no support queue, billing bugs were filed as public 1★ fraud accusations instead. Report 12: five reviewers said the listed support email does not exist; refund and support failures were twice as prevalent in small storefronts, where users are charged and stranded. Report 18: support silence (32, mean 2.72★) landed hardest on payers — a week of silence on a lifetime account with purchase screenshots; the Japanese in-app feedback form rejected every valid e-mail and its text was invisible in dark mode, so Japanese users could only file bugs through the App Store; KakaoTalk was the only Korean channel and closed at weekends; a Canadian found the in-app support link resolved to an ad. Report 20: support went from answering reviews and fixing bugs same-day in 2019–2020 to a dead 'Contact Us' e-mail with an autoresponder and a dormant Instagram account (0.05% → 13.0% of reviews by era); among 148 support-silence reviews the mean was 1.33 versus 3.63 for the 30 who were restored or fixed — the same defect produced either rating depending only on whether anyone answered, worth ~+2.3 stars per recoverable incident. Report 23: support praised (49, 0.67%) with fixes bringing edited upgrades, but genuine silences recur and one reviewer says support implied they don't own an Apple Watch for testing. Report 24: 947 (2.18%, mean 1.528) automated-only support; the refund path works when reached — several 1★ → 4★ edits after a refund — so the failure is reaching it. Report 25: a solo developer answering within a day ('feature requests implemented in less than 24hrs'; 'I can't believe one developer made this') is a purchase trigger — 'After testing the app and interacting with the developer… I've decided to pay without any hesitation' — but support praise thinned 3.0% → 1.6% → 0.9% and one 1★ says the developer 'preferred to argue about what I could see on my end'. Report 26: support unreachable 13 (mean 2.77), support praised 10 (all 5★); support's own advice to reinstall destroyed a paying user's progress and purchase; a premium subscriber's crash went unanswered for months. Report 27: not one review in four years mentions contacting support or a developer reply; the website link in Settings leads to an inactive domain, so the support path is broken — and a solo-developer app with no support channel absorbs an OS-transition break entirely through its public rating. Report 28: 'There is no Support button in the app. Nor on developer's website'; 'no matter how many emails you send, they don't reply'; yet the four who reached the developer got excellent service — a 1★ converted to 5★ after a verification reset 'within an hour… on a Sunday, on a 3 day holiday weekend'; support quality is not the problem, discoverability is — an in-app 'Contact support' and 'Restore purchases' entry point is the cheapest rating intervention available. Report 29: support effectively unreachable — 'I contacted the dev twice but got no response'; a support link that 'takes you to a super-sketch website, circumventing Apple's privacy settings'; with no account and no backup the review page is the only support channel, which is why bugs arrive as public 1★. Report 31: 460 reviews (8.87%, mean 1.32) say support never replied or the contact path was broken (dead typeform links, a Mail-app-only link), rising 0.6% (E1) → 20.3% (E4) → 20.8% (E5); in E1 support was praised (11 of 18 support-praise reviews) — staff a single working contact path with a published response time and resolve by receipt, not by argument. Report 33: support is two-sided — praised 103 (mean 4.73; 'Hana … sent me a video'; 'within one minute') vs support failure 131 (1.70; 5 weeks without reply then the review deleted); English-only replies frustrate Japanese and Chinese users; AI-only support is an emerging negative (8 reviews, 7 in 2025–26: 'Their support is AI'; the chatbot 'stops answering'). Report 34: a single 'Support doesn't respond to emails' in an app whose main asset is a named, responsive solo developer. Report 36: both support-failure records are payers ('contacted the developer twice … I waited too long for a reply and I have now paid. Service matters'; 'a small company and cannot solve problems in mainland China'). Report 41: the only support channel is a mailto: link that dead-ends users without the Mail app ('forcing me to add a mail account'; a trial user 'likely will cancel'), in an app where support closes sales and is the only data-recovery path; support praise collapsed to 1.7% in 2025 as volume tripled, then recovered. Report 42: a paying customer with data loss had no route to a human — 'it says mail isn't connected, but there's no section in the app to connect it' — and replies are canned ('they just reply the same thing to everyone', a 10-vote review). Report 43: support is bimodal because the intake is broken — praised by 24 (mean 4.67; a 2★ raised to 5★ after the exact fix shipped; 'requested a small new feature… added a few days later') vs 7 with no response (mean 1.29, the lowest theme) and 4 reporting the in-app feedback form itself fails ('Feedback email can not send'; 'They have a report bug feature, but that also doesn't work'); 'no response' rose 0.57% → 2.60% by era while praise stayed flat. Report 46: 7 unanswered (mean 1.57; 'sent 3 different email… Not a single reply'), four of them 2024–26 and two paying customers with unresolved data loss or an unrecognised subscription; support praise 53 (4.94) is falling 4.30% → 1.82% as volume grew. Report 47: no findable support route — unresponsive 7 (mean 2.57): '問い合わせ先もわからない'; 'サポートサイトにも窓口がない'; a feedback form that crashes; account-deletion messages unanswered — while 12 reviews (mean 4.42) acknowledge a fix: the gap is the channel, not responsiveness. Report 48: support is reachable only inside the app, so users whose app will not open have no route — 14 reviews (1.08% of 2022–26 and growing) are 1★ reviews written as support tickets, nine from payers; the report's fix #3: publish a support e-mail on the website and the listing; separately 29 got no response (1.55). Report 49: 'contact support' is not a button (3), App Support resolves to a 404, multi-day silence — 21 unreachable (1.43), 10 of them payers; when support does answer it is outstanding (9 at 4.89 — a refund plus a free year) — 'The capability exists; the routing and the staffing do not.' Report 50: in-app support chat praised by 8 (5.00) and developer responsiveness by 11 (4.91) — 17 unique; one negative ('sometimes customer service give is not very caring'); support re-sent a lost discount offer and closed the sale — 'an asset to protect… not a cost centre to optimise'. Report 52: support silence rises with each crash wave (SUP_BAD 184, 2.33; payers ×4.53 at 1.92) across e-mail, WeChat, Weibo and Xiaohongshu; a support address that bounces; fast fixes are among the strongest praise (SUP_GOOD 148 at 4.93: a purchase crash fixed the next day, a request shipped within days). Report 53: support went from praised to silent — SUP_GOOD 31 (4.71) all Nov 2017 → Mar 2022 (a proactive follow-up, an icon idea shipped in days, VoiceOver added on request) and SUP_BAD 64 (1.58), 41 in 2023–26; the in-app contact needed a configured Mail account and later 'the support email it opens does not send'; payers with silent support average 1.17; F4: a contact that works without Mail, an auto-acknowledgement and a known-issues note. Report 54: support unresponsive 6 (1.50), rising to 4.2% of 2023–26; 'Your support pages and email are down' (GR, Aug 2026); 'there's no app support to write any of this to… which I feel like should be a thing if you have to pay for an app'. Report 55: support silence from Jan 2016 to Apr 2026 (SUP_BAD 83, 1.45, 66 at 1★; payer lift 6.21) — a developer site returning errors, a contact form that won't send, ticket numbers with no reply, canned answers; 'will update my review based upon their response'. Report 56: four in-review support questions (data recovery, widget transparency in Korean, language reset, back-dating) left unanswered, each answerable in one sentence. Report 57: Korean users write support tickets in the review box — 50 direct questions to the developer (49 Korean, 8.10% vs 0.57%), mostly 5★ about existing features; support praised 2019–24 for fast KakaoTalk replies ('got a reply the moment 9am hit') then silent ('they just read it and never replied. What a waste of money'); 'the support link goes to some Asian industrial company'; the in-app bug-report form crashes on Submit; F6: a support link and FAQ where users are already asking. Report 59 (Tappsk): reviewers praise Telegram and condemn e-mail — 'пишу на почту уже 2 раза, ответа нет' (e-mailed twice, no reply); 'На почту пишешь не отвечают, в тг пишешь бот' (e-mail unanswered; on Telegram you get a bot); SUP_NONE 64 (6.09× among purchasers), SUP_CONTACT 31, both more frequent in the latest eras; fix: route billing and sync tickets to the channel that answers and acknowledge bug reports with a status. Report 60 (Mindway): seven reviewers (3.24%, mean 1.43) used a 1★ public review as a help desk — 'the absence of a visible support path', six of the seven about money; the one who tried the proper route ('asked this question of the developer and awaiting the reply') rated 3★ where the other six went straight to 1★ — 'the one payer who found a support route rated the app two stars higher than the ones who didn't'; F3: put an in-app support route in front of the review prompt, and answer it — seven support tickets became permanent public 1★ reviews. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): no reviewer — including three paying customers with a broken app — reports contacting the developer; the reviews are the support channel by default. Report 64 (Critique AI): three 1★ reviews are unanswered, resolvable tickets — a parent's three emails on a login issue got one 'please clarify' then silence ('My son was so excited to use this app, but now it's just taking up space'); billing; a frozen paid app — F5: 'low rate, 100% conversion to 1★'. Report 65 (Rabit): SUP_SILENT 5 — every one 1★ and every one a payer ('Mandei dois e-mails solicitando o estorno da compra, mas até o momento não deram retorno'; 'ninguém responde… Um descaso total!') — each a problem one reply would have converted; F3: 'the cheapest rating repair available'. Report 67 (Habio): U_SUPPORT_FAIL 425 (20.72%, mean 1.04) — no reply 213, slow 78, templated 59, evasive 46; 'Funny how when it's public your response is timely'; retention questions in reply to cancellation requests; 37.7% of reviewers whose money left their account report a support failure.

title: Family plan
statement: Demand exists (people bought it); report 1's failed only through discoverability (Apple Family Sharing with no in-app affordance). Report 23: Family Sharing is supported on the one-time purchase; a few want to track a child's chores alongside their own inside one account. Report 33: a paid family plan (2025) whose sharing is described as not working (7, mean 2.00). Report 46: no Family Sharing — 'for that, €29 a year is too expensive' (DE, 1★); 'too expensive to have 5 subscriptions so my entire family could use the tool'; the report: offer it on annual and lifetime. Report 53: the listing claimed Family Sharing that the in-app purchases did not support (PAY_FAMILY 8; refund requests in kr). Report 57: Family Sharing advertised on the listing and not working for a buyer ('I do not think it is right that they lie', MX). Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_FAMILY_SHARE 13; 'написано, что поддерживается семейный доступ' (it says Family Sharing is supported) is a paid-twice complaint.

title: Dates, streaks and statistics correct on every surface — month boundaries, week starts, DST and timezones
statement: Miscounts are ×10.2 over-represented among buyers. Off-by-one dates across app/widget/Watch were report 2's longest-lived bug. Night routines that cross midnight must log to the day they started, honouring a user 'day ends at' setting. Report 23: un-pausing a task marks paused days as missed and resets the streak; a completion 'un-completes' seconds later under sync conflict. Report 25: over-achievement carries into the next day (exceeding a goal pre-completes tomorrow) and logging a bad habit at 200% is rewarded as success (7, 0.53%). Report 29: a month-rollover and weekday-header-offset bug was the dominant defect — 37 reviews (10.11%, mean 2.95 vs 4.73), 78.4% filed on days 28–3 against a 27.6% baseline ('On the last day of every month the app has no idea what day it is… April 30 defaulted to Feb 28'); 62.5% of all 3★; users taught each other to reinstall, which wiped local-only data. Test every date surface at month end, leap day and both week starts. Report 31: time-zone travel rewrote 600- and 1,500-day streaks (13); the week-start setting was ignored and weeks reset on Sunday, including in widgets (30; a 3-year premium user 'begging'); store completions against the local calendar day, not a UTC timestamp. Report 47: calendar weekdays off by one day for reviewers outside the Japan / Korea time zone — 14 (2.38%), 13 from China, Italy, France, Spain and Australia, 2019 → April 2021 ('4 January 2021 is a Monday and it says Tuesday'; 'it lost 29 February'); habit order scrambling (5, 2022), counts displayed wrong (5, 2025–26), late-night check-ins leaving a gap (fixed); a Sunday week start added on request. Report 48: timezone / date bugs 26 (3.35, 2014–22); wrong counts / stats 85 (2.59) across every era; day-boundary 2. Report 49: the day counter advances wrongly — 20 reviews, flat Oct 2024 – Jun 2026, never fixed; the daily recap closes scoring at a fixed ~9pm (10). Report 54: the paid calendar rings show the wrong completion — two reviewers on two continents tie it to the long-press undo not propagating to the calendar (9, 2.56, 5 payers). Report 55: 'not more than' goals saved as 'at least' — inverting success for quit-smoking and drinking goals ('Smoke not more than 10 cigarettes… they actually show as requiring you to do the task at least that many times'); streaks reset at the year change in 2018 and 2020; editing a frequency rewrites history; a traveller's completions shift days; a July 2020 update marked taps on the wrong day. Report 56: 'the calendar is a day out so when you complete a dot on the Monday it highlights the Sunday before' (GB, rated 5★) — F2: verify week-start and timezone handling (Europe/London vs UTC feed); the UI switched to Chinese unprompted. Report 57: 'Display on' per-weekday filter shipped and silently ignores selections for 8 users over five years ('I set Tue/Thu/Sat and it shows every day'). Report 65 (Rabit): completed habits reported as missed — 'Tengo un hábito cumplido todos los días y mi planta sale muerta y con 0 días de racha' (BUG_STREAK 7, mean 2.43); week start offered only as Friday or Saturday, never Monday (3); a calendar mapping dates to the wrong weekday; F7, F9.

merged_from.title: Date arithmetic must survive month boundaries and week-start conventions
merged_from.note: C243 (report 29: a month-rollover / weekday-offset bug) is a specific failure of C038's rule, not a separate decision

title: Reminders fire reliably, once
statement: Reminders that work are a top praise item; not firing or spamming is a 1★ driver. Report 23: 97 (1.33%, mean 3.48, 18.6% 1★) — reminders that don't fire (Thailand 4 of 22, 18.2%, limited evidence), fire for already-completed tasks, fire all at once at night, ignore Do Not Disturb, or interrupt a meditation to say meditate; the 'smart' auto-timing algorithm is widely disliked. Report 24: notification volume/control 744 (1.71%, mean 2.437) — users turn all notifications off, which disables the product; give per-notification-type control. Report 27: the reminder fires for a goal already marked complete today — 'a notification that contradicts app state actively trains users to ignore notifications'. Report 28: notification annoyance 5 (0.61%, mean 2.80) — decay-guilt pushes ('YOUR BUNNY'S LOSING HEALTH'). Report 29: reminders that never fire, deleted reminders that keep firing (surviving delete-and-reinstall), and changed times that don't take (6, mean 3.17) — one problem: the notification schedule is written once and never reconciled against the habit's state; cancel scheduled notifications on delete and stop the day's reminders on check-off. Report 30: a user wants an alarm, not just a notification — 'receives an alarm from the app itself and doesn't need another alarm on the phone'. Report 33: reminders praised by 91 (repeat every 30 min until done) and broken in 68, notably when iOS 13 broke notifications. Report 34: the reminder time picker broke for a paying user ('I payed for this app … I might just cancel my membership', Dec 2025) and again Mar 2026; a 2019 buyer got no notifications and returned the purchase. Report 43: an iOS 15 notification regression ran five public weeks (13 Oct – 10 Nov 2021: firing after completion, double notifications, 'I don't think the solution is to have us individually email tech support. It's clearly a bug'; a payer 'over a month and a half… no bug fix'); ghost habits — deleted habits still firing at midnight after reinstall and a new phone (2); notification bugs 15 (2.35%, mean 2.60) on the app's signature feature. Report 46: a deleted habit's notification kept firing (the most-voted review in the corpus, 25 votes); reminders not firing 7; finer reminder control (per day, stop once done) requested by 9. Report 47: reminder time-setting buggy Jan–Feb 2021; non-scheduled weekdays notified until fixed by June 2026 — notification bugs 11 (1.87%). Report 48: notification bugs 78 (1.77%, 2.64) at a stable ratio against 224 reminder praise; notification overload 12 (2.33). Report 52: reminders were why people installed (and in 2017 what they reviewed to unlock), so REM_FAIL carries a 3.62× payer lift — silent mode kills the sound, reminders keep firing after the habit is done (23 votes), archived habits still remind, changed sounds revert. Report 53: in an app named HabitMinder reminders are tied to a time-of-day section, not a clock time — an evening habit reminds at 8 am ('the only reminder that can be set is for 8am'), a 30-reminder list hits iOS's scheduled-notification cap so some habits are never reminded, and reminders fire for habits already done (REM_CONTROL 56, 2.88; REM_ANNOY 28; REM_FAIL 13). Report 54: notification defects — no badge, nagging after completion, wrong sound (6, 2.50). Report 55: medication reminders that fail; push instead of sound-only in silent mode. Report 59 (Tappsk): BUG_REMINDER 96 (0.63%, 2.78★) in every era — 'unless you open the app every other day, the reminders you set will stop working'; 'за весь день дай бог словить хотя бы 2 уведомления' (lucky to catch two notifications a day); PR_REMINDERS 401 shows the same feature is a top praise when it works. Report 65 (Rabit): the ledger's clearest reminder regression — REM_FAIL 66 (13.25%, mean 2.91), 10.8% of launch-era reviews, 0.8% for the next 25 months, then 45.7% of everything written from Nov 2023 to Sep 2026 and still open at the last review; 14 reviewers (2.81%) report the app is absent from iOS Settings → Notifications altogether, across iPhone and iPad, seven storefronts and five languages, after reinstalls — 'almost certainly a missing or failing UNUserNotificationCenter authorization request'; 'Qual o sentido de fazer um app de habitos e nao ter notificação?'; 15 of 66 are 4★ and 9 are 5★; REM_GOOD (a perfect 5.00) fell 8.1% → 0.8%; the loop a reviewer described — cue (notification), routine, reward (the tree) — loses its first step; three abandoned lifetime / subscription purchases, 10 of 49 payers, three refunds; F1: confirm the authorization request on a current device before anything else.

title: Widgets must not go blank, stale or disagree with the app
statement: Broken widget is ×7.8 on 2★. Report 10: the widget rendered as a grey box for five years (117 reviews) — reported mostly by fans, so it never generated pressure. Report 18: the widget went from the top request (31 reviews at 4.77★ before launch) to the top defect surface (214 mentions, 10.45%) — blank, missing from the picker, wrong weekday, false 'all done', check-off opening the app, routine widget rendering to-dos. Report 20: the widget was the top defect surface for five years and the 2★ band's peak theme (13.0%). Report 23: widgets rendering blank or losing configuration (57 explicit widget-bug reviews, mean 3.16; 20 blank/config reports) alongside the interactive-widget regression. Report 25: widget stopped working / not interactive / font fixed (6, 0.46%). Report 27: the widget is the most consistently under-delivering surface and the only one to produce a 1★ on its own ('Widget does and shows absolutely nothing… Just says 0% ALL the time'); 9 gap/defect reviews (6.52%, high-priority) across every one of five years vs 5 praising it. Report 28: no widget at all — 14 requests (1.71%), mean 4.64, zero negative ratings, continuous April 2022 → September 2026, 'i want to be able to click on the widget and shortcut to check a habit as done'; the clearest uncontested gap in the corpus. Report 29: no widget at all — 16 requests (4.37%), the only absent feature with demonstrated substitution (a user on 'Check Me' because it has one) and the one explicit payment offer ('add widget support happy to pay for a lifetime'); three withhold a star for it. Report 30: the Home Screen widget is paywalled and a documented switch followed — 'I downloaded it only for the widget. Turned out it's a paid feature… competitors include it free — I went there'; the widget shown in the store screenshots is not the widget the app provides; the one user who has it is the happiest reviewer. Report 31: widget mentions 195 (3.76%) — positive in E1, demand in E2, complaint after the Oct 2021 downgrade; the widget ignored the week-start setting. Report 34: widget rendering broke with the iOS 18 tinted home screen (white), two of six widgets didn't show days, 'keeps getting disabled' — 5 reviews, 3.0% of E4, one payer 'waste money'. Report 46: widgets blank, stale or wrong — 21 (mean 3.33): 'I deleted the Dry January task but the widget still shows it'; 'every day the home-screen widget colour blocks get scrambled'; 'The widget is the heart of the application' (1★ after contact); interactive widgets also record accidental taps ('marks the completion of that day by mistake… Not great for a paid app') — the report: keep it, add a lock / view-only mode. Report 47: the 2025 widget gets stuck at 0 or goes blank (5, all 2025–26: 'ある日突然ウィジェットがずっと0表示になってしまいました'); the report's fix #2 pairs it with wrong month-view counts. Report 49: the same blank / stuck-on-day-1 widget reported in Mar 2025, May 2025, Nov 2025, Dec 2025 and the final week of the corpus (8). Report 50: widget lag (1, 5★). Report 52: widget defects 454 (2.20%), 62.8% in 2020–21; a widget renders blank on iOS 26 Clear / Tinted home screens. Report 53: widgets blank on tinted home screens and no longer interactive on iOS 18/26 (WIDGET_BUG 5.1% of 2025, 7.5% of 2026). Report 56: a widget tap that opens the app instead of progressing the habit (BE, 4★). Report 57: the widget is both the most-loved feature and the largest defect surface — 129 (16.56%) raise a problem: 50 won't appear or go blank (rising 3.89% → 6.67% → 10.80% by era), 25 don't reflect check-ins, 9 show a live group as 'deleted' (Apr 2024 – Dec 2025), 6 clip items; 58 of 90 defect reviews are 4–5★; 'every single update breaks the widget'; 'I have to reinstall five or six times a month'; 23 of 99 payers affected; a Premium payer considering switching over three widget layouts. Report 58: widget habit icons render as white boxes in iOS clear / tinted icon mode — the only functional defect in 91 reviews, with a stated repro. Report 59 (Tappsk): BUG_WIDGET 100 (0.66%) — widgets blank or stale after updates and not changing at day change ('при переключении дня задачи на виджете не меняются'; 'каждый раз обещают направить разработчикам, но проблема остается' — each time they promise to pass it on, the problem remains); fix: widgets that refresh at day change without opening the app; the 2.6.2 release notes list 'faster widgets'. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): the widget is the paid hook, so its gaps are voiced by the highest-LTV buyer — no dark theme, 'so basic' — from a lifetime purchaser.

title: Editing a habit never wipes its history
statement: Multi-year bug; fixing it brought reviewers back to raise their rating. Report 25: archiving or deleting a habit destroys its history (4); preserve history through archive and restore. Report 30: the only way to stop a finished habit is to delete it, which destroys its history.

title: Aim at ADHD / neurodivergent users, students, medication & chronic-illness trackers
statement: Highest-fit, highest-satisfaction audiences (ADHD 7% of US at 4.79; students 4.87). Report 10: 7.36% of 70,041 reviewers self-identify as ADHD/autistic/ND; Australia's base is 11.4%. Report 18: ADHD/ASD/depression/burnout reviewers were the highest-rated audience (36 at 4.53★; 5.95% of US reviews) and the developer put 'ADHD' in the Korean store title — but the same population is most damaged by streak mechanics and excluded by a 9-to-5 onboarding; the positioning ran ahead of the product. Report 23: self-identified ADHD/autism/executive-dysfunction users are a growing, high-satisfaction segment (73, 1.00%, mean 4.45; 0.66% → 0.70% → 1.90% across eras) the app never marketed to; 28 arrived on a therapist/coach/doctor recommendation (mean 4.50); several of them are the strongest capacity complaints because task decomposition is what executive-function support requires, and one calls the help-page wording ableist. Report 24: ADHD/autism/executive-dysfunction users are 933 (2.15%) and grew 30× across eras to 6.01% of 2024–26 reviews — but they are the angriest segment (mean 2.747, 54.2% 1–2★) because the interface overstimulates and the cancel flow exploits executive function; depression/anxiety/PTSD/grief context is 1,256 (2.89%, mean 3.938); clinicians review it and recommend it (24 + 9). Report 25: ADHD/autism/OCD self-identified users are the highest-satisfaction segment (41, 3.13%, mean 4.44, 32 5★; plus 24 at mean 4.67 describing executive difficulty without a diagnosis; three arrive via a clinician including a psychologist recommending it to clients) — and they supply the sharpest paywall anger ('just another app trying to profit off of your disability'); ADHD vocabulary is 4.8× more common in high-spend markets, a diagnosis-prevalence difference not a needs difference. Report 26: ADHD/neurodivergent users (81, 2.11%, mean 3.84 — the lowest of any positively-framed segment) succeed because of simplicity and are hit hardest by the 5-habit cap; mental-health users (32, mean 4.66) are the highest-affect reviews; teens and students (25, ages 10–21, mean 4.16) cannot pay. Report 28: ADHD/autism users (15, mean 4.33) say the reward loop 'works so well for my brain' — and produce the harshest ad verdicts ('whenever I click to complete a habit, it shows me an advert'; 'Bad for ADHD — Has Potential'): interruption cost is not evenly distributed; kids and students are 40 (4.87%), several aged 8–10. Report 31: ADHD / autism / OCD users 33 (mean 4.09 — 'every other app overcomplicates… this app is BEAUTIFUL and simple'), medication and body-care tracking 36 (3.42), mental-health context 38; coaches, clinicians and therapists recommend it — they are the most loyal and the most hurt by regressions (monthly frequency, streak display, medication streaks). Report 33: ADHD, neurodivergent and health users praise the structure ('as an adult with ADHD'; 'I'm neurodivergent and I really hate routine'; medication) and object most clearly to guilt copy and unclosable banners ('I have adhd … huge banner … you CAN NOT CLOSE'). Report 34: ADHD users (5) prefer the simple general tracker — 'apps designed specifically for ADHD … too detailed … This app is simple with just the right amount of detail'; 'MUST. FILL. BOXES.' Report 43: ADHD (18, mean 4.61) and other accessibility accounts (12, 4.75; autism, depression, chronic illness, head injury, ASD, anxiety) are the fastest-growing theme (0.00% → 4.22% → 7.79% by era) and almost entirely US (24 of 25) — 'severe ADHD… complete tasks that would otherwise take hours on end — cooking, cleaning, and even applying makeup'; 'motivated me to shower for the first time in a week'; 'when I don't have the brain power to think it just tells me what to do next'; the mechanics are the multi-step timer and the widget; the listing's 'ADHD-friendly interface' claim is earned without targeting. Report 46: neurodivergent and chronically ill users (30, mean 4.83, 23 US, growing 0.54% → 1.70%) name the forgiving skip ('one off day doesn't kill your streak'; 'neutral data instead of a personal failing'), the widget ('if I don't see something I forget it exists') and minimal input ('a simple yes/no input, which is perfect for me and my ADHD because I've quickly become burnt out by decision fatigue on other apps'; 'Literally 3 click options'). Report 47: study / learning users 9 (mean 4.78; 'ピアノ練習100日目'), neuro / focus 2; fitness / diet 24 (4.08; a high-schooler's diet log with 14 votes). Report 48: ADHD is the lowest-rated segment (13, mean 3.77) in a corpus where every other segment averages 4.6+; students 24, mental health 23 (4.78), health / medical 24. Report 50: ADHD users 7 (3.41%, 4.29; 5 US at 4.80 — 'ADHD life saver ❤️'; 'the best app to help me with my crazy ADHD'; 'ADD/ADHD/OCD me Loves You!!!'); the one 1★ is an ADHD user whose household tasks no longer fit in 3 free habits; mental health 4 (5.00 — depression, bipolar 1, memory loss, low mood). Report 52: medication and chronic-illness logging named in reminder praise (an IVF medication schedule; a chronic-illness patient agitated by ads); the ADHD subtitle has only 6 supporting reviews (0.03%) in a 20,634-review Chinese corpus. Report 53: medication, stroke, bariatric care, alcohol recovery and brain-injury users ('I haven't missed a dose since I started using this app') — a small set of older, disabled or recovering users most exposed to confusing billing. Report 54: 7 self-identified ADHD, autistic or anxious reviewers all at 4–5★ discovered the fit themselves though the subtitle names ADHD; 'with my adhd, once it's closed i never use it' (widget). Report 56: one ADHD reviewer — 'tried countless apps that claim to help neurodivergent people… They end up being made for quick cash grabs or having a wildly confusing interface… With Dots, you get exactly what you download' — the report advises earning the audience by staying simple, not claiming it (n=1). Report 57: two US ADHD reviewers disagree — one left over the ad at first setup, one calls colour coding and views 'amazingly functional for my ADHD'; a medication user asked for multiple stamps per day in 2019. Report 58: 8 of 91 self-identify as ADHD or neurodivergent, unprompted, across 6 storefronts, all 5★, 5 tying it to simplicity ('ADHD HEAVEN… Not overwhelming or complicated… my brain is happy'; 'Setting up is simple. No extras') while the listing does not target ADHD — 'produced by users, not by marketing'; one wants more celebration for dopamine. Report 59 (Tappsk): 'As an ADHD person'; 'keeps me together with my bad ADHD'; 'Я очень забывчивая, и это приложение буквально спасает меня' (very forgetful; this app literally saves me) — OUT_MEMORY 326 (2.15%), USE_HEALTH distinctive in the US (6.89×) and UK (8.76×), OUT_MEMORY in France (3.34×) and Sweden (5.01×); these users are the most exposed to the missing task time; students (USE_STUDY 90 — 'made a student's life five times easier') and managers (USE_WORK 163 — 'the flow of tasks is endless') are the other named contexts. Report 60 (Mindway): an app named for ADHD — 4 of 216 (1.85%) mention it, 3 praise the fit at 5.00 with zero ADHD-related complaints, across US, TR and CH: 'This app helps me a lot since I was suffering from ADHD from my childhood. It helps me organize my day'; 'As someone with ADHD. This helps me stay on task instead of getting distracted'; 'Parfait pour un TDAH'; and 'I don't think I have ADHD but it really helps' — the positioning reaching beyond its target rather than narrowing the market; D4: commit to the ADHD positioning and say so in the listing — the only differentiated claim the corpus supports and one Reminders / Notes / Calendar cannot match. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): an Arabic reviewer became consistent with morning adhkār, dhikr and daily Qur'an reading ('even if just a page') and advises others to include remembrance of God in their habit — a religious-practice use case the 'Atomic Goals & Accountability' positioning does not address, already running 3+ habits, i.e. over the free cap. Report 65 (Rabit): subtitled 'ADHD Help' but only 2 of 498 reviewers name ADHD or autism — one ADHD user: 'Esse App é tudo que eu sempre quis', one autistic user uncomfortable with the icon; medication adherence and depression use cases rely on reminders that stopped firing; §9.4: re-examine the positioning before spending further on it. Report 67 (Habio): the ADHD audience the ads target is the most harmed segment (97, mean 1.25) and finds the product 'way too overwhelming' for ADHD; §8.9: a short path to the first tracked habit, skippable pop-ups, the quiz after first value.

title: Flexible / custom frequency
statement: Every X days, specific weekdays, bi-weekly, quarterly, yearly, total-over-a-window — the #1 unmet functional need and highest 4★ lift. Report 12: weekday-only repeats were asked for in Jul 2022 and still missing in May 2026 — three years and ten months. Report 20: frequency was 'N times in M days' only — specific weekdays ('Gym Mon/Wed/Fri') were never expressible in seven years (22 requests) and drove a share of the notification complaints. Report 23: times-per-week, per-day, per-month and every-N-days shipped incrementally; still absent after eleven years — yearly goals, arbitrary intervals (every 6 weeks, quarterly, a shift worker's 4–5-day rotation) and specific dates of the month (101 requests, 1.39%); a non-daily habit also consumes a daily slot under the cap. Report 24: per-weekday / shift-work scheduling requested by 31, 51.6% of them 4–5★. Report 25: flexible scheduling primitives are a stated reason to choose the app — an every-N-days reminder ('the ONLY APP I've found'), N×/week, skip, vacation mode, a custom day-start for shift workers (capped at 11:45); a weekly habit cannot be pinned to a chosen day. Report 26: flexible recurrence ('3× per week') and a vacation/pause mode ('exception periods' while travelling) requested by 12 (0.31%); only per-habit day-of-week scheduling exists. Report 27: flexible weekly frequency shipped ~2025 and is praised ('tasks that can be completed a few times a week rather than everyday'); per-weekday scheduling ('run 1 mile per day during the week, and skip Saturday + Sunday') remains a request; a Monday week-start setting was asked twice in early 2024 and never again. Report 28: a weekly-target-only model — monthly, every-other-week, multiple-times-per-day and specific-weekday scheduling requested by 15 (1.83%), one explicitly blocking a purchase: 'I can't see myself purchasing without being able to make these distinctions'. Report 29: weekday checkboxes only — x times per week without naming days ('practice golf 3 times a week but it doesn't matter on which days'), every other week ('My off days Fri, Sat, Sun every other week… its frustrating' — the only feature-driven 1★), monthly and custom intervals (14, 3.83%) — the one structural gap persisting across all five half-years. Report 30: non-daily scheduling (days of week, x per week, weekly, monthly) is the only feature gap with multi-market evidence — 4 storefronts, 4 languages — and the only build item the report supports. Report 31: 'N times per period' with no fixed days is praised by 81 (a monthly view prevents 'feel bad' spirals); removing monthly and yearly frequencies (Dec 2022 – Jan 2023) drew 58 requests still arriving in 2026 ('This was the ONE reason I used to love this app'; contact lenses monthly, weight loss yearly; 'call friend once a month or take a vacation three times a year'; deep-clean the oven monthly). Report 33: 'N times a week' and every-N-days frequency are named differentiators (flexible scheduling praised 79, mean 4.80); 'N per week' was removed in Habitify X and restored; monthly nth-weekday and end dates are still requested (82; haircut, bills on the 15th, can't end a 30-day challenge). Report 34: x-days-per-week added on request (Apr 2019), flexible frequency praised by 13 (mean 4.92); every-other-day and monthly targets still requested (7). Report 36: flexible schedules (every N days, N×/week or month) requested by 7 in E1–E3 and not since Dec 2024 (probably addressed); habits shown on unscheduled days (3, all 4–5★). Report 41: 'X times per week, any days' / 'every N days' (13) and seeing which day a weekly habit was done (9) — one request asked twice, every year 2021–2026, 8 of 13 at 4★: 'I would like the option of doing something 3 times a week, not necessarily on the same day'; the app models which-days and how-many-times as alternatives. Report 42: setting which days, dates and repetition is Premium ('task repetition is paid-plan only', JP 1★); 'Tue & Thu' and shifting a habit to another day requested. Report 43: scheduling flexibility is the longest-running unaddressed request (29, 4.55%, mean 3.38; Jan 2017 → Jan 2025) — intervals beyond one month ('Wish I'd known that before I paid for it'), Nth weekday ('1st Tuesday of each month'), 'X times per week' without fixed days, every other week, a due date rolling from last completion; a redesign regression made 'every 2/3 weeks' habits show every week. Report 46: every-N-days, X-per-week without fixed days and monthly schedules are the longest-running functional request (34, mean 4.09, every era Sep 2019 → Jul 2026) — 'a medicine I must use every other day and I can't put it on this app'; a shift worker on trial calling it 'potentially a deal breaker'; 'most of my habit are repeated every 3 days… Apple reminders is WAY more efficient' (churned). Report 47: X-per-week and monthly habits requested by 8 (mean 4.12) — absent, and a 5★ requester withdrew the request to protect simplicity. Report 48: arbitrary cadences such as every-other-day requested by 35 (3.97); weekday scheduling — weekly goals that still demand a daily answer — 21 (3.57). Report 50: 'at least N per week' goals missing (2, 5.00 — a weekly goal marked complete at Mon–Thu cannot record Friday and Sunday); every-other-day, future start date and 15-minute increments requested (4). Report 52: monthly, every-other-day and N-per-week rules (299); weekly-N habits spoil a '100% day'. Report 53: '3 times a week, any day', every other day, a day of the month (CORE_FREQ 54, 3.76); a 3×/week habit fails Monday and Tuesday and support's Skip 'skips that task for the week'; '2 times weekly' must be done twice in one day. Report 54: 'X times a week without naming the days' — 24 (6.50%, 3.79); two call the scheduling model 'unusable' ('I don't care or know when those days will be but this app makes you designate them'; shift workers, DE). Report 55: 'You set your own standards (every day, certain days a week, or a number of days in a week/month)… it doesn't disqualify you if you don't do each habit every single day' (CORE_FLEX 148, 4.82 — the named differentiator); gaps: weekly totals, monthly periods, custom week start, optional end dates. Report 56: non-daily scheduling is the oldest request (day one) and the only one with a rating penalty — the corpus's only 3★: 'Great daily but no weekly… I love the daily tracking for free with no premium version, but I feel like we need a weekly/monthly/select days option!'; five of six forms reduce to 'this habit is not daily' (x per week, weekly, monthly, select days); a deadline request is a different product (D1). Report 57: every-N-days, monthly, yearly and month-end scheduling requested (7). Report 58: times per day, per weekday ('only make habits show up on specific days for my gym sessions'), biweekly and monthly — 4 reviewers, 4 storefronts, one gap in a weekly-goal model. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_HABIT_OPTIONS 113 (0.74%) and REQ_RECURRENCE 51 — habit scheduling and count options are a steady request beside REQ_CUSTOMIZE 234, the largest single request (80 of the 4★ reviews). Report 60 (Mindway): recurrence limited to daily / weekly / monthly is the largest functional request — R_REPEAT_OPTIONS 3 and R_CUSTOM_TASKS 4 of only 10 requests: 'I don't need to flip my mattress every month, but that's the only option I'm given'; hourly hydration, every 2 weeks, every 6 months, haircuts; plus fixed 28/38-day programme pacing the user cannot control ('neden tüm planları kendimiz hemen o gün yapamıyoruz'); D5: fix the recurrence model before adding anything else — four of ten requesters ask for flexibility in different words. Report 65 (Rabit): CORE_FREQ 9 (1.81%, mean 4.11), all Brazilian over five years — 'Preciso estudar música 3x por semana (0/3)… (1/3), (2/3) e (3/3)'; 'minha rotina não permite sempre me exercitar nos mesmo dias'; 'Sem isso a assinatura não vale a pena' (a conditional purchase); with skip, partial multi-per-day, reset time and week start, 15 reviews (3.01%) describe one model limitation — fixed weekdays; S2; research: why only Brazilians ask.

title: Mac / desktop / web app
statement: Strongest 3★ driver; users volunteer to pay extra for it. Report 23: the Mac app was a separate purchase in 2020–21, then included in the universal purchase from late 2021 (≥8 reviews, a classifier miss at 1); one unverified report of the Mac app creating millions of files and locking the user out. Report 25: a Mac app is part of the included platform surface (8 mentions, mean 4.00). Report 27: a macOS app requested once, 5★. Report 31: iPad / Mac / landscape / web / Android wanted by 98 (1.89%, mean 3.49), peaking in the 4★ band (7.5%) and in E1 (5.3%), falling to ~1% after 2021 as those users left. Report 33: a Mac app (sold separately in 2018), a menu-bar mini app, web, Android and Windows exist; the Mac app could not sign in or sync through 2021–22 (Mac/web 18.5% of 2022, Russia 10.1%) until macOS 13.0.1. Report 34: no iPad / Mac / web app (8) — 'The only reason i'm going with a competitor … is because I don't always want to use my phone'; 'I'd even pay for separate versions as long as they synced'. Report 43: a macOS / desktop app requested by 3 (mean 4.67); the listing claims Mac (M1+) — possibly discoverability. Report 46: a web app and Chrome new-tab extension pre-dated the iPhone app and held the early community ('I have it as my default Chrome tab page'; 'I am not allowed my phone at work'), fading 2.15% → 0.23%; the Mac build is criticised as slow. Report 48: a Mac app from ~March 2022 was welcomed by long-term users and lifted multi-platform praise to 3.13%; the web app (2015 – ~2019) was discontinued and its removal is still resented — 17 want it or Android back (0.84% of 2022–26), Windows users in particular lost access. Report 49: iPad and Mac builds exist but layouts are broken (device incompatibility 15, mean 1.27). Report 50: Mac and iPad companion with one account (praised). Report 52: a Mac build exists but cannot bind the WeChat account the membership lives on. Report 55: no Mac or web app (PLATFORM_WANT 24). Report 57: Mac requested by 8 (all Korean). Report 59 (Tappsk): U_PLATFORM_REQ 385 (2.54%) — REQ_DESKTOP 208, REQ_WEB 104, REQ_ANDROID 28; desktop requests fall from 6.0% of the launch year to 0.6% after the Mac app and hold near 1% since, shifting to Windows and the browser ('Сделайте версию для ПК на WINDOWS 10'; 'нужна веб версия, товарищи'); the report's experiment is a read-mostly web view priced into Premium to test demand before a full client; REQ_WATCH fell from 4.7% to 0.0% after the Watch app shipped.

title: Grouping / folders / categories / tags
statement: #2 feature request in report 1; the highest-mean request in report 3 (zero 1–2★, power users tracking 20–100 counters); named in report 8's only subscription-price statement. Report 20: categories/folders (58) and a compact row option (26) co-occur — both are what happens when a power user exceeds ~8 habits. Report 23: extra capacity is wanted for time-of-day pages (morning / work / evening / bedtime) and life-domain segmentation (health / work / relationships / creative). Report 25: groups and sub-groups are a praised paid feature (customisation 65, mean 4.49); group creation reported locked on free. Report 26: per-habit gardens or categories requested (18). Report 27: tags exist but existing tags cannot be selected and duplicates don't group — two storefronts, two months apart, same bug, both cost stars. Report 31: groups/categories (added Mar 2018) were paid and valued by buyers; forced daily/weekly grouping and order resets in v3.0 (22) drew complaints. Report 33: areas / folders (Dec 2019) are free and mixed (31). Report 41: lists / tags with per-list rings and widget filtering (2022). Report 46: folders / habit groups shipped Aug 2025 after 10 requests ('The new habit folder feature is — chef's kiss'). Report 48: tags / filters / a Today list are premium; requested by 26 (4.12). Report 50: journal notes filterable by activity or category. Report 53: 'so close to perfect… ability to group activities' (4★). Report 56: separate lists / habit groups requested once. Report 58: user-defined sections requested once — test as an opt-in invisible until the first section is created. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_PROJECTS 33, REQ_TAGS 24, REQ_CHECKLIST 21; PR_LISTS 185 and hidden lists (books, films, shopping) 29 are praised. Report 60 (Mindway): 'There is no folder system. I can't categorize my reminders' (one 3★ request). Report 65 (Rabit): routine grouping caps at two even for subscribers, or duplicates habits and empties tabs.

title: Shortcuts / Siri / URL scheme / API
statement: Power users who evangelise. Report 23: Siri Shortcuts, URL actions and NFC triggers are a power-user favourite (72, 0.99%, mean 3.94). Report 25: Siri Shortcuts exist; a Mac app and formerly Vision Pro; Shortcuts gaps 1. Report 31: Siri Shortcuts were removed in the Mar 2022 rebuild and automations broke (14). Report 33: x-callback / Shortcuts, Zapier / IFTTT, a public API, calendar sync and NFC habits serve power users (47, rising to 2.5% of E5; API 'unbeatable'; 'Pairs nicely with agentic workflows'); Siri Shortcuts broke in Habitify X. Report 41: Siri Shortcuts with near-full app control praised by 36 ('I was able to automate 80% of habits tracking'); public API / Zapier / IFTTT requested by 5. Report 43: Siri / Shortcuts praised by 5 (all US); one asks for Shortcuts integration. Report 48: Siri Shortcuts praised (17 with Health); an API or IFTTT / Zapier automation requested by 11 (4.18). Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_INTEGRATIONS 57 (Siri, Reminders, Health), REQ_CALENDAR_SYNC 56, REQ_NOTIF_ACTIONS 28, REQ_QUICK_ACTIONS 21.

title: Cumulative totals and total-days counter
statement: '47 hours read this year'; total days instead of consecutive to reduce streak anxiety. Report 47: totals and statistics requested by 11 (mean 4.55); cumulative total shipped by 2025; a payer wants average and total study time. Report 50: stats praised by 23 (4.83) — weekly / monthly / yearly reports, grid map, success percentage, 'consistency (not only streaks)'; payers name statistics depth as the value. Report 53: totals and trends in units, not only completion % — 'a total of 1000 push ups'; a 7-hour sleep against an 8-hour goal shows 0% (R6).

title: Flexible units / partial progress
statement: Drag to 60% instead of a binary tick — a named reason for choosing over competitors. Report 23: 77 reviews (1.06%) in seven languages ask to record effort beyond the goal or short of it — over-achievement is discarded ('goal 30 minutes, read 90, it stops at 30') and partial progress renders as failure ('6 of 8 glasses shows an ✗'); the two most-upvoted reviews in the 7,270-review corpus (313 and 126 votes) are this request; 'do 30 push-ups' breaks on a 25 day where 'push-ups per day' would record 25 and preserve momentum. Ship floor-without-ceiling goals and a partial-progress calendar state without changing the streak rule. Report 25: measurement units — count, minutes, distance, custom steps — and track-only habits with no goal number. Report 29: quantity/unit tracking (steps, litres, reps; one proposes a slider) requested by 4 — only as an optional habit type outside the default flow. Report 31: unit tracking with custom increments (dollar amounts for business referrals) is praised; a custom-count input bug added an extra unit ('I type in 50 pages … it counts 55', 16). Report 33: goals with units and multiple check-ins per day shipped in Aug 2020; custom units (kg, kcal, metric) and icons still requested (56). Report 34: quantity / partial completion requested by 11 — 'I Drank 80oz … I wanna be able to track that'; '8 of 10 glasses counts as progress'. Report 36: multiple completions per day / quantity targets (water in ounces) requested by 5. Report 43: multiple completions per day with 0/2, 0/4 counters (water, reps) exist free and are a purchase trigger ('the 0/2, 0/4 etc feature that visually shows you how far behind you are… it made me buy it'); praised by 14 (mean 4.71). Report 46: several completions per day (12) and numeric targets — glasses, steps, pages (9, mean 4.56) — requested. Report 48: numeric Target and rolling Average trackers are the reason 485 reviewers chose the app; flexible units requested by 13 and true time-duration HH:MM by 8 — see [[C265]]. Report 53: US units only for water, weight and distance ('Stuck with Dopey American units'; 'In Europe we have no idea what a US Fl Oz is!'; notifications in ounces with litres selected — DES_UNITS 47, 20 storefronts); log beyond the goal (CORE_OVER 10). Report 55: numeric habits with 'at least', 'exactly' or 'not more than' success rules alongside yes/no — 'counting habits like 8 glasses of water a day'. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'store a value or note per day (walked 5k, then 7k) and see it over time' (ZA, 4★) — the same data-model change as within-day counting (P5).

title: Mood tracker
statement: Meaningful praise where shipped; mentions rose after launch (report 1); asked for only by 5★ users (report 8); an automatic mood prompt is a memory aid and moving it behind a button destroyed users' mood datasets (report 10). Report 24: a daily mood check-in exists inside the routine app. Report 25: a Russian lifetime buyer with ADHD proposes a mood/energy tracker so the statistics screen can answer why a habit failed. Report 28: a mood tracker with limited free moods (paid moods 10 complaints, mean 3.90; mood entry mandatory on open 2); journal/mood used by 38 (4.63%, mean 4.29). Report 33: a mood log (Aug 2021) with multiple moods per day as Premium — 14 mentions, mixed. Report 41: mood tracking added via Apple Health (Sep 2024, 'I'm very happy to see mood tracking added'); 5 wanted it inside the app's own history. Report 50: a mood tracker and body-weight tracker bundled in. Report 58: themed mood, gratitude and day-rating logging proposed in a 1,030-character review. Report 65 (Rabit): a mood / feelings diary and wellness prompts (REQ_MOOD 3, mean 5.00).

title: One-off to-dos alongside habits
statement: Emerging request. Report 18: routines and one-off to-dos interleaved in one time-ordered list was a named purchase trigger and 'MyRoutine's one advantage' over to-do apps; to-do parity (carry-over, subtasks, tags, priority, undated, recurring) was requested ~30 times. Report 25: one-off, non-repeating tasks in a separate list or tab requested by 10 (7 of them 4★) alongside the time-of-day request. Report 28: a to-do checklist exists separately from habits and users want it to earn carrots (9, mean 4.44 — 'the more irksome and time consuming tasks that you procrastinate on'). Report 31: one-off tasks / today-only items requested by 28 (mean 2.86). Report 33: one-off tasks requested by 10. Report 50: tasks / to-dos and 'Lista' sections alongside habits (requested May 2024, shipped); the list section reported broken (MX, Aug 2026). Report 52: to-dos (小事) shipped ~2024 and rose to 3.0% of that year's reviews — welcomed, then sorting and hiding regressions. Report 59 (Tappsk): the strongest evidence yet for the hybrid — a daily to-do list with a habit row on the same screen is what 15,176 reviewers praise: PR_ALLINONE 293 (1.93%), PR_HABITS 445, and the most-voted review in the corpus (156 votes) is 'Задачи и привычки в одном приложении - гениально' (tasks and habits in one app — genius); switchers come from Notes/Reminders, Todoist, Trello, Notion and Things. The to-do half brings its own design decisions: today / tomorrow / this week / later buckets (PR_SECTIONS 134, PR_ONE_SCREEN 82; Germany praises the one screen at 8.92×), automatic carry-over of unfinished tasks (PR_AUTO_CARRY 69 — 'all your unfinished today's tasks move to tomorrow') which the report says to keep as the default but with a per-task opt-out because recurring tasks carrying over is unwanted by 28 and recurring tasks invisible on future dates by 32; and the missing event time ([[C276]]). Report 65 (Rabit): a separately paid to-do list — 'só o todo-list que não é [gratuito], achei meio injusto' — that vanished for a payer and has no reminders ('die sinnlose Aufgabenliste ohne Erinnerungsfunktion… Total sinnfrei').

title: Android version
statement: Requested; cross-platform continuity matters to switchers. Report 26: Android asked about repeatedly (CN, FR, SE). Report 31: Android and web appear in the 98 platform requests. Report 47: an Android version exists; Apple ↔ Samsung sync is why some users chose it and why 2022 sync failures hurt. Report 52: Android build exists but membership, price and login differ (PLAT_ANDROID 195, 3.53). Report 57: Android requested by 13 (all Korean) — 'please release this on Play Store so Galaxy users can use it too'. Report 65 (Rabit): an Android build exists but cannot restore to iPhone.

title: Points / rewards / wish list
statement: Weak request; one proposes a cash-stake mode. Report 48: gamified rewards requested by 17 (4.47); the 2013–14 points system drew 10 complaints and was dropped. Report 52: 光芒值 'sunshine points' earned per check-in and exchanged for self-set wishes — 312 (1.51%, 4.65), rising from under 1% before 2021 to 1.9–3.1% after; praised as a way to delay spending and curb impulse buying; requests for separate point currencies and for multi-check habits to earn points. Report 58: points redeemable for self-chosen real-world rewards requested once.

title: Custom time-of-day segments
statement: Beyond morning/afternoon/evening — shift workers. Report 23: one page per time of day — morning, work, evening, bedtime — is the top reason people ask for more capacity. Report 33: time-of-day sections (morning / afternoon / evening / anytime) are a named differentiator — 'no other app does as well'; 'the best thing about Habitify' — and paired with flexible frequency form 'a winning core'; a hidden time-of-day filter also produced false bug reports. Report 54: time-of-day grouping named as a differentiator by 10 (2.71%).

title: Never run incentivised / review-for-premium campaigns
statement: Bought rank and a fake average, 0.86% purchase signal, reputational backlash, unreadable data. Report 26: a review-for-cosmetic-unlock reward produced reviewers who volunteer they have not used the app; the ≤25-char 5★ tier doubled to ~35% of the corpus. Report 33: review solicitation — a founder-named 5★ burst (12 Oct – 1 Nov 2018: 110 reviews at mean 4.64 vs 3.30 before), 'a strange email … asking for a rating', a free-lifetime link after reviewing, contests awarding Premium, and a CEO asking for 5★ — 'Who the hell is peter?'; the burst left no durable effect and the report's last cheapest win is to stop it. Report 34: a free-lifetime giveaway (~29 Jun 2023) produced 27 short, mostly 5★ reviews in three days (55.6% ≤ 25 characters) and moved the mean by ~0.01. Report 42: six US 5★ reviews in three days (Aug 2020) with 13–30 helpful votes each and nonsense titles ('Hgfgg', 'Bdbdbd'), and eleven of Canada's twelve reviews 5★ generic praise in 13 days (May 2021) — 17 reviews (8.25%) that inflate the mean from 2.968 to 3.136 and leave Canada unmeasurable. Report 43: a launch-week burst of 13 seeded 5★ reviews inside 24 minutes moved a ten-year corpus by 0.02. Report 46: an aggressive in-app rating prompt produced 297 reviews (13.64%) in 44 days in May–June 2023 at mean 4.58 vs 4.29 — permitted by Apple, not fake, but it tripled volume with contentless 5★, diluted every later negative rate and 'made the post-2023 corpus less informative per review'; 17 reviews say they are writing only to make it stop. Report 52: a 2017 review-to-unlock gate (reminders unlocked by writing a review, with a length check) produced 462 unlock reviews, 427 in 2017, all 15 busiest days of nine years, keyboard-mash filler and 5★ reviews reading 'please stop forcing people to write reviews' — the launch year is unusable as a baseline.

title: Never gate or delete reviews
statement: Users catch it and call it a ToS violation. Report 33: one unverified claim that the developer deleted a review after 5 weeks without support.

title: Don't build AI features on demand grounds
statement: 0.011% demand; users ask for the opposite. Report 23: exactly one review mentions the 'Break It Down' AI feature (May 2026) — and asks for it to be removed. Report 24: an AI chat/coach bubble added ~2025 is an unwanted addition for long-tenure users, and AI-generated art/copy is the worst-rated non-billing theme (64, mean 1.156, 90.6% 1★) — the theme did not exist before 2024. Report 28: zero of 821 reviews request AI features; the only AI mention is a complaint about AI homework-cheating ads served inside the app — 'no evidence of AI demand in this audience'. Report 33: AI 'smart fill' and AI / chatbot support (2025–26) drew mostly negative reviews — 'Stop shoving AI everywhere'. Report 34: across 743 reviews over eight years, no review mentions AI, ChatGPT or an AI feature. Report 36: exactly one review mentions AI — as a substitute after uninstalling over the cap ('doing it with AI daily tasks until I find an alternative'). Report 41: Apple Intelligence habit suggestions shipped (Sep 2025) drew one light positive ('I like the apple AI to help with ideas'), while 'an AI coach' is on the report's do-not-add list. Report 46: 'I'm really sick of apps with a million features and AI just to convolute things' (Apr 2026, 5★). Report 47 (counter-evidence): an AI coach replying to each check-in is the first premium feature reviewers praise unprompted (13, mean 4.69) — see [[C263]]; the objections are silent stops and a toggle bug, not the feature. Report 64 (Critique AI): the AI is the brand ('AI Coach' in the name) and 'among people who used it, the weakest part' — 19 AI reviews at mean 2.21 vs outcomes 4.92 and gamification 4.00; a paying 5★ splits the product: 'for the AI plan? No. For speaking coaching and challenges to improve overall? Yes'; the substitute named for the AI half is ChatGPT / Grok / Gemini. Report 65 (Rabit): zero AI mentions in 498 reviews spanning 2020–2026 — 'worth knowing before assuming AI features are table stakes in this category'.

title: Offer a non-pastel / premium design option
statement: Recurring critique from men and users wanting a premium look. Report 25: native Apple design language reads as premium — ''Apple' design all over it'. Report 26: reviewers convert on beauty within minutes of install ('I bought premium within the first couple minutes of downloading'; 'as soon as I saw the visuals and music I bought premium') — aesthetic is the mechanism, not decoration, and 'It's not just an app it's a piece of art'. Report 29: UI/visual design praised by 45 (12.30%, mean 4.64); a font complaint (1); more colours / custom colours requested (4). Report 48: 62 call the UI dated (3.63, rising to 1.68% of E5) while 14 praise its plainness ('does not include "cute" graphics') — the report: do not redesign for novelty; the tap-count lesson is the larger risk.

title: Discovery runs through social video, Reddit, therapists (US) and Xiaohongshu / Bilibili (CN)
statement: Plan marketing around where users say they found the app. Report 10: 381 reviews involve a clinician recommending the app; two clinicians publicly withdrew the recommendation over data loss. Report 19 (negative case): paid Instagram/YouTube ads → web quiz → web checkout → a checklist; six reviewers named the channel and the funnel, not the software, generated the corpus. Report 23: therapists and psychologists recommending it to ADHD clients (28, mean 4.50), Atomic Habits and habit literature (14, mean 4.79), podcasts and blogs (Daring Fireball, MacBreak Weekly, Do By Friday, Diary of a CEO; 12, mean ~4.6); Apple editorial / Design Award traffic was the worst channel (17, mean 2.53). Report 24: acquisition runs through Instagram / Facebook / X ads into a web questionnaire; credibility signals (Duke/Stanford framing, Atomic Habits adjacency) and 'the trial produced a result in days' are the conversion stories. Report 25: Instagram / TikTok / Reels ads are a stated acquisition channel for buyers; three arrive via a clinician. Report 31: TikTok / Instagram / YouTube / press named by 117 (mean 1.72), 81 of 98 TikTok mentions in 2022 — the channel that brought the largest audience arrived during a launch crash. Report 34: launched via Reddit (Jul 2018); 6 reviewers (mean 5.00) say they found it via Reddit, social or reviews; early Reddit adopters wrote long, personal reviews to the developer by name. Report 36: an App Store Awards / Apple Design Award feature drove discovery at launch (Jun 2022); a professional coach prescribes the app to clients. Report 55: a Reddit launch post with the developer answering in the thread produced 21 reviews on day two (4.71 for 2015), and BuzzFeed plus a TV review produced 105 in January 2016 (4.77); a Korean rapper's recommendation in 2019–20; therapists and a clinical psychologist recommend it to clients. Report 57: the only AI-discovery attribution in the corpus — 'I found it by asking GPT to recommend an app with the features I wanted' (KR, 2025); Korean word of mouth (24 advocacy). Report 58: founder TikTok is the only named channel — 8 of 91 ('I saw the creator talking about her app on TikTok'; 'thanks to that tik tok girl'), no reviewer names search, friends or ads; single-channel, founder-dependent acquisition that also inflates the mean via audience selection; attribution fell 13.3% → 4.3% between halves. Report 59 (Tappsk): Russian-language acquisition — the founder's vc.ru article (MKT_PRESS 13), bloggers (MKT_BLOGGER 19: 'посмотрел видео у Маргулана'; 'я смотрела тик ток'), word of mouth (MKT_WOM 41), ads only 9.

title: Be visibly responsive; fixes bring reviewers back
statement: Users who see their bug fixed return to raise their rating. Report 18: the developer shipped what users asked for — widget, Watch, dark mode, bundles, timer, routine modes — roughly 18–36 months after the request, often breaking something else in the same release; six reviewers raised their rating after a developer reply, and one returning churned subscriber wrote '神✨'.
