Report 65 (Rabit): written 3.677 vs public 4.76 (−1.08; −0.30 Vietnam to −2.10 Portugal) — 'both are correct, and the store number is the better estimate of average satisfaction while this report is the better guide to what is broken'; six 5★ reviews carry price complaints or crash reports — here stars under-report dissatisfaction; non-Brazilian reviewers left faster over the 2023 changes. Report 67 (Habio): corpus mean 2.35 vs US public 4.28 (3,932), gb 3.68, ca 4.04, au 3.71, fr 3.05, de 2.65, mx 3.31, es 2.93; 'the complaint does not depend on the market' — non-seeded means near 1★ everywhere, only the mechanism varies (workbook gb / es, language bait fr / de, cancellation and support au / de); the US is two corpora (555 of 886 flagged; non-seeded US 1.35).

merged_from.old_title: Audit the sales funnel per market — the same product can rate 4.3 in one storefront and 2.1 in another on billing alone
merged_from.note: reports 59, 60 and 62 attached three kinds of evidence beyond the original per-storefront rating split: removing one storefront (RU) removes billing complaints but not praise (59); a US-vs-rest split that is a funnel-stage split — bought-and-disappointed vs stopped-at-the-door (60); and written-vs-public gaps of up to −3.56 stars per storefront with a 5★ band that is 17.6% non-endorsements (62) — the point is now about what the review channel measures, not only about one billing-driven rating gap

title: Payment retries are bounded — daily dunning against a declined card reads as fraud to the customer and their bank
statement: Report 24: 584 duplicate/repeated-charge reports (1.34%, mean 1.134), 117 describing daily or near-daily retry attempts, and 123 whose bank flagged or blocked the merchant as fraud; a same-day retry loop is indistinguishable from theft from the customer's side. Report 59 (Tappsk): 'После отмены подписки приложение каждый раз пытается списать с карты средства' (after cancelling, the app keeps trying to charge the card) — off-store billing retries after cancellation and after deletion; the fix is to stop retries after deletion.

title: Content the user paid for is saveable and replayable — a library, not a stream
statement: Report 24: long-tenure paying users cannot save or re-listen to the morning coaching piece — 'the main reason, every year, I seriously consider whether or not I will even renew'; journal entries cannot be revisited; background music was removed. Missing this is a stated renewal factor for the app's best customers.

title: Statistics stay readable on the free tier — gating the progress view removes the motivation loop the category sells
statement: Report 25: statistics of any kind were paywalled in every era and the calendar view by 2026 ('Pay to even look at calendar'); the reviews that name it average 1.40 and one explains why — for someone at rock bottom, free statistics are the motivation; gating it removes the reason to upgrade rather than creating one. The report predicts, counter-intuitively, that free statistics increase conversion and proposes the A/B. Sits beside C011 (paid weekly/monthly/yearly reports): the basic progress view is free, the deep report is the paid layer. Report 31: statistics (145 mentions) and charts were a paid unlock and a purchase trigger in the one-time era. Report 46: statistics free; richer stats requested by 11. Report 60 (Mindway): the paid product has no progress view at all — 'thought this would give more feedback on completion percentage - tracking consistency. It's just a basic to do list'; 'very little flexibility or encouragement'; no reviewer in 216 describes a streak, chart, score or progress view; D3: build the tracking layer — 'the largest non-pricing gap in the report' and the capability that justifies a subscription because it cannot be replicated in Notes (E4: completion %, current streak, 30-day grid).

title: A first-run failure escape hatch — skip setup / continue offline, with a visible error state
statement: Report 25: 51 reviews (3.90%, mean 1.63; 1.3% → 5.8% across eras) describe the app freezing on or just after onboarding with the main screen unresponsive to touch; four say reinstalling does not help and then delete the app; one names iCloud sync as the stuck state. A 'skip setup / continue offline' path and a visible error would turn some of those 1★ reviews into support tickets. Report 49: signup blocked — a name field that could not be scrolled past (Aug–Sep 2025 cluster, 23 at 1.13).

title: A free-tier limit must announce itself — never silently stop a visible progress signal
statement: Report 26: the free tier lets the garden grow to ~17% and then silently stops; 50 verified reviews (1.30%, mean 2.96) report the flower 'not growing', 17 of them naming the same 17% across April 2022 → December 2025, filed as 'Glitches 🙄', 'Bug', 'Fake Flowers' — several learned only from support that it was intentional. Users conclude the app is broken and say so publicly. A one-line in-app explanation at the moment the ceiling is hit converts a 1–3★ 'it's broken' review into a legible upgrade prompt — the cheapest high-value fix in the corpus. Report 33: the habit limit was announced only after users created habits. Report 46: the free tier cannot fill the product's own 4-row widget ('it leaves the 4th row blank… it bothers me so much'; 'makes many widgets appear broken as they tend to have a multiple of 4 rows'). Report 48: the cap 'announces itself' only after setup — 48 reviews at 1.65★ met the wall after investing effort. Report 50: own statistics locked after hitting the reduced cap (TR).

title: The reward loop needs a content runway — finite gardens, themes or levels exhaust long-term users
statement: Report 26: garden-motivation praise declined monotonically 7.93% → 8.41% → 5.65% → 5.03% → 3.76% across five years while aesthetic praise strengthened, and reviewers report running out of gardens ('when I grew all the gardens, there is nothing to do'; 'YOU NEED MORE GARDEN DESIGNS!!'; 'I'll get bored if more aren't added'). For a product whose entire retention mechanism is the garden this is the most strategically important soft signal; per-habit gardens would also soften the all-or-nothing rule. Report 28: users complete all rooms and the motivation engine stops — 16 (1.95%), including a paying customer leaving ('this one doesn't motivate me anymore'), 'after level 200 you get items less frequently, and the hype is gone', 'incentives stop after level three hundred'; one specifies the remedy — reset the house and make it dirty again, counting resets like a prestige. Report 36: a 60-day monument that is the same journey for every habit — curiosity brings people back on day 3 ('I can't stop because I'm curious about what the next reward is'; GAME+ 74, mean 4.69) and the identical journey and hard stop drive them away around day 60–120 (17 distinct, mean 2.76: 'the story is repeated for all habits … pretty boring', 8 votes; 'it's a shame that it lasts only 60 days … I could have built something infinitely'). Report 49: 'what happens after day 66' and further programmes requested (5); several describe second, third and fourth 66-day cycles. Report 50: long-tenure reviewers (9) all rate 5★; requests deepen rather than stop. Report 54: more plants / a garden or shelf (9) and richer plant behaviour (9); growth stopping at 67 days — see [[C273]]. Report 65 (Rabit): the garden is the retention mechanic (GAM_PLANT 21, mean 4.62; MOT_GOOD 21, 4.86 — 'ver minhas plantinhas crescendo me incentiva a continuar') and under-built — more plant varieties (3), a placeable garden 'more like FarmTown' with tap-a-plant-for-detail, a widget that shows the garden and warns when a plant is near death; 'the cheapest available investment in the thing people already love'.

title: A rewarded-ad unlock path for users who cannot pay (teens, students)
statement: Report 26: teens and students (25, mean 4.16; ages 10–21) cannot pay and say so, and three independently ask to watch ads instead ('I will watch ads all day long if I have to'); report 25: six reviewers volunteer 'show me ads instead' of a paywall. Demand exists in a segment converting at zero — but it conflicts with the reviews that praise having no ads (report 26: 7 at mean 5.00), so it is research, not a decision. Report 31: teens blocked by the cap and price in the 2022–23 TikTok cohort — a student / low-income price is the report's answer. Report 47: rewarded video for cosmetics was accepted ('動画を見れば使える色が増えます', 14-vote 5★, 2022) where rewarded video for logging yesterday produced 1★ — a rewarded unlock is safe on decoration, never on the record. Report 64 (Critique AI): 12 reviewers (2.86%) volunteer ads as the price of access on a teen-heavy app with no free tier; one paying adult objects ('I'd rather pay than see ads'); a free teen tier is the most-upvoted ask. Report 65 (Rabit): a coin economy earned by watching rewarded videos, with purchasable fertiliser — the videos fail and an unclosable ad blocks earning (GAM_COIN 2).

title: A personal origin story in the listing builds trust — and turns any later gate into a betrayal
statement: Report 27: a solo developer's story in the listing produced 10 reviews (7.25%, every one 5★) thanking her by name — 'Thanks Emily'; 'It's clear that someone made this with joy, not for money'; 'built/maintained by an individual female developer — THANK YOU'; 'you are a hero'. The origin story does measurable acquisition work, and it is a constraint: a trust-based relationship is what makes a paywall feel like a betrayal rather than a transaction. Report 25: 'I can't believe one developer made this' and 'after interacting with the developer I decided to pay without any hesitation'. Report 59 (Tappsk): the developer's own vc.ru article brought the first users (MKT_PRESS 13) and a Russian creator is itself praised ('это еще и русский создатель а не зарубежный').

title: Never interrupt the completion moment — no ad, upsell or rating prompt on the check-off tap
statement: Report 28: a forced full-screen interstitial fired on every habit check-off is the single largest fact in an 821-review corpus — 164 complaints (19.98%, mean 2.73 vs 4.35 for every other review; 52.4% of all 1★), 33 naming the per-tap mechanic as a punishment ('it feels like a punishment for doing what you were meant to do'; 'replacing the feel-good with this uncanny worry'), 30 calling the app unusable, 19 five-star reviewers still complaining, and the users most helped by the reward loop (ADHD) the most damaged by breaking it. Users are not asking for zero ads; they propose batching ('let me tick them all off and then show me an ad') or a cap per session. Report 24: checking off one habit takes 3–5 screens of celebration; report 25: upsell sheets on every action; a 2026 rating prompt fired on check-off produced a 1★ purely about the prompt. Report 29: the rating prompt fires on the first habit check-off. Report 42: a mandatory 'congratulations' trophy modal on every check-off blocks the Continue button and freezes the app for heavy users ('It takes me at least 5 minutes to mark two tasks as done'; 'pops up far too often'; messages 'not coherent') — 4 reviews; a settings toggle is the cheapest fix in the report. Report 43: the Oct 2025 redesign put a journal prompt on every skip — 'Bad design to have to do skip every time' (long-time payer, 1★). Report 46: a rating prompt 'every other time I marked a habit as complete'; a Dec 2022 completion animation on every log ('so annoying'). Report 47: the clearest evidence in the ledger — a video ad on each check-in (May–Dec 2024) produced 24 reviews at mean 1.46 and 20 exits in eight months, banners before and after were tolerated, and the 2025 upsell page after each completed task (4, mean 1.25) and the rating prompt shown to payers repeat the same mistake; the report's rule: nothing between 'tap' and 'done' — monetise elsewhere. Report 48: a post-log upgrade prompt (Jul 2024) is 'the only monetization mechanic in the corpus that users say actively reduced their intent to pay' (6 in three months); the 2021 logging redesign added taps to the same moment and was rolled back. Report 52: an ad after every check-in (2025) and a status sheet added to the check-in tap (2021) are both named as the moment the app broke. Report 60 (Mindway): the upsell interrupts the planning task itself — three reviewers (1.39%, mean 1.33) describe pop-ups 'every 5 seconds' while building a routine ([[C093]]). Report 65 (Rabit): an interstitial on habit completion from 23 Dec 2022 — 'Cada que completo un hábito me aparece un anuncio!!!'; 'vengo a desinstalarla después de ver unos 40 anuncios'; 'They don't even let you finish what you were doing' — ADS_BAD 15 (3.01%, mean 2.33), 12 of 46 reviews in the launch window (26.1%); 'An app whose entire behavioural model is complete the habit → see your plant grow → feel rewarded inserted an interstitial exactly at the reward moment'; the close button rendered under the iPhone 13 status bar and forced a restart; F5.

title: Sell entitlements as non-consumables — a consumable currency cannot be restored and has no 'paid member' state to honour
statement: Report 28: one consumable currency ('carrots') sells cosmetics, functional caps, ad removal and cloud sync; 10 of 24 identifiable payers (41.7%) report a purchase that did not deliver or could not be restored — 'I paid 10$ to remove ads but I still get ads'; 'cannot restore purchase on a new device'; 'I paid the 14.99… it's still saying I need to purchase'; and a $10 buyer is charged again when a new paid feature ships ('i'm already a paid member; why do i have to make another purchase?'). Reviewers cannot tell what they are buying ('I now realize just buying anything gives u cloud access') and ask for it unbundled ('just pay like two dollars to just get unlimited tasks'). An architecture problem presenting as a trust problem. Report 49: an under-18 / student free programme granted case by case is invisible to almost everyone.

title: Never monetise by routing the user's device or bandwidth for third parties — and never gate first launch behind any such opt-in
statement: Report 29: a free tracker whose whole reputation was 'actually free' (46.99% of reviews) added a launch-screen prompt in May 2026 asking users to enable 'web indexing' — letting third parties use the phone's IP to download web data — in exchange for an ad-free experience. Every reviewer who described it gave 1★ ('This app now interrupts use unless you agree to run a malware proxy downloader'; 'Didn't get past the opening screen… No thanks'; 'You PAID for this free app'); two of three quit before using the product; a reviewer had already asked 'Am I trading off data privacy for this?'; the listing's privacy label ('analytics and diagnostics') does not obviously cover it. It turned the 1★ band from bugs into privacy in one half-year. If any consent-based monetisation is used, ask after first value, in plain language, reversible, never as a gate.

title: Date arithmetic must survive month boundaries and week-start conventions
statement: Report 29: a month-rollover / weekday-offset bug was the dominant defect — 37 reviews (10.11%, mean 2.95 vs 4.73), 78.4% of them filed on days 28–3 against a 27.6% baseline ('On the last day of every month, the app has no idea what day it is… April 30 defaulted to Feb 28'; 'the 31st listed twice'; 'went backwards into April instead of forwards into July'; 'Monday thru Sunday… but the dates go Sunday thru Saturday'); it was 62.5% of all 3★ and 66.7% of 2★, peaked at 20.2% of 2025H1 and fell ~8× by 2026H1 with a residual weekday-offset tail; users taught each other to reinstall, which destroyed their local-only data. Test every date surface at month end, leap day and both week starts.

title: Never seed the launch rating with templated or bought reviews — the rating decays and the markets they cover become unmeasurable
statement: Report 30: 83 of 166 reviews (50%) matched a five-phrase list across languages ('I highly recommend it' / 'so simple, perfect' / 'the best one'…), all 5★, in two dated campaigns (EN Jul–Sep 2025, ES/NL Nov–Dec 2025), including a Dutch sentence concatenating all five phrases posted on the Russian storefront. When the campaigns stopped, the half-year mean fell 4.65 → 3.17 → 3.00 and the organic 1★ rate rose 12.5% → 44.4%; the US storefront (31 reviews, all 5★, 22 templated) and GB (nothing after the campaign) became commercially blind — the highest-spend markets yielded 8 substantive reviews averaging 3.50 against a 4.79 headline. The public rating is a decaying artefact, not an asset.

title: Every SKU delivers exactly what its label says — one clear shelf, a working monthly option, and 'lifetime' that is lifetime
statement: Report 30: four SKUs (Monthly $5.99, Yearly $44.99, a second Yearly $29.99, Lifetime $59.99) and five of the six reviewers who reached payment had a bad outcome — charged with premium never unlocking (treated as a P0), the monthly plan unpurchasable ('it charges for a year'), 'Te dicen que es de por vida el plan y es solo para un año' (lifetime delivered as annual — 'Cuidado, engañan'), an annual charge with no trial, an accidental subscription with no refund route; all four purchase-flow defects are 2026 events. Collapse the shelf and audit entitlement delivery end to end.

title: No ads in a personal habit tracker — 'no ads' is among the highest-rated topics and ads on the reward loop are the largest 1★ driver
statement: Report 1: 'no ads' is the highest-rated topic in the corpus (181 of 182 mentions positive, mean 4.91). Report 3: 206 reviews praise the absence of ads at mean 4.94 with zero 1–2★. Report 4: no advertising business; 67 praise it (mean 4.45). Report 20: no ads is a top-rated praise theme. Report 2: ads in the free version are a stated reason for 3 purchases. Separated from C006 because the ad decision now has its own counter-evidence and cost data — C082 (ads in the free tier, report 28: an interstitial on every check-off was 19.98% of reviews, 52.4% of 1★) and C240 (never interrupt the completion moment). Report 34: no ads; 'no ads / no nagging' praised by 6 (mean 4.83). Report 36: no ads — '0 ad clutter. 0 monthly charges'; NOADS 6 (mean 4.33). Report 41: no ads anywhere; six name the absence as a reason they chose the app vs one who would prefer ads to paying €1.99/month. Report 42: no ads and none asked for — the complaint is the upsell interstitial. Report 43: no ads ever; praised by 5 (mean 4.80). Report 46: zero ads; no ads praised by 10 (mean 4.90). Report 47: banners in a free tier are tolerated (11 mild complaints over five years, most offering to pay) but a per-action video is not — ad overload 24 at mean 1.46 and 0 ad complaints in 146 reviews after the rollback. Report 48: no ads in eleven years — 33 praise, 0 complaints; the report's first 'do not change'. Report 52: see [[C269]] — the 2025 in-flow ad wave drove 35.0% of six months' reviews at mean 3.70. Report 54: no ads — the 7 reviewers who praise the absence are all 5★. Report 56: 9 of 67 name ad-freeness; ads 'caused instant deletion' of competitors. Report 58: 8 of 91 praise no ads, and 'no ads' plus 'no bad free version' is the pitch against competitors. Report 59 (Tappsk): PR_NO_ADS 127 (0.84%, 4.91★) with no ad complaint coded across 15,176 reviews; 'no ads in the free tier' is on the report's keep list. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): zero ad complaints in 45 reviews; §8.5: do not build ads — 'a habit app whose appeal is calm minimalism has more to lose than to gain'. Report 65 (Rabit): ads introduced into a formerly ad-free app cost it its distinguishing praise; a reviewer names the perceived intent — 'se o objetivo é fazer pagar o premium ou desistir de usar o app'; M5: consider removing ads for free users entirely and monetising on depth.

title: Never make a sibling-app bundle the only way to buy this app's own premium
statement: Report 31: from mid-2021 the Growth Bundle (Tally, Do, Grateful, Moody, Last, Time Block, Reflectly) was the only upgrade path — 36 reviews (0.69%, mean 2.03): 'There is no way to only upgrade this app to premium'; 'the renewal jumps up to 10x the price in a year's time'; buyers of a $19.99 'lifetime' were routed into a 'gift' bundle upsell, and dismissing it dropped them back to Basic. A bundle can be offered alongside, never instead of, a single-app purchase. Report 36: 'I only want to buy this one' / 'Me gustaría que vendieran el premium de solo esta app' — SUITE- 9; one buyer bought Habits alone as 'the only app in the pack truly worth it'; the report: sell Habits standalone, prominently.

title: Never show an upsell to anyone holding an active or historical entitlement
statement: Report 31: 314 reviews (6.05%, mean 1.57) were upsold after paying — 197 of 625 explicit payers (31.5%) — rising 0.3% (E1) → 12.1% (E4): 'It's not encouraging customer loyalty!!'; mood-disorder tracking interrupted by the offer; a banner in Dec 2020 hid the bottom habit even for paid users. The report's first upsell rule: suppress every offer for any past or present entitlement, and test every-launch vs weekly vs never-for-past-payers on conversion, D30 retention and 1★ rate. Report 33: cross-promotion ads for the developer's other apps (Nirow, Poly) shown to lifetime payers — 'False advertisement – Still get ads with lifetime premium'; a premium user shown notices: 'No. deal with it'; 'I wish the upgrade button would disappear when you buy premium' — 14 + 12 reviews.

title: Account deletion completes in one step, in-app and on the web, and is confirmed — never a spinner or a silent chatbot
statement: Report 33: account deletion that spins forever drew 47 reviews (1.19%) at mean 1.23 — zero 5★, 41 1★, the worst-rated theme in a 3.74★ corpus — 23 of them in 2020 and still reported in 2025, 16 from Korea (5.5% of that storefront): users who wanted to switch apps found support silent ('emails keep coming, so I can't uninstall'), the app crashed on delete, 'once you ask the chat bot … it stops answering'; 'Did you choose to block account deletion to keep customers?'; 'I trust it isn't deliberate… but inflating users this way looks bad'. It reads as dark-pattern retention, carries data-subject-deletion exposure, and is among the cheapest fixes relative to its reputational cost. Report 47: the account is optional (backup only) but cannot be deleted in-app, nor the e-mail — 5 reviews (mean 1.60): '退会したいと何度かメッセージ送ってますがもちろん反応はないです'; Guideline 5.1.1(v) has required in-app deletion since June 2022.

title: Marketing e-mail needs consent and a working one-tap unsubscribe — never e-mail dormant or deleted accounts
statement: Report 33: in July 2023 (28 Jun – 31 Aug: 59 reviews, mean 2.88; 9 on 5 July alone, mean 1.67) users who had not opened the app for one to two years, or had deleted their account, received daily 'habit' e-mails with no working unsubscribe — 37 marketing-email reviews (0.94%, mean 1.41, 81.1% 1★), 27 in 2023 (12.7% of that year), six of Germany's seven from the wave: 'They probably do this on purpose to inflate their active user stats'; 'daily spam messages that contain all my data … I'll report them to the ICO for breaching GDPR'; CAN-SPAM cited. An unsubscribe link added quickly after the complaints cut the theme to 0.1% of later reviews, but a privacy professional still found it broken in May 2024 ('this is simply embarassing'). Honour deletion across every marketing system. Report 46: 'An email at exactly 12 every day is really intrusive, and I can't find how to cancel'; 'the sender has a new address for each message' (1★).

title: If cross-platform is what people buy, ship every platform in parity — same release, same entitlement, or a visible 'coming' state
statement: Report 33: one account across iPhone, iPad, Watch, Mac, web, Android and Windows is a top purchase trigger (106 cross-platform praise reviews rated 4–5★; 'since I get Mac OS, iPad, and Apple Watch apps all for one subscription … I'm fine with it'; 'signed up for premium mainly because this has a web interface') and the top engineering complaint of 2020–23 — platform issues 354 (8.99%, mean 2.87), 18.7% of E3 and 19.9% of E4; the Mac app stalled for a year ('left for a year at a time'; support: 'the update version is only released on phone, not the MacOS yet'), Mac/web reached 12.2% of E4 and fell to 2.2% after the macOS 13.0.1 fix; entitlements did not follow the person across web (Paddle) → iPhone, guest → account or a new phone (~25 cases, some taking 6+ weeks). Cross-platform wins sales and loses stars unless every device ships on the same day with one entitlement. Report 49: no restore between iPhone and iPad (3). Report 54: a Google Play buyer must rebuy on the App Store (ES, 1★). Report 55: the Android version is described as more capable and reliable (reminders with sound control, one-tap sync, fewer crashes) — 'I recently switched my Android for an iPhone and unfortunately it doesn't work well' (USER_ANDROID 16, 2.81). Report 59 (Tappsk): the Mac app was left behind — 'Там какое то старое приложение, которое давно не обновляется' (some old app that has not been updated in ages); 'garder à jour la version Mac qui semble délaissé' (keep the Mac version up to date, it seems abandoned) — and is the reason several leave for Things ('пришлось отказаться в пользу things из-за отсутствия поддержки Mac').

title: Complete a habit from the notification — an actionable reminder is part of the one-tap loop
statement: Report 34: two reviewers ask to mark a habit done straight from the reminder notification (10052127570, 10100128513), and 'actionable notifications' recur among US 4★ requests — the missing piece between a reminder and a check-off in an app praised for one-tap logging. Report 53: 'It should be a single tap to complete one once the reminder pops up' (gb, 3★). Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_NOTIF_ACTIONS 28 — actions from the notification or lock screen; the listing's 'reminders that repeat until acted on' is praised (PR_REMINDERS 401).

title: Notification restraint — few, finely controllable notifications keep the users that spammy rivals lose
statement: Report 36: notification restraint is praised by 12 (2.22%, mean 4.67) and framed as the reason people switched — 'fine-tuned control over the notifications you receive — probably the #1 reason I've deleted other habit apps was that they spammed me with a billion distracting notifications' (13967987039); a US talking point (3.97% vs 0.69% non-US). More / snoozable reminders are also requested (7) — make any escalation opt-in so the restraint is not lost. Report 43 (counter-case): the nag loop is the differentiator — user-controlled frequency ('as often as you want') is what makes heavy notification acceptable; one review in 638 finds it excessive. Report 46: a daily e-mail at exactly 12 with a new sender address each time (3, mean 1.67, 2020–23) was made switchable ('You can turn them off if you don't like it'). Report 48: notification overload 12 (2.33) against 224 reminder praise — custom text and per-tracker control keep the ratio stable. Report 50: per-habit reminders praised by 10 (4.90); notifications broken on the new Watch app (1).

title: An all-habits overview with one-tap check-off — never force one-habit-at-a-time navigation
statement: Report 36: a full-screen one-habit canvas with names in a small strip at the top produced 27 distinct navigation complaints (5.00%, mean 3.56, mostly 4–5★), asked continuously from Dec 2021 to Apr 2026 (one review 45 helpful votes): the centre check button swallows horizontal swipes, the strip is 'quite a reach', and it gets worse with more habits — i.e. for the paying user ('I have to swipe through 16 habits. That alone is enough for me to not want to use this app anymore'); 12 ask for 'a consolidated list / calendar view of all of your habits' to 'check or uncheck' on one page. A Dec 2025 partial fix was praised the same week, but complaints continued. Report 43: groups / profiles that can be toggled on and off (e.g. weekday vs weekend sets) requested by 4 (mean 4.25). Report 47: a combined all-habit overview calendar requested by 6 (mean 4.50); a 'today / not yet done' list by 3 (4.67); today's status unclear 5 — the home surface must show every habit's state at once. Report 48: a Today list exists but is premium (tags / filters / Today); a 3-tracker free tier keeps the overview small. Report 59 (Tappsk): the one-screen today / tomorrow / later layout with habits on top is the praised overview (PR_SECTIONS 134, PR_ONE_SCREEN 82, PR_SWIPE 58 reschedule by swipe; 'Die Ansicht „heutige und zukünftige Aufgaben“ ist bei keiner Anderen App so gut und Übersichtlich aufgeteilt').

title: An in-app language selector that respects the user's choice — shipping a localisation must never trap someone in a language
statement: Report 41: after Czech shipped, a Czech user wanted to keep English and 'there's no way to change the language' (13309363635, 5★); a French user's app switched itself to German — 'Why this language change to German??? I can't set it back to French? I'm so disappointed, I loved this app' (13509177027, 1★, Dec 2025). A regression introduced by localising, which converts a feature investment into a rating loss; the report's fix F5 is an explicit in-app language selector. Report 42: Ukrainian users served a Russian interface with no way to switch ('How to switch to Ukrainian/English interface?'). Report 43: 'The app is a mess, full of spelling mistakes' (GB, 1★) — localisation quality. Report 46: two German reviewers could not use the app because they do not read English (2020, Dec 2023) although German is listed. Report 47: notification options rendered as '汽車' and '手冊' in Traditional Chinese, mainland terms shown to Taiwan, a French machine translation that caused an immediate delete — translation quality 5, none Japanese. Report 52: Chinese-reading users on English systems ask for an in-app language setting independent of iOS; the Traditional setting in Taiwan still shows mostly Simplified. Report 56: the UI switched to Chinese unprompted and the user could not find how to change it back.

title: Skip, miss and not-yet-logged are visibly distinct states, and the stats explain which is which
statement: Report 41: a paying user never used the app because 'what does it mean when you forget to record a habit as completed, is that skipped or recorded as a miss. I don't understand how the stats work' (9373324084, GB, 3★); five years later 'when you go into a habit's history and see gaps, you don't understand whether you forgot to tick that day or whether it was a skip' (14303067862, UA, 4★); others ask for an explicit 'not achieved' (未達) state distinct from skip and to 'mark no if you missed it' (11107932681, 11725650343). Onboarding is the lowest-rated non-monetisation theme (8, mean 2.88). Report 43: a skipped vs missed distinction is part of the swipe confusion ('I was constantly marking things as done when I really wanted to mark them as skipped'). Report 46: 'missed' distinct from 'not recorded' requested by 6 (mean 4.67) — and the skip semantics confuse 19. Report 47: a note on a missed day that does not count as done requested by 4 (mean 4.50, 3 KR); show missed days 2 — the missed state needs its own visible, optional marker. Report 48: no vacation / illness handling that leaves a streak or an average intact (13); weekend 'misses' on weekday habits (21). Report 49: tasks marked done / partial / skipped by swipe; no pause for illness or absence (3). Report 50: skipped days should be visually distinct (1); a Skip that breaks daily completion is part of the pause request. Report 59 (Tappsk): 'чтобы можно было задачу пометить как НЕ сделанную' (so a task can be marked as NOT done) — a missed item cannot be marked as missed, only carried forward. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'unlimited back-dating makes streaks less meaningful' — a fan asks to mark missed days explicitly (a cross / red mark) and to lock past days; P4: streak integrity as an option, because some users need back-fill, and §8.5: do not remove back-dating — make it lockable.

title: Never paywall reminders — it moves the comparison from 'which habit tracker' to 'why pay for an alarm'
statement: Report 42: reminders sit behind the paywall and are the feature most often named as the thing behind the wall (5 reviews, mean 2.60 — 'I just wanted to use the habit reminder feature and that would cost me 40 a year? Come on. That's insane!'), while working reminders are praised at mean 5.00 (6); three reviewers independently conclude the phone's own tools substitute — 'better to use the native Lista app on iPhone… doesn't freeze and is free'; 'the paid version adds a reminder — you can set that in the calendar too'; 'Your alarm or reminder on your phone can do everything this app does. Wasted $20!' The report calls un-paywalling reminders 'the most defensible single paywall change'. Report 43 (counter-case): reminders, including the nag, are free and the app's reason to exist; only the habit count was ever gated. Report 46 (contrast): reminders are free; the paid gates are habit count, dark mode, offline use and sync.

title: A 'nag until done' repeating reminder — the one reminder shape reviewers say no other app offers
statement: Report 43: 'nag me until I'm done' repeating reminders are praised by name in 22 reviews (3.45%, mean 4.86) and reminders generally in 54 (8.46%, 4.76) — 'Best feature by far is the nag me until Im done option, which is something no other app has offered thus far'; 'HabitHub relies on good old-fashioned nagging. It's simple and effective'; 'The first time in my life I gave money to something to NAG me 😐'; 'you can set it to nag you as often as you want and don't have to stop what you are doing to turn off an alarm'. Praised in every era 2016–2025 and found excessive by one review in 638. The report calls it the product's moat and warns it is the mechanism most exposed to notification regressions on iOS updates; do not soften it into a single daily reminder. Report 52: 'repeat until done' and a silent-mode 'strong reminder' alarm among reminder requests (588). Report 59 (Tappsk): the listing advertises reminders that repeat until acted on; PR_REMINDERS 401 (2.64%, 4.90★) is the fourth-largest praise theme and distinctive in SA, CA, AU and GB.

title: An in-app help screen — first-run tour, searchable FAQ, per-setting explanations — for any product whose setup is richer than its daily use
statement: Report 43: no guide / tutorial / FAQ / help (9, mean 2.78) plus a learning curve (14, 3.36) — 20 reviews (3.13%) requested continuously from Feb 2017 ('There must be some tips or suggestions in start') to Aug 2026 ('I don't understand nothing') and never addressed: 'There is no help option in settings which makes at least one action I want to take impossible… I can't find instructions for this in the app, on YouTube, or through a Google search'; 'I have had to contact support twice on things that could have explained up front'; 'it took me an hour or so to figure out how to make it work… I'd pay for this if it had some adjustments in usability'. Roughly a tenth of the 29 scheduling-gap reviews ask for capabilities the app already has (custom days, timers, untimed tasks) and land as 1★ / 2★. The same product draws 123 'simple' reviews — daily use is simple, setup is not — so a help screen targets a different surface from the praised simplicity.

title: Never argue price in a public review reply, and never ask a reviewer to change their rating
statement: Report 46: 6 reviews (0.28%, mean 1.33, all 2021 or later, five in 2024–26) say a public developer reply was rude or defensive — 'snarky remarks about working for free and making an overpriced app isn't the way to do it'; 'developer takes any criticism with such a nasty attitude'; 'After reading developer's response I am degrading rating to 1 star from 2… 5/5 rating for app but 0/5 for your behaviour' (13298363427) — and 2 say the developer pressed them to change their review ('the developer keeps contacting me to pressure me into changing my review', 11709301622). Every one of these reviews went from 'too expensive' to 'and the developer is hostile', a reputational cost no pricing change recovers, while 53 reviews (mean 4.94) praise the same developer's private support. The report's zero-cost fix: thank, state the free tier and lifetime option factually, never argue value, never ask for a rating change.

title: A colour palette users can extend — more defaults, a hex picker, softer sets — because colour is the reward surface
statement: Report 46: 'more / custom / softer colours' is the top feature request in every era after 2020 — 59 reviews (2.71%, mean 4.36; 35 at 5★, 15 at 4★): a hex-code picker ('I would love very much to have the option to enter a hex code… I will pay for this feature!!', 9952382181, tracking 21 habits; 11699632553), pastel and neutral palettes, 'more (than 7) default colors', colours for 21 habits, and 'I would totally splurge a buck 99 for a rain themed color pallete' (12101755389); four say long streaks turn colours muddy ('Yellow disappears completely and turns red. Red turns brown. Green turns olive', 13866974245). A palette pack is the only in-app purchase the corpus asks for unprompted; the request sits on the product's differentiator (the colour-saturation grid, 228 reviews at mean 4.86). Report 47: more colours requested 3 (2019–20), later unlocked by watching a video.

title: Never gate a recovery action — back-dating a missed day, undoing a wrong entry and restoring history stay free forever
statement: Report 47: back-dating is a trust feature (it makes the streak honest) and charging for it reads as charging to undo the app's own penalty — the backfill-demand union is 52 reviews (8.83%: check off a past day 22, a start date before creation 21, the 2024 gate 9), named in the very first review in the corpus (Feb 2019); it shipped 29 March 2020 (the most-voted review, 23 votes: '日付を遡ってチェックインできるようになってました！！！') and the request fell from 7.1% of 2019–21 reviews to 0.7%; then in April–June 2024 it was put behind a video ad and produced 9 reviews at mean 1.67 ('¥200 a month to log past days is too much') alongside the 2024 exits. The rule the report draws: every purchase trigger reviewers name is additive (AI coach, photos, stats, sync) and none asks to pay to restore something that used to be free — recovery actions are the one surface where a gate is read as extortion. Related: [[C010]] (backfill is a free feature), [[C176]], [[C204]]. Report 52: 32 reviews say restoring their own data after a crash-reinstall required buying membership — 'after reinstalling I bought lifetime membership to restore my data, and restoring crashed the app'; F3: never gate restoring a user's own backup. Report 57: backup and restore gated behind Premium while 12 users lost data — §8.2: 'Gating recovery behind a purchase converts a bug into a grievance'; at minimum an automatic local export or a one-time free restore after detected loss. Report 65 (Rabit): premium took previous-day marking in Nov 2020, and when the app falsely marked completed days as missed a reviewer concluded it was deliberate — 'the app marks completed days as missed so you will buy the subscription that lets you edit past days… Tática desleal' — the perception is a monetization cost even where the cause is a bug.

title: An AI encouragement reply on each check-in as the premium hook — the first paid feature reviewers praise unprompted; its state must be visible
statement: Report 47: an AI coach that comments on each check-in (from September 2025) is praised by 13 (2.21%, mean 4.69) — 'そんなわけないだろ、AIだろ、って感じると思うけど意外に嬉しい' ('you'd think come on, it's just AI — but it's surprisingly nice'); 'AIに褒められてる感じがしなくて、承認欲求も満たされて' ('it satisfies the need for approval') — an AI-coach union of 18 (12.3% of 2025–26 reviews) with friction 9: 5 say comments stopped without explanation after about a week ('1週間くらいでAIのコメントが来なくなっちゃった'), 3 did not want it, 1 hit a surprise paywall, and a payer's on/off toggle would not turn back on. The report's E3 is the coach as the premium hook with a clearly labelled free taste; its fix #4 is a visible state ('trial ended', 'off', 'error') so a silent stop is never mistaken for a bug. Counter-evidence to [[C056]]: here the AI feature monetises by adding value, which the 2024 gating did not. Report 49: AI planning is welcomed (6, 4.50) while AI decoration is rejected (53) — see [[C267]].

title: Log-entry friction is sacred — never add a tap to the logging path; a logging redesign is the highest-risk change in the product
statement: Report 48: a mid-2021 redesign of history logging that multiplied the taps to back-fill days drew ten reviews in three months (May–Aug 2021 window n = 78, mean 3.86★, 28.2% 1–2★ — 'Latest update forces you to double click for every single activity'; 'turning a 10 second daily update to about 60'), disproportionately from long-term users (7) and payers (6); the developer restored the one-click behaviour and the reinstatement was welcomed by name, after which too-many-taps fell to 0.24% — 'log-entry friction is uniquely expensive for this product' because simplicity of logging (817 reviews, 18.56%, mean 4.84 — 'open the app, click a check mark, exit') is its most load-bearing quality. Report 47 (DotHabit): a long-press → record screen → done flow counted as too many taps by 14 (mean 2.86) with one-tap logging requested since 2019. Related: [[C240]] (nothing between tap and done), [[C159]], [[C229]] (a deliberate gesture must complete the log, not open a form). Report 52: 'a check-in used to be one tap… now it's at least two' (Jun 2021 status sheet, 29 reviews in a month); every added step on the check-in was reviewed negatively within days; R2: protect one-tap check-in and one-tap undo. Report 53: swipe-to-complete and the completion sound are liked; editing habits 'are a nightmare - you have to tap in multiple times'; compared unfavourably with Productive's one-swipe check (DES_UX_NEG 38). Report 59 (Tappsk): entry speed is a named reason for choosing the app — 'позволяет тебе записать задачу быстрее чем ты ее забудешь' (write the task down faster than you forget it); 'Задачи добавляются за пол секунды' (added in half a second); voice entry by holding the add button praised by 52. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'just check and carry on. As it should be' — one-tap check-off is the praised loop; when the June build broke tapping, the app was unusable.

title: Tracker types beyond yes/no — numeric target, rolling average and project milestones — as the reason people switch from binary habit apps
statement: Report 48 (Strides): four tracker types — Habit (yes/no), Target (a number by a date), Average (rolling mean), Project (milestones, %) — are the defining feature and the differentiator: 485 reviews (11.02%, mean 4.82★) — 'I don't want to reduce everything to the binary yes/no' (2013) repeated in structure in 2024; a reviewer lists seven rivals before 'Strides is the only app that does both'; highest in GB (13.79%), AU (14.52%), IN (16.90%); bad-habit / 'less is better' inversion praised by 105; goal pacing (the projected-date and 'am I on pace' maths only Target and Project provide) praised by 56 at 4.97★ — 'This theme, not streaks or design, is why people switch to Strides'. The cost is a decade of setup confusion (118 reviews at 2–3% in every era, concentrated on choosing between the four types) and yes/no semantics that turn ambiguous for bad habits (12). Related: [[C108]] (goals / targets), [[C048]] (flexible units / partial progress), [[C019]] (quit-habit mode), [[C136]] (choose the mode at creation), [[C135]].

title: A generated programme escalates on observed completion, never on a fixed calendar — and never past what a health limit the user declared allows
statement: Report 49 (Life Reset): a 66-day programme whose targets rise on a fixed weekly schedule reaches 90-minute lifts plus 4-mile runs six days a week and 2 gallons of water a day for people who were sedentary at week 1 (ramp unrealistic / unsafe 20, mean 2.85; 3–4 litres prescribed without assessment); advanced users get beginner plans (13); reviewers who complete everything are still told they have not improved and a German reviewer who wanted habit stability found the escalation demotivating (guilt-inducing tone 13, Germany +3.34pp); asthma, post-surgical injury, nerve damage and mobility limits cannot be entered (10 — 'ableist and short-sighted'), running is the only cardio (20). The report calls it partly a safety matter and recommends adapting the ramp to observed completion, which addresses the ramp, level-mismatch and guilt complaints together, while keeping the 66-day structure itself (13 at 4.77★). Related: [[C160]] (a declared limitation must change the suggestions), [[C103]] (vulnerable users), [[C203]], [[C095]].

title: No AI-generated art, copy or content in a paid product — reviewers accept an AI coach and reject AI decoration
statement: Report 49 (Life Reset): AI-generated task icons, achievement art, motivational copy and book summaries are criticised by 53 reviews (4.30%, mean 1.85) — the only product criticism rising in every era (0% → 4.4% → 4.0% → 5.5%), spreading from images to the writing ('replete with the odd linguistic signatures characteristic of an LLM'), typos and code, and double the global rate in Australia (10.34%). The objection is craft tied to price: 'I cannot see myself paying full price for something that is completely built by AI… Only then can I say this is something I'd actually tell my friends about'; 'for an app promoting ideas of doing the work and not being lazy, using AI instead of just paying an artist… seems like a very cheap move'; 'Just pay humans to do work'. AI planning is welcomed (6, mean 4.50) — 'The distinction is decoration versus function.' The report: commission at least the hero assets; fixing typos removes the most visible AI tell. Report 47 (DotHabit) is the complementary case: an AI coach replying to check-ins is praised unprompted ([[C263]]). Related: [[C056]], [[C185]]. Report 52: AI-generated note titles (Feb–Apr 2026) that could not be switched off — every review mentioning them negative. Report 64 (Critique AI): TRUST_AISLOP 4 (0.95%, mean 1.50) accuse the app itself of being AI-generated, one from inside after paying; the community page read as 'probably fake'.

title: Journal / notes prompts are optional — a toggle to stop the post-completion journal prompt, and a text editor that never corrupts input
statement: Report 50 (HelloHabit): the built-in journal (notes on habits reviewable in a diary view) is a primary reason people choose and keep the app — 19 reviews (9.27%, mean 4.74; 'To me this is gold, and the best implementation I've seen of this feature'; 'it let me delete a couple other apps') — yet it is also the worst-quality surface: the notes editor corrupts input (3 reviews, mean 3.33, Jan 2025 → Apr 2026, unresolved 16 months — keyboard covers the cursor, a letter stuck by the cursor, 'my second sentence somehow gets pieced into my first'; two name it as the withheld fifth star), and a journal prompt fires after every task with no way to switch it off (2, both 5★ — 'I don't use the journaling feature and wish there were a way to turn off the prompt') — the report's 'cheapest fix' and 'cheapest rating repair'. Related: [[C172]] (per-day notes), [[C006]] (every addition opt-in), [[C228]] (IME-safe text fields). Report 52: autosave so an interrupted note isn't lost, and no forced or AI titles.

title: If the free tier carries ads, never use hijacking ad mechanics — no auto-jump into other apps, no shake or tilt triggers, a close control that closes, and no ad on the check-in
statement: Report 52 (ShineDay / 小日常): the June 2025 in-flow ad rollout is the largest negative event in nine years — AD_NEG 546 of 1,562 reviews (35.0%) in Jun–Nov 2025 against 0.6% in Jan–May, July 2025 the lowest month in the corpus (3.35), 885 total (4.29%, mean 2.46). Reviewers did not object to ads as such; they named the mechanics: ads that open another app automatically (Taobao, Pinduoduo, Meituan, Quark) 107, a close / skip button hidden, tiny or ineffective 88, shaking or tilting the phone triggers the ad 33, and ads after the check-in itself — 'the skip and close buttons get more hidden… move the phone slightly… it jumps into the ad page'; a close button that opens 'a full-screen Taobao ad that also can't be closed'. The report's reading: 'not a pricing decision that users rejected… an interaction-design decision'; an ad dismissal also bypassed the passcode lock. The 2019–21 splash and undismissable follow-us pop-ups produced a smaller wave (206). Related: [[C246]] (no ads at all), [[C127]] (never to payers), [[C240]] (never on the completion moment), [[C082]] (ads in the free tier).

title: Free habit capacity that grows with continued check-ins — an earned cap reads as generosity, not as a wall
statement: Report 52 (ShineDay / 小日常): from 2025 the free habit quota grows as the user keeps checking in — 'keep checking in and it gives you more habit slots' (5★); 'I thought it was capped at 8, then found it grows with use' (4★); the design called 'very kind' (5★). The free-quota complaint PAY_CAP5 fell from 8.2% of reviews (2018) and 7.1% (2020) to 0.6% in 2026 — the only monetisation theme with a sustained, monotonic decline — though it was already falling 5.3% → 3.3% in 2021–24, so the mechanic is consistent with the decline, not proven to cause it. Report's M2: keep it and explain it on the paywall, because only reviewers who notice it praise it. Related: [[C007]] (fixed generous cap), [[C222]] (opt-in pressure valve on a hard cap), [[C219]] (concurrent, never lifetime).

title: One membership at one price across every platform the app ships on — never sell the same entitlement twice or price it differently by store
statement: Report 52 (ShineDay / 小日常): the membership is sold separately on Android and iOS, at different prices and with different logins (QQ on Android, WeChat on iOS) — 49 reviews combine an Android mention with a tier or restore failure (mean 2.80); 'only after buying did I find Android membership must be bought separately'; 'iOS lifetime 88, Android 48? Where's the justice' (Feb 2026); the iOS free quota was also tighter than Android's ('on Android I could add a dozen, why treat us differently?'). PAY_TIERS carries the highest payer lift in the corpus (×5.11). Report's M5: price parity or a single cross-platform membership (platform-fee constraints noted). Related: [[C251]] (platform parity), [[C033]] (restore), [[C035]] (account). Report 54: a buyer on Google Play had to pay again on the App Store (ES, 2023). Report 59 (Tappsk): the Mac app shipped 2020-06 and was sold separately from iPhone Premium — MON_PER_DEVICE 59 ('is it paid for those who already have premium?'), its peak 0.8% of that era; later reviewers describe Mac sync as part of Premium. Report 65 (Rabit): an Android build exists but does not bridge — 'a opção de restaurar só acontece de celular androide para androide'; an Android→iPhone payer could not restore and got no reply; another could not find the sign-in button on iPhone.

title: Built-in timers survive backgrounding, a call and screen lock, and always alert at the end — store the start time, compute elapsed
statement: Report 53 (HabitMinder): CORE_TIMER 52 (2.98%, meaningful, mean 3.54) — praised as unique, yet 13 of 52 describe progress lost when the app is backgrounded, paused or the screen locks and 9 more say the timer ends without an alert: 'after 90 mins you had a call and after the conference call you come back and found that the counter is no longer running and now you've only read 0 minutes' (my, 2★, 2019); a years-long user left because the screen now powers off during a 30-minute meditation (ca, 1★, Nov 2023); a meditation timer that 'runs for 11mn and then logs in 22mn46s'. Report's R4: store the start time and compute elapsed, and always alert at the end via a local notification and Watch haptic. Related: [[C066]] (focus timer), [[C120]] (routine timer), [[C072]] (timed habits written to Health). Report 65 (Rabit): a free per-habit timer ('tem até timer e é de graça!!!!!') that stops counting when backgrounded or the screen locks — 'eu estudei por volta de 1 hora e marcou apenas alguns segundos' — reported Jun 2020 and still Jan 2024; manual time entry proposed and never shipped (F8).

title: The reward mechanic must never silently stall — a plant, pet or garden that stops growing reads as the app taking the reward away
statement: Report 54 (Avocation): a plant watered by completing habits is the emotional engine — 35 reviewers (9.49%, mean 4.43) motivated by it ('Growing my plant has 100% been the thing that has kept me on track') — and when it stalls the product stops working: a signature state 'my plant says infinity days until next growth … It makes me want to stop using the app, since the little reward of growing the plant has been taken away' (US, 3★, payer) and 'Says infinite days until new growth. Does this mean my tree is dead?' (ZA), seven weeks apart, plus growth stopping at exactly 67 days (ES) and in 2026 for a Pro buyer (DE, 1★) — 5 reviewers (1.36%, mean 2.40), all 3★ or below, 3 payers; 'the highest-leverage bug in the report' (F2). Related: [[C237]] (content runway), [[C117]] (companion character), [[C024]] (gamification).

title: A close or dismiss control must never start a purchase — no fake X, no dismissal that lands on the payment sheet
statement: Report 55 (Habit-Bull): a full-screen premium pop-up shown on every launch from 5 July 2020 had a close control that started a purchase — 'I clicked on the x at the top, but instead of giving me the data screen, it acted like I'd tried to make a purchase' (us, 4★); 'The pop up has a fake X in the top corner to close the message, which if you press, causes your account to agree to the premium subscription' (gb, 1★); 'after mistakenly upgrading' (2024). PAY_FORCED 20 (0.99%, mean 1.25, 18 at 1★, all 10 Jul 2020 → 3 Jan 2021) plus PAY_NAG 44 (2.02); in July 2020 35 of 68 reviews (51.5%) carried one or both, the month's mean was 2.09 with 39 one-stars and 11 reviews on 12 July alone; the German-speaking storefronts took it hardest (PAY_NAG 10.7%). The report's F2: make close controls unambiguous so no dismissal can start a purchase — 'the cheapest change with the clearest rating effect in the data'. Related: [[C093]] (no upsell nagging), [[C145]] (every modal dismissible), [[C180]] (no exit discounts or countdowns), [[C269]] (hijacking ad mechanics). Report 57: 'I tapped to see what Premium was, pressed OK to close the sheet, and it bought it' — 6 accidental purchases (2019–2023), all refund requests. Report 67 (Habio): NEG_DARKUX 163 (7.95%, mean 1.01), used by reviewers who work in UX — 'As a UX designer I should have seen the dark patterns from the start'; '환불을 어렵게 만드는 전형적인 다크 패턴'.

title: Never gate the core create action behind an ad — an interstitial at setup is the churn engine, and an ad that fails to load must never block creation
statement: Report 57 (DayStamp): a free tier that requires watching a full-screen interstitial to create a habit (from Jan 2021; 5 seconds in 2021, 29–30 seconds from Sep 2023) is the single most destructive mechanic — ads 47 of 779 (6.03%, mean 2.234, half of them 1★), 26 naming the creation gate (2.154), and 20 of the 25 reviewers who state they deleted the app (80%) name ads, against zero stated deletions for crashes or data loss: 'A full screen ad after just creating one habit? Wow, immediately uninstalled'; 'The developer is losing a lot of app sales because the full screen ads are so horrible that you will stop using the app before finding out if you like the functionality'; an ADHD user 'as soon as I made a single activity scheduled it gave me an add. Literally distracted me before I could get familiarized with the app'. From 2024 the gate started failing — 8 reviewers (7 since 2024, latest 24 Aug 2026) could not create a habit at all because no ad loaded ('Can't add a task - no ads to show'; 'seven ads to add three goals… I got angry trying to build good habits and deleted it') — 'a monetization mechanic that can hard-block the product's core action is a reliability bug, not a pricing decision'. Six reviewers who tolerate ads all gave 5★ and all describe them as short and confined to creation ('survivable at 5 seconds and not at 30'); ads run 9.20% of non-Korean reviews vs 2.48% Korean and 15.15% of US reviews, where 8 of 10 uninstalls blame ads. Options the report supports: back to ~5 seconds, move to a session boundary, or gate after the nth habit rather than the 3rd–4th. Related: [[C269]] (hijacking ad mechanics), [[C246]] (no ads), [[C240]] (never on the completion moment), [[C147]] (use before pay).

title: An optional event time (and duration) on a task or habit, distinct from its reminder, with the day sorted by it and shown on the widget
statement: Report 59 (Tappsk, 15,176 reviews): the most persistent functional request across eight years — U_SCHEDULE_REQ 471 (3.10%, Very strong): REQ_TIME 186, REQ_SORT 132, REQ_CALENDAR_VIEW 118, REQ_ADVANCE_REMINDER 68; a task has a reminder time but no event time, so the day's list does not order itself by timeline ('чтобы задача на 09:00 стояла выше задачи на 11:00' — so the 09:00 task sits above the 11:00 task) and users write the time into the title ('тк нет в приложении времени - я просто в названиях пишу время'); REQ_TIME is at its era maximum in E6 (1.8%) and is the third-largest 4★ theme (69 of 1,671) — the report's hypothesis is that it converts the most frequent 4★ request into 5★; the guard is bloat — PR_KEEP_SIMPLE 49 ask the developer not to change the app. Related: [[C050]] (to-dos alongside habits), [[C006]] (stay minimal), [[C053]] (time-of-day segments), [[C198]] (routine blocks).

title: Price the paid tier against what the phone already gives away — a paywall that sells task slots, reminders or a checklist is compared to Apple Reminders, Notes and paper, and loses
statement: Report 60 (Mindway, 216 reviews): price objections are relative, not absolute — 13 reviewers (6.02%, mean 1.69, no 4★ or 5★ among them) reject the price by comparing it to a substitute they already own, and 6 (2.78%) name it: Apple Reminders, Notes, Calendar, a paper planner — '8€/WOCHE für einen Tagesplaner, den man sich auch selbst im Kalender bauen kann. Frech.' (€8 a week for a day planner you could build in your calendar. Cheeky.); 'einfach zu teuer dafür dass ich das auch gratis in meinen Notizen machen kann'; 'paper planner is cheaper than this LOL'; 'Just use your remind app it's the same thing'. The report's reading: 'the competitive set Mindway is being priced against is not other habit apps — it is the free tools already on the phone', and a count-based paywall ('you have used your 2 free tasks') invites exactly that comparison because task slots are what those tools give away, whereas guided routines, progress history and a self-care library are not comparable to Reminders — 'the corpus shows Mindway losing a fight it chose' (D2: sell the outcome, not the task slots). Related: [[C214]] (a bare checklist cannot carry a premium price), [[C133]] (gate on capability, not quantity), [[C004]] (price against subscription competitors).

title: Do not name the app after an established competitor — a name collision makes the product 'the fake one' before it is tried, and the cost cannot be measured from reviews
statement: Report 62 (Streaks – Daily Habit Tracker by yusuf kildan, 45 reviews): 'If you are planning to get such app based on online review them do not download this app. This is fake and similar name app to the original one. The og has orange colour logo' (IN, 1★) — the collision is real and corroborated in this repository: folder 23 is Streaks by Crunchy Bagel Pty Ltd (app ID 963034692, 7,270 reviews vs this app's 45), so a user searching 'Streaks' meets both and the smaller app is 'losing on brand identity before the product is even tried'; the icon-colour claim could not be verified; how much the collision costs in installs is a research question the corpus cannot answer. Related: [[C184]] (a neutral name is already tested), [[C134]] (lead the listing with what users love), [[C114]] (ads must match the app).

title: An AI analysis must consume its input — reject empty, silent or black input instead of returning a confident score
statement: Report 64 (Critique AI, 419 reviews): four independent reviewers in four storefronts over ten months ran the same adversarial test and got a confident result — a black photo returned 'things that were good and stuff to work on' (paid $25), a voice coach toggled off 'without saying a word' gave the same generic feedback (paid $50: 'It doesn't actually listen'), silence into a speaking exercise scored 79 ($12.99/mo), and 'No matter what photo you upload, it gives the same results' — 'a claim that at least one analysis path does not consume its input', the highest-severity product finding in the report; three of the four had paid and publicly concluded the product was fake; AI_QUALITY 8 (1.91%, mean 2.00), 7 of 69 users who got in (10.1%), 3 of 13 payers, 7 of 8 from Feb 2026 as the user base grew enough to audit the headline feature; F2: reject empty/null input in every AI path. Related: [[C056]], [[C148]] (the paid product must deliver what the ads demonstrate), [[C267]].

title: An app-blocking focus mode must always unlock when its condition is met, never lock apps permanently, never override OS Screen Time, and never depend on a notification the OS can suppress
statement: Report 64 (Critique AI): focus mode — block selected apps, earn them back for ~15 min by doing push-ups or meditation — is 'the most distinctive thing in the corpus and it is also the most broken': 10 mentions (2.39%, mean 3.40), 6 of them failures (1.43%, mean 3.50) — the unlock exercise 'takes me no where', apps stay locked after 10 push-ups so the user turns the mode off 'which gets rid of the point', apps blocked permanently overriding Screen Time permissions (paid $25), no in-between state, and a 5★ defender supplies the root cause: 'you can't unlock apps in focus mode in silent mode because you cant receive the notification'; four of the six are 4★/5★ advocates; one reviewer installed specifically for it and never reached it; Clearspace named as the free substitute; F3. Related: [[C066]] (focus timer), [[C272]] (timers survive backgrounding).

title: Brief every creator and acquisition channel to state the price — an audience told 'it's free' converts marketing spend into permanent 1★
statement: Report 64 (Critique AI): 42 reviews (10.02%, mean 2.38) name a creator, YouTube, TikTok or a friend as the reason they installed (13 name the founder-creator); 30 (7.16%, mean 1.23 — the lowest-rated theme after 'scam', 25 of 30 at 1★) believed the app was free: 'Ich wurde von nem YouTuber angelockt das es kostenlos sei aber es ist so ein scam' (de); 'advertised on a YouTubers channel and he never mentioned anything about a paid subscription' (us); 'Say that in the videos. Just disrespectful.' (co) — 'the highest-leverage finding in the report that costs nothing to fix': the product is not mispriced, it is mis-expected, and every such reviewer 'was acquired at full marketing cost and converted into a permanent 1★'; the only major theme with no downward movement across 17 months (6.5% / 8.8% / 5.6% / 7.8%); M2, and with price-before-quiz (M1) it addresses 53 reviews (12.65%) at mean 1.28. Related: [[C058]] (discovery channels), [[C218]] (listing copy stays true), [[C181]] (paid-only says so up front).

title: A generated plan belongs to the user — it persists, every assigned task can be deleted, declined and reordered, and it is built around the user's fixed commitments
statement: Report 64 (Critique AI): plan rigidity is the top non-price complaint among users who got in — 9 (2.15% global, 13.0% of the 69 inside, mean 2.00) — in five mechanics each named by at least two reviewers: the plan regenerates weekly and own tasks must be re-entered every week; assigned tasks cannot be deleted or declined; tasks cannot be moved; the plan ignores real constraints ('It just says leg day on Wednesday… What if you don't train on Wednesday?'; a gym → home setting that will not change; too advanced for a 12-year-old); content reads as generic filler ('more like XP grabs'; 'all it does is organize workouts I had already organized myself'); three of the eight feature requests are the same ask — build the schedule around school, sport and work; R1, R2; complaint order after price among users: plan rigidity → AI quality → focus failures, 'the list that governs retention rather than acquisition'. Related: [[C203]] (user authors their routine first), [[C266]] (generated programme escalates on completion), [[C073]] (reorder and edit free).

title: Never sell by telling the user they are deficient — an onboarding score that invents a shortfall reads as manipulation
statement: Report 64 (Critique AI): TRUST_MANIP 6 (1.43%, mean 1.17): 'tells you that you are 27% less confident than the average even if you are 100% confident in your answers. I dislike companies that lie especially to manipulate others insecurities' (us); independently, in Hebrew: 'I love myself and have confidence, and the app decided I don't have much confidence and I need to pay monthly to improve it' (il) — on an audience that is substantially 12–15 years old; R6: review the onboarding score's framing. Related: [[C095]] (neutral tone), [[C103]] (minors are a sensitive surface), [[C111]] (no long quiz before the price).

title: Verify the rendered price string in every storefront currency — a decimal or tier error on the paywall suppresses conversion invisibly, because nobody who closes a paywall writes a review
statement: Report 65 (Rabit, 498 reviews): four independent Brazilian reviewers, Jun–Nov 2022, report the monthly price as R$299–R$300 and one as R$600, against R$29.90 reported elsewhere — 'Excelente só corrijam o bug do preço mês que está R$ 299,00 e não 29,90' (5★); 'desinstalei por medo de sem querer assinar o plus e ter que viver de aluguel pois custa 600 reais' (5★, uninstalled); 'Cobrar 300 reais por mês pra ter acesso a coisas fúteis' (3★); two of the four rated 5★ while reporting it as a bug; PAY_PRICE_BUG 4 (0.80%, mean 4.25) — 'high-severity, low-volume': in the storefront holding 77.2% of the app's 5,366 ratings a 10× display error 'would suppress conversion invisibly'; F4: check the App Store Connect BRL tier and the paywall's own string formatting — research #1, 'Highest-value single check in this list'. Related: [[C113]] (one stable, disclosed price), [[C092]] (regional pricing).

title: Never charge a one-off add-on on a single tap against the authorisation just given for a trial — the add-on shows its price on the button, asks its own confirmation, defaults to 'no thanks' and ignores repeat taps
statement: Report 67 (Habio, 2,051 reviews): a $29.99 'workbook' / 'Get my PDF' button shown straight after the paid-trial payment and charged against the card just authorised with no second confirmation — MON_WORKBOOK 189 (9.22%, mean 1.01, 2023-10-15 → 2025-05-04, 41 in 2024-04 alone): 'The consent to charge text is in such a low contrast colour with the background, and such a tiny type size that it hurts my eyes to even read it!'; 'la vérification est demandé donc ils ne la redemande pas ensuite'; 'cliqué en un espacio para informarme más acerca de un pdf y directamente me cobraron 29€!' (es — 39.62% of the Spanish storefront); MON_DOUBLECHARGE 157 (7.65%) often two workbooks ('adhd_workbook' + 'habits_workbook') from a button that seemed not to respond; support answered 'we do not offer refunds for in-app purchases', which in EU storefronts collides with the 14-day withdrawal right; ADHD reviewers: 'They use lack of focus among the targeted ADHD group and trick You into in app purchase without confirming payment!'; §8.2: price on the button, separate confirmation not the trial's stored authorisation, default 'No thanks', idempotent repeat taps, refund an unopened PDF on request. Related: [[C211]] (no second separately-cancelled add-on subscription), [[C274]] (a dismiss control never starts a purchase), [[C213]].

title: Never advertise or sell in a language the app does not ship — a localised ad, quiz or checkout for an English-only app is a refund request waiting to happen
statement: Report 67 (Habio): MKT_LANG_BAIT 86 (4.19%, mean 1.07), every one dated 2024-03-28 or later — the ad and web quiz ran in French, Spanish, German, Arabic or Japanese and the paid app turned out English-only (lookup API declares EN; listing titles localised as 'Habio: Tagesplaner. Checkliste', 'Habio: Habitude et Objectif'): 'L'ensemble des publicités ansi que les questionnaires avant l'achat sont en français, et l'application n'est dispo qu'en anglais'; France 30 of 91 reviews (32.97%), Germany 12 of 85, Chile 10 of 25; 34.9% of these reviewers ask for or are refused a refund ('nunca me contestaron para decirme si podía cambiar a español o no'); the language request itself predates the ads (6 in the free era) — 'The ads made it worse; they did not create it'; §8.5: localise, or state 'English only' in every non-English ad, quiz and checkout. Related: [[C027]] (localise early), [[C148]] (deliver what the ads show), [[C218]].
